Adversarial review returned PASS: reviewer built an independent correctness oracle over 258,864 generated patterns with no resolver code in the loop and measured 137 unsound answers on master vs 0 on the branch, audited all 134 accept->refuse transitions (all 134 already refused by master when written with a variable, byte-identical messages), and reproduced 8/8 author mutations plus 7 of its own under a go vet screen with zero blank-name kills. GH #788 and #790 both CLOSED by the merge.

title: codegen/age: the dialect gap table is short — four constructs are suspected and unwitnessed
description:
The Apache AGE backend refuses a query on its TEXT when it spells a construct
the pinned image cannot accept (`internal/codegen/age/dialect.go`). Every entry
in that table carries a probe and the answer a live session gave, and a sweep
(`TestEveryDialectGapCarriesItsWitness`) refuses an entry with no witness. That
is the right shape, and it leaves the table SHORT: three openCypher constructors
and one namespaced call are every bit as suspect as the five that are refused,
and none of them has ever been run.

## Unverified, and therefore not refused

Against `apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8bb86a6b2ea44e9ad06c73856e12b209de295124603a599dd7feb70eb`
(PostgreSQL 18.1, AGE 1.7.0 — the digest is a constant in
`test/data/codegen/live_age_test.go`):

1. `RETURN time()` — expected `function time does not exist`, never run.
2. `RETURN localtime()` — same, never run. Load-bearing: it is what
   `test/data/codegen/invalid/unrepresentable_temporal_localtime_column` and
   `TestTemporalProjectionNamesThisBackend` rest on. If localtime() turns out to
   be undefined, the dialect gate answers those two ahead of
   `codegen.ErrUnrepresentableTemporal` and BOTH have to move to a constructor
   that is still unwitnessed — or the fixture has to reach a temporal column
   some other way.
3. `RETURN point({x: 1, y: 2})` — expected `function point does not exist`,
   never run. Not a temporal, so it would be a third gap rather than a name
   added to this one, and the refusal prose would have to change: the present
   message says "defines no temporal constructor at all".
4. `RETURN duration.between(a, b)` — namespaced, so a different name from
   `duration` (Cypher.g4 §oC_FunctionName is `oC_Namespace oC_SymbolicName`) and
   not covered by the `duration` probe. `cypher.UnqualifiedFunctionCalls` drops
   namespaced calls by design, so refusing it needs a second scanner as well as
   a witness.
5. The SQLSTATE for every refusal in the undefined-function gap. The spike
   (gqlc-35yu.5) recorded the server's MESSAGE and not its code, so
   `TestAGERefusesTheFunctionsItDoesNotDefine` asserts the message alone —
   unlike the alternation gap, which pins 42601. PostgreSQL's
   `undefined_function` is 42883 and AGE plausibly reports through the same
   channel, but plausibly is not measured.
6. The first run of `TestAGERefusesTheFunctionsItDoesNotDefine` itself. It is
   nightly-and-manual only (`codegen-live.yml`, job `live-smoke-age`, skipped on
   PRs), so the five refusals it re-measures ship having been verified by hand in
   the spike and not yet by CI.

## Why this is a separate bead

Answering any of the above needs Docker, and therefore needs CI: the
`live-smoke-age` job is the only place in this project with a container. The
work is to add the probes, read the answers off the run, and then — for whichever
turn out to be refused — add them to the gap table with their recorded answers,
which the sweep will accept only once the live test carries them.

## Done when

- Each of (1)–(4) has been run against the pinned image and its answer recorded
  in this bead.
- Each one that AGE refuses is in `dialectGaps` with its probe and answer, and
  the ones AGE accepts are in the gap's `served` list so the gate is pinned not
  to refuse them.
- The undefined-function rows assert a SQLSTATE, as the alternation rows do.
- `just test` and one green `live-smoke-age` run.

title: resolver: an unlabelled binding is not narrowed by the edges that pin it
description:
Pre-existing on master, found while reviewing `gqlc-0tft`.

A binding that carries no label in the pattern is not narrowed by the edges that
pin it, so it resolves to the union of every declared type its edges could
reach rather than to the intersection they actually prove.

## Reproducer

    MATCH (p)-[f:FOUNDED]->(x:Company)
    OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[r:WORKS_AT]->(c:Company)
    RETURN p

With the Phase B feature disabled, `p` resolves to `Employee&Person`.

`p` carries no label of its own. Both edges pin it, but the resolver reads the
bare binding as unconstrained and hands back the union — so a caller writing
against the generated surface is offered a type the query cannot produce, and
the fields that differ between the two are the ones that will be empty.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed

Not this epic's territory: it is on master ahead of the multi-backend work and
is not reachable from any `gqlc-35yu` child. `gqlc-0tft` narrows plural
endpoints for *labelled* bindings; this is the unlabelled case one axis over,
and folding it in would have widened that branch past what its fixtures cover.

Adjacent to `gqlc-0tft` (same pass, same `s.bindings` walk) — check whether the
two should be taken together, because a fix here almost certainly lands in the
same function.

## Acceptance

The reproducer above resolves `p` to the intersection its edges prove, not the
union.

Both directions need a fixture: a bare binding that the edges genuinely narrow,
and a bare binding whose edges prove nothing, which must stay wide rather than
being narrowed to whichever type happened to be seen first. Confirm each
reddens when the narrowing is reverted — the defect class this repo keeps
finding is a guard green over nothing, and a fixture that passes before and
after the fix is not coverage for it.

Filed by the coordinator during `gqlc-0tft`'s review round.
notes:
PR #963 (branch fix/resolver-unlabelled-edge-narrowing, head 2544079c). Do not close on my word; adversarial review pending.

MEASURED CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S PREMISE. The literal reproducer in the description --
MATCH (p)-[f:FOUNDED]->(x:Company) / OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[r:WORKS_AT]->(c:Company) / RETURN p
on valid/schemas/satisfy_plural_edges.gql -- ALREADY resolves p to Employee&Person on
origin/master 2f74f2b6, and identically on the branch. candidateTypes already intersected
per-edge contributions; acceptance criterion 1 was met before this branch. What it did NOT do
is narrow the FAR END each contribution is read through, and that is the real defect.

Note also that Employee&Person is arguably the WRONG answer for that reproducer, because
WORKS_AT is OPTIONAL there -- a Person who founded a company and works nowhere still comes
back. That is gqlc-sxzj's class, not this one.

The witness actually fixed, on satisfy_plural_edges_inline_subtype.gql:
  MATCH (p)-[w:WORKS_AT]->(c:Company) / MATCH (c)-[h:HAS_DESK]->(d:Desk) / RETURN p.personOnly
  master: ErrAmbiguousBinding 'candidate types: Employee&Person, Person'  (the UNION)
  branch: accepted, STRING NOT NULL                                       (the INTERSECTION)

gqlc-sxzj (#852) measured before and after: byte-identical on both spellings of its witness.
Not fixed, not worsened.

Differential vs master's sweep.manifest.tsv: 11780 cells same verdict, same sentinel, same
detail; 0 moved; 740 new cells from the new fixtures/schemas.
ROUND 2 (adversarial REVISE answered). Head is now 220af33d, not 2544079c. Round 2 was body-only plus two comment edits; no behaviour changed (AST-stripped md5s equal across both edited files, positive control live).

The round-1 PR body's line "An empty narrowed intersection falls back to the unnarrowed one, so no refusal changes sentinel" was FALSE and is replaced. The fallback is a claim about candidateTypes' own return only: acc accumulates identically whether or not narrowing is nil and the narrowed answer is returned only when non-empty, so the function returns the empty set on exactly the inputs the nil lane does -- hence the narrowed lane cannot reach commitUnlabelledRound's case 0 and turn ErrAmbiguousBinding into ErrUnknownLabel. It constrains NOTHING downstream of a successful commit. Falsifier, on valid/schemas/satisfy_plural_edges_inline_subtype.gql:
  MATCH (p)-[w:WORKS_AT]->(c:Company) MATCH (c)-[h:HAS_DESK]->(d:Desk) RETURN p.employeeId
master 2f74f2b6 -> ErrAmbiguousBinding; head -> ErrUnknownProperty. A refusal moving, not an acceptance lost, but a refusal changing sentinel all the same.

Differential re-measured this round over the WHOLE cross product rather than master's manifest alone: 12518 same / 0 detail / 0 sentinel / 0 verdict, 2 cells refuse->accept, both the intended witness.

CORRECTION (2026-08-18, orchestrator, after round-2 adversarial review). Two errors in the ROUND 2 paragraph above; the paragraph is left standing so the record shows what was said.

1. "12518 same / 0 detail / 0 sentinel / 0 verdict, 2 cells refuse->accept" -- the verdict figure is wrong. It is 2 different-verdict, not 0. The clause contradicts the clause immediately after it (2 cells cannot change refuse->accept while 0 verdicts differ), and the categories only sum to the cross-product total on the corrected figure: 12518 same + 2 different = 12520, and 12520 is the measured cell count at this head (183+130 = 313 schemas x queries, times 40). Read: 12518 same / 0 detail / 0 sentinel / 2 verdict. The author's own working log recorded it correctly; only this durable carrier was wrong.

2. "Head is now 220af33d ... Round 2 was body-only plus two comment edits" -- stale by one commit. Round 2's head is 60cd12c2 and it carries three commits, not two. The substance is unaffected: the round remained comment-only, and the AST-stripped-md5 proof was independently re-derived at 60cd12c2 with a live positive control per file.

Neither error touches a measurement. The differential itself was re-derived independently by the reviewer and reproduces exactly: 12518 same / 0 detail / 0 sentinel / 2 verdict, both differing cells being valid/unlabelled_narrowed_by_pinned_far_end.cypher against the two copies of the new schema, refuse->accept, which is the intended witness.

Filed here rather than in the PR body because a bead note is one of this repository's three durable carriers and a wrong number in it outlives the PR.

title: codegen: ANY PROPERTY VALUE has no fixture on any target, so its column path is unexercised
description:
`gqlc-dcap` fixed `ANY VALUE` query columns (they resolved to Go `any` and took
the driver-carrier lane, emitting `neo4j.GetRecordValue[any]`, which does not
compile) and added `schema_any_property` fixtures plus an `AnythingColumns`
runtime corpus entry.

`ANY PROPERTY VALUE` is a distinct declared width in the same family and has
**no fixture on any target**. Found by `linus-dcap-ibg5-r1` while reviewing that
branch.

## Why this is not just a missing test

The two widths are close enough that the `ANY VALUE` fix might already cover
`ANY PROPERTY VALUE`, or might not, and nothing in the tree answers which. The
question is whether it resolves to the same Go type and the same `ColumnKind`.
If it does, the routing `dcap` added applies and this bead is a fixture. If it
resolves differently -- to a narrower carrier, or to a different kind -- then it
takes a different lane and `dcap`'s fix does not reach it, which would mean the
same compile failure is still live under a different declaration.

Answering that is the first task, and the answer decides whether this is a
half-hour of fixtures or a second fix.

## Where it must land

`schema_any_property` is the natural home, enrolled on all three targets so it
also sits inside `TestBackendInvariantSurface`. Cover nullable and non-nullable,
single-column and multi-column, the same axes `dcap` covered.

## The trap

Do not let this rest on golden bytes. A golden-only kill proves the bytes moved,
not that behaviour is pinned -- `-update` blesses it away. `dcap` added
`AnythingColumns` to the runtime corpus for exactly that reason and this needs
the equivalent: read the emitted decoder back over driver values, including a
held null.

Related: `gqlc-tez0` records that the `record.Get` lane on neo4j emits no
arrived-null gate at all, which is the exception among column kinds. If
`ANY PROPERTY VALUE` shares that lane it inherits the same gap, so check the two
together.

title: ci: the vuln gate's directory-coverage postcondition passes vacuously over an empty walk
description:
`gqlc-pig9` added a second half to the govulncheck gate's postcondition: every
directory holding a Go file must have been matched by `go list ./...` under the
derived tags. It is what catches the wholly-build-constrained directory that
`go list`'s wildcard silently skips.

It is checked as a comparison between two sets: the directories the on-disk walk
found, and the directories `go list` matched.

## The hole

If the walk itself returns nothing, both sets are empty, the comparison passes,
and the gate goes green having verified nothing. The walk is the measurement;
the comparison is only as good as it.

This is the same defect class the commit that introduced it was fixing, one
level up. `gqlc-nsq4` closed exactly this shape on the accepted-advisory
register -- 'the register was fail-closed only while it was non-empty' -- and
graded the id extraction against the output it reads so an empty measurement
fails rather than passes. The directory walk did not get the same treatment.

Ways the walk can empty that are not hypothetical: the module-root discovery it
is bounded by returns nothing; a `find` predicate stops matching after a
coreutils change; the walk root is computed relative to a cwd that moved.

## Fix

Grade the walk against something independently derived, the way the id
extraction is now graded against the `Vulnerability #` header count. At minimum
the walk must find at least one directory per discovered module, since a Go
module with no directory containing a Go file is not a thing.

## Acceptance

Break the walk so it returns the empty set and confirm the gate FAILS. Today it
exits 0. That single reproduction is the whole bead.

Note `test/data/tagblind` already asserts its own shape before any scan runs,
for the same reason -- a fixture that quietly stopped having its shape would take
the guards out of service silently. This bead extends that reasoning from the
fixture to the walk.

Backup: /tmp/quota-rescue/20260804/vuln-p2.patch and /tmp/quota-rescue/20260804/modscope/. Resume from the working tree; do NOT reset or git restore.

An empty walk is now the measurement broken, not the module empty (3e9388ef), and
a walk that failed halfway is not a walk that found nothing (30f1db21). The
vacuous-pass hole this bead describes — both sets empty, comparison passes, gate
green having verified nothing — is refused rather than shrugged at.

The branch's thesis is exactly this bead's: an empty measurement must FAIL, not
silently pass. Round 3 found the branch had NOT applied that correction to two of
its own new checks (they compared sets disjoint on this corpus, so the guarded
ordering was untestable); round 4 found a third instance; both are closed and

title: bd-gh-sync's pull path reports 'held 0' over a bead set nobody witnessed
description:
`gqlc-w4q9` established the rule that a listing this script could not read must
not be counted as an empty listing. `gqlc-mbe0` extended it to listings
truncated at their `--limit`. Both landed on the **push** path.

The pull path does not apply it.

## The shape

`bd list` answering `[]` with exit 0 on pull yields:

    bd-gh-sync: pulled 0 bead(s), held 0, left N unmirrored GH issue(s) alone.

`held 0` over a bead set nobody witnessed. Push refuses exactly this shape and
exits BLIND; pull reports a number as though it had counted something.

It is loud in practice — every mirrored bead becomes an ORPHAN line, so a human
watching the output will notice. That is why this is P2 and not P1. But "a human
would probably notice" is not the standard the push side was held to, and the
asymmetry is unexplained: the same failure, on the same script, one line apart,
gets a refusal on one side and a cheerful zero on the other.

## The trap, which is why this is not a five-minute fix

The symmetric guard does **not** work here, and the implementer of `gqlc-mbe0`
deliberately did not add it. A bead's `external_ref` regex is `/issues/(\d+)$`
over any URL, so a ref can legitimately name **another repository**. Mirrored
beads plus an empty all-state listing is therefore a reachable, legitimate
configuration — and a guard that refuses it would false-alarm on every
`git pull`.

So the fix has to distinguish "the listing was unreadable" from "the listing was
readable and genuinely empty", on a path where an empty answer is a normal
answer. Push does not have that problem because a push of N>0 followed by an
empty open listing is contradictory on its face.

That distinction is the actual work of this bead. Candidates: separate `bd list`'s
exit status and its parse from its cardinality, so an unreadable listing is
refused on the *status* rather than inferred from the count; or scope the
witness to beads whose `external_ref` names *this* repository, which makes the
contradiction recoverable.

## Acceptance

An unreadable pull-side listing exits BLIND naming the reason. A legitimately
empty one still exits 0. A test for each, and the second must fail if the first
guard is widened to swallow it.

Filed by the coordinator from `carmack-ghsync-p3b`'s out-of-scope list.
notes:
Landed via PR #825 (branch fix/bd-gh-sync-pull-witness, 15 commits, squashed).
The prior session's work was never pushed; this session rebased onto master
(f1f23cb6, clean — no conflicts with PR #778, which was already an ancestor),

2. The escaping was then unasserted on the per-bead WARNING one line above the

title: ANY VALUE columns diverge between neo4j and AGE on null, behind an identical declared surface
description:
`gqlc-dcap` fixed the compile failure in `ANY VALUE` column projections
(`neo4j.GetRecordValue[any]` does not compile, because `any` does not satisfy
`neo4j.RecordValue`) and added `AnythingColumns` to the runtime corpus. Doing so
exposed two divergences it did not fix, both on the null path.

## The two shapes

**Non-nullable `ANY VALUE` arriving null.** neo4j hands the nil straight
through to the caller's `any` field. AGE fails the row via its `raw == nil`
gate. Same query, same declared Go type, two different outcomes — one returns a
value the caller must nil-check on a field the schema said was non-nullable, the
other returns an error.

**Nullable `ANY VALUE` when AGE delivers agtype `null` as text rather than SQL
NULL.** AGE would give pointer-to-non-nil-holding-nil where neo4j gives a nil
pointer. Both type-check; they differ in what `if x.Maybe == nil` answers.

## Why nothing catches this

`TestBackendInvariantSurface` compares **declarations only**, so an identical
`Maybe *any` on both backends is all it sees. `gqlc-05tl`'s new decoder gate is
about label reachability and does not touch this either.

The runtime corpus *would* catch it, but only neo4j's half runs: the AGE corpus
needs a live container, and the machine this was implemented on has no Docker.
So the divergence is currently unmeasurable rather than merely unmeasured — the
first thing this bead needs is a live AGE run, which means CI (`codegen-live.yml`
runs nightly, and `live-smoke-age` exists).

This is the same measurement gap the `gqlc-35yu` epic has been closing one
construct at a time; `ANY VALUE` is a construct nobody has pointed the live
battery at yet.

## What to decide

Which behaviour is correct, then make both backends do it. The candidates:

1. **Non-nullable null is an error on both.** Consistent with AGE today, and
   with the project's general posture that a schema's promise is load-bearing.
   Changes neo4j's behaviour for existing callers.
2. **Non-nullable null passes through on both.** Consistent with neo4j today.
   Means a non-nullable field can hand back nil, which makes the nullability
   annotation decorative for `ANY VALUE`.
3. **Refuse `ANY VALUE` non-nullable columns at generate time.** The ADR
   0025/0027 posture — if the two backends cannot agree, do not emit. Most
   consistent with the epic's precedent, most disruptive.

Do not decide this from reading. Run the live AGE corpus first and find out what
AGE actually does with an agtype `null`, because shape two above is stated as a
conditional ("*if* AGE delivers it as text") and nobody has checked.

## Acceptance

A live AGE run recording what actually happens in both shapes; a decision
recorded in an ADR; both backends agreeing; and a corpus case that runs on both
and would fail if they diverged again.

Filed by the coordinator from `carmack-dcap-ibg5`'s out-of-scope list.
notes:
SHARPENED (2026-08-04, coordinator) from linus-dcap-ibg5-r1's NB-4, which located the mechanism rather than the symptom.

The divergence is not a subtle encoding difference. It is a MISSING GATE, and the asymmetry is exact:

- AGE emits writeNonNullGate on this lane.
- neo4j emits NO arrived-null gate on the record.Get lane AT ALL.

That makes the record.Get lane the EXCEPTION among neo4j column kinds -- every other column kind on that backend carries a null gate. So this is not 'two backends chose differently'; it is one lane on one backend that skipped the thing all its siblings do. That reframes the fix: the question is not 'which behaviour should both adopt' but 'why does this one lane have no gate', and the answer is likely that gqlc-dcap routed ColumnProperty to record.Get without carrying the gate across with it.

Which means the regression window opens with gqlc-dcap (PR #767) and the fix belongs close behind it.

Acceptance should assert the gate's PRESENCE structurally -- a sweep over column kinds on the neo4j path confirming each emits an arrived-null gate -- not just a behavioural row for ANY VALUE. A behavioural row pins this one column kind; the sweep is what stops the next lane from skipping it too. Beware the usual trap: a sweep over an empty or mis-derived set of column kinds passes vacuously, so pin the set's size against an independently derived count.

title: neo4j decoders consult no label, so decodePerson fills a Person from a Post
description:
`gqlc-05tl` built `TestEmittedDecodersGuardOnlyOnStampableLabels`, which checks
that every string an emitted `decode<T>` compares for equality is a label the
fixture's schema actually declares. It found the AGE join-spelling bug it was
built for.

Building it surfaced a second, larger thing on the other side of the ledger.

## The finding

The neo4j targets' decoders carry **no label guard at all**. The gate records
this as `labelGuardingTargets[neo4j-go-v5] = false`, guarding 0 of 123
decoders, and that number is asserted rather than assumed — so this is measured,
not suspected.

`decodePerson(node dbtype.Node)` reads properties off the node without ever
consulting `node.Labels`. Hand it a `Post` whose property names happen to
overlap and it fills a `Person` and returns nil error.

## Why it is a separate bead

`gqlc-05tl`'s gate is about **reachability** — a decoder whose guard no wire
value can satisfy is dead code. This is the opposite axis: a decoder with no
guard accepts too much. Same file, opposite failure, and fixing it means
emitting a guard that does not exist today rather than correcting one that does.

It is also a behaviour change on a shipped backend, which is not the kind of
thing to bolt onto a branch whose subject was a test.

## What needs deciding first

Whether a missing label check is a defect at all. The argument that it is not:
a caller reaches `decodePerson` only through a query the resolver typed, so the
driver should not be handing back a `Post` in the first place. The argument
that it is: that reasoning is exactly the "the resolver would never build this"
shape that `gqlc-h4ug` moved five taxonomy rows out of §3 for — what the
resolver builds does not bound what a caller can hand over, and `dbtype.Node`
arrives from the driver, not from gqlc.

Note the asymmetry it creates meanwhile: AGE guards on 95 of 95, neo4j on 0 of
123. Two backends disagreeing about whether a wrong-label node is an error is a
divergence in *behaviour* behind an identical declared surface — precisely what
ADR 0025 line 121-126 already records as invisible to
`TestBackendInvariantSurface`.

## Acceptance

Either a decision recorded in an ADR that the neo4j decoders are correct
without a label check, with the reasoning; or a guard emitted and
`labelGuardingTargets` flipped to `true` for both neo4j targets, with the
ledger's count derived rather than re-blessed.

Filed by the coordinator from `carmack-05tl`'s out-of-scope list.
notes:
RULING (2026-08-04, coordinator). The bead asks whether a missing label check is a defect at all before any work starts. Deciding: IT IS. Emit the guard.

The argument that it is not a defect -- 'a caller reaches decodePerson only through a query the resolver typed, so the driver should not be handing back a Post' -- is the 'the resolver would never build this' shape, and THIS REPO HAS ALREADY RULED ON THAT SHAPE ONCE. gqlc-h4ug moved five taxonomy rows out of s3 for exactly it. Re-litigating it here to the opposite answer would leave the codebase holding two incompatible postures about the same reasoning, which is worse than either posture alone.

The substantive reason it fails: dbtype.Node arrives FROM THE DRIVER, not from gqlc. What the resolver builds bounds what gqlc ASKS FOR; it does not bound what comes back. A decoder is a boundary, and the repo's own rule is that boundaries validate.

The asymmetry is the second reason and it is not cosmetic. AGE guards 95 of 95, neo4j 0 of 123, behind an identical declared surface. The epic's central design property is that the Go surface must not vary by backend -- and while that property is literally about declarations, ADR 0025's precedent extends it to what a caller can actually rely on: it rejected a shape because 'it emits a column no decoder can fill at exit 0'. This is that inverted -- a decoder that fills from the wrong thing at exit 0. Same objection, other sign.

## What to build

A label guard on the neo4j decoders matching AGE's posture: mismatch is an ERROR, not a silent skip and not a warning. A decoder handed the wrong node type has no correct value to return, so there is nothing for a softer outcome to mean.

## The extensibility property, which is the part that must not be skipped

gqlc-05tl's gate already measures this and ASSERTS the number (labelGuardingTargets[neo4j-go-v5] = false, 0 of 123). That assertion is what makes this bead's completion checkable rather than claimed. When the guard lands, that same gate must flip to 123 of 123 and the assertion must be updated to demand it -- so a future emitter arm that forgets the guard reddens. Do not delete the census to make it pass; invert what it demands.

Beware the standing trap: a census that counts 0 of 0 passes vacuously. Pin the denominator against an independently derived decoder count, not against itself.

Sequencing: 05tl's gate must merge first, since this bead's acceptance is expressed in its terms.

title: ci: build_tags derivation turns !windows into -tags windows, excluding the file it came from
description:
The `build_tags` derivation added on the vuln-gate branch reads `//go:build`
lines and turns the terms it finds into `-tags` arguments. It cannot tell a
**build tag** from a **GOOS/GOARCH term** or a **Go-version term**, and the
three are syntactically identical in a constraint expression.

The consequence is not "a term is ignored" — it is that a negated platform term
becomes a positive tag that **excludes the very file it came from**:

    //go:build !windows      ->      -tags windows

That is the inverse of the intent. A file guarded to build everywhere *except*
Windows is handed a flag that makes it build nowhere the scan looks. The scan
then reports clean over a file it never compiled.

`go1.N` terms have the same problem in a different direction: `-tags go1.24` is
meaningless to the toolchain, which derives release tags itself, so the term is
silently inert rather than wrong.

## Why it has not bitten

The tree's live files use plain custom tags (`codegen_live`) with no negation
and no platform terms, so every term currently derived is a genuine build tag.
The derivation is correct on today's corpus and wrong in general.

## Shape of the fix

Terms fall into three classes and only one belongs in `-tags`:

- **known GOOS/GOARCH values** — `go tool dist list` is authoritative; these
  should set `GOOS`/`GOARCH` or be dropped, never passed as tags
- **`go1.N`** — drop; the toolchain owns release tags
- **everything else** — a custom build tag, pass through

Negation needs a decision of its own: `!foo` cannot be satisfied by adding a
tag, so the honest handling is to drop the term and let the file build in the
default configuration, which is what its author meant.

## Acceptance

A fixture file carrying `//go:build !windows` is compiled by the scan on Linux.
Verify by mutation: restore the naive derivation, watch the file drop out of
the scanned set, revert.

Filed by the coordinator from `carmack-vulngate-r2`'s out-of-scope list.
Discovered-from `gqlc-rohp`.
notes:
CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT (2026-08-04, linus-vulngate-r1). The negated case reproduces exactly as filed:

    derived tags:  windows
    IgnoredGoFiles under -tags windows:  example.com/revneg: unixonly.go

//go:build !windows derives tag 'windows'; -tags windows then satisfies 'windows', so !windows is false and the file is EXCLUDED. The gate does go red, so this is fail-closed rather than fail-open -- but the diagnostic names only two causes (a GOOS/GOARCH filename suffix, or //go:build ignore) and the real cause is a third: the derivation excluded the file itself. The diagnostic wording is being fixed on fix/vuln-gate-derivation; the derivation defect this bead owns is not.

Also measured: release-tag terms are benign, not merely inert -- 'go list -tags go1.30' is accepted, rc=0. So the go1.N half of this bead is cosmetic and the GOOS/GOARCH half is the load-bearing one.

Closed by branch fix/vuln-gate-walk-and-fence @ 620cea66. Adversarial review PASS
at round 5 (/tmp/lead/verdict-vulnr5.md).

A build tag is now a judgement about a term rather than the term with its
punctuation stripped (59436a0a). `!windows` is classified as a platform term and
never becomes `-tags windows`. Two follow-on corrections: a GOOS spelling declared
in run.build-tags is still a GOOS (603ebefc), and a platform spelling the toolchain
knows is one whatever the live `go tool dist list` says (a367b89f) — the latter
adds a hardcoded floor unioned into the vocabulary, byte-faithful 18/18 GOOS and
24/24 GOARCH to GOROOT's syslist.go.

Disclosed cost, pinned rather than left in prose:
TestAnUndeclaredFloorOnlySpellingIsDroppedWhereItUsedToBeRefused
(internal/tools/modscope/main_test.go:582) asserts BOTH halves — pre-floor
gradePlatformTerms still errors on an undeclared `//go:build hurd`, post-floor
platformTerms drops it silently. Verified first-party by the lead: name is unique
in the tree, runs anchored, passes; and by the reviewer under mutation, where
`_ = platformFloor` and deleting "hurd" from platformFloor both KILL it by name
with `go build ./...` rc=0 asserted per row.

The implementer's own worry that the pin would misfire on a real Go hurd port is
false, and the reviewer showed why: gradePlatformTerms/platformTerms take the

[]string{"linux/amd64","windows/amd64"}, and it guards on

title: ci: the govulncheck fence hardcodes test/data/codegen while the sweep discovers modules
description:
`gqlc-rohp` made the govulncheck sweep discover Go modules from disk rather than
naming them, so a third module added to the tree is scanned. The **fence** was
not given the same treatment and still names `test/data/codegen` literally.

A third module therefore gets a vulnerability scan and no build, vet, tidy or
lint gate at all — the weaker half of the pair is the one that generalised.

## Sites that hardcode the path

- `justfile:140-142` — `test-codegen-fence`'s `go build` / `go vet -tags
  codegen_live` / `go mod tidy -diff` all `cd test/data/codegen`.
- `justfile:159, 216, 221, 229` — the same literal in the lint and check
  recipes.
- `check-codegen-external-tests` — sweeps that one directory.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `codegen-fence` — invokes the recipe, so it
  inherits the literal.

## Why this is worth closing rather than accepting

The repo has exactly two modules today, so nothing is currently unfenced. The
cost is that the invariant "every module in this tree is built, vetted, tidied
and linted" is not stated anywhere that can fail. Adding a module is a silent
downgrade: `govulncheck` picks it up, everything else does not, and no gate
reports the asymmetry.

## Shape of the fix

Derive the module set once — the same discovery `gqlc-rohp` built for the
sweep — and drive both the scan and the fence from it. If the recipes cannot
share the discovery, the minimum is a gate asserting that the set of modules
the fence covers equals the set the sweep finds.

## Acceptance

Add a throwaway third module under the tree, confirm the fence covers it
without editing a recipe, then remove it. A hardcoded-list implementation must
redden that check.

title: conformance: AGE un-enrolment from an alternation-carrying fixture is invisible
description:
A conformance fixture under `internal/codegen/conformance/testdata/invalid/`
names, in its manifest, the sentinel each enrolled target is expected to
answer with. `TestInvalid` compares the sentinel a target actually returned
against the one the manifest names, and reports a mismatch as an ordinary
test failure.

That is the right shape for a fixture whose refusal is a property of the
fixture. It is the wrong shape for a **structural rule about a backend** —
"AGE refuses every query carrying relationship-type alternation" — because
the rule is enforced only where a manifest happens to spell it.

## The concrete hole

`gqlc-35yu.14` un-enrolled `invalid/unrepresentable_edge_union_shared_label`
from `apache-age-pgx-v5`: the fixture is `-[r:LIKES|WROTE]-`, so AGE now
answers it with `ErrRelationshipTypeAlternation` rather than the
`ErrOutOfC6Scope` its manifest names. The un-enrolment is correct, and the
branch argues the coverage it carried is preserved by
`invalid/plural_endpoint_edge_union_shared_label`, which reaches the same
portable refusal with no `|` in it.

But nothing in the tree states the rule that made the un-enrolment necessary.
If a future fixture adds an `apache-age-pgx-v5` target to a query containing
`|`, the failure it produces is "expected sentinel X, got Y" — indistinguishable
from a plain manifest typo. A reader fixes it by editing the manifest to name
`ErrRelationshipTypeAlternation`, which is exactly wrong: the fixture should
either drop the AGE target or lose the alternation.

Symmetrically, if the gate is later weakened so AGE stops refusing alternation,
no test names that. `unrepresentable_edge_union_shared_label` would quietly
become enrollable again and nothing would notice it had not been re-enrolled.

## Shape of the fix

Assert the rule directly, over the corpus rather than over one fixture: for
every fixture enrolled for an `apache-age-pgx-v5` target, its query text
contains no relationship-type alternation — reusing
`cypher.RelationshipTypeAlternations` rather than grepping for `|`, since the
pipe character appears in list comprehensions too. The complement is the
interesting half: every fixture that DOES carry an alternation is either
un-enrolled from AGE, or enrolled with `ErrRelationshipTypeAlternation` named.

Either polarity is defensible; pick one and say why. What must not survive is
the current state, where the rule exists only in the reviewer's head and in a
commit message.

## Acceptance

Adding an `apache-age-pgx-v5` target to a `|`-carrying invalid fixture turns a
gate red with a message naming the rule, not a sentinel mismatch. Verify by
mutation: make the edit, watch it fail, revert.

Filed by the coordinator from a candidate raised by the `gqlc-35yu.14` round-3
implementer. Adjacent to `gqlc-rv0h` (a backend's sentinels are unnameable in a
manifest) — check whether that bead's fix subsumes this one before starting.

title: resolver: ResolvedType is not sealed at all — embedding defeats the marker, so no switch on it can be total
description:
`internal/resolver/validated.go:79` documents `ResolvedType` as "the sealed
sum of resolved types". The unexported `isResolvedType()` marker does seal it
against **new implementations**. It does not seal it against the **pointer
forms of the existing eight**: every variant declares both `isResolvedType()`
and `String()` with **value receivers** (`validated.go:97-364`), and a
pointer's method set contains its value methods. So `*resolver.ResolvedNode`
satisfies `ResolvedType` while `case resolver.ResolvedNode:` does not match
it. The sum an out-of-package caller can inhabit has **sixteen** forms plus
nil.

The doc comment says none of that. Any package that type-switches on
`ResolvedType` and reads that comment will conclude its default arm is dead,
and will be wrong in the same way `internal/codegen/prepare.go` was.

## Provenance

`gqlc-h4ug` found and closed this for `internal/codegen`: two branches tagged
`//gqlc:unreachable` on the strength of that reasoning turned out reachable by
an assembled `Input`, returning their sentinel cleanly with no panic. Those
rows moved §3 → §2 and the taxonomy's §5.1 step 5 was rewritten to tell a
classifier to count a sum's **inhabitants**, not its declarations.

That fixed the consumer. It did not fix the claim at the source, and the
implementer explicitly flagged that they **did not audit consumers beyond
`internal/codegen`**.

## Scope

Two parts, and the second is the one that matters.

1. Correct the doc comment at `validated.go:79` to say what the seal does and
   does not cover.
2. **Audit every other type switch on `ResolvedType` in the tree** for the
   same undercount. Grep is enough to find them; the judgement is per site —
   a switch whose default already refuses is fine, one whose default is
   documented or tagged as unreachable is not.

Note the related posture question belongs to `gqlc-edze`, not here: whether
pointer forms should be normalised away at `Prepare`'s boundary so switches
see value forms only, or refused with the default arm treated as a permanent
reachable branch. This bead is about the claim being accurate wherever it is
made; `edze` is about choosing the behaviour.

## Acceptance

The doc comment is accurate, and every `ResolvedType` type switch outside
`internal/codegen` has been visited with a one-line verdict recorded — either
"default refuses, fine" or a filed follow-up. A grep-and-shrug is not the
deliverable; the deliverable is knowing the count.

Suggested by the `gqlc-h4ug` round-5 implementer, filed by the coordinator.

PR #881 merged 2026-08-17 as 2ca30818; GH #744 CLOSED.

The guard walks the AST, not source bytes.

title: codegen: TestBackendInvariantSurface compares declarations only, so an unfillable decoder is invisible
description:
`TestBackendInvariantSurface` (`internal/codegen/conformance/conformance_test.go`)
is the gate that holds this project's central design property: the Go surface a
caller writes against must not vary by backend, only the encode/decode path
does. It compares **declarations only** — `*ast.GenDecl` with `token.TYPE`, and
`*ast.FuncDecl` with a receiver.

So an unexported, receiver-less function is invisible to it. `decodeFoo` is
exactly that shape. **A backend can emit a structurally identical declaration
whose decoder can never fire, and the invariant test stays green.**

## Measured, not argued

Found while implementing `gqlc-35yu.15`. AGE stamps exactly one label per
vertex, so a node type keyed on two labels cannot be represented. One candidate
posture was "emit the struct anyway, with a label check". Built and measured:
patching `wireEntity` to return `ok=true` with `label = string(labels)` left
`TestBackendInvariantSurface` **green in 0.034s**, over a `models.go`
containing

    if label != "Employee&Person" {
        return PersonEmployee{}, fmt.Errorf("decode PersonEmployee: expected label %q, got %q", "Employee&Person", label)
    }

`Employee&Person` is gqlc's own `LabelSetKey` join spelling. No AGE vertex
carries it and no AGE statement can stamp it, so that decoder is dead on
arrival. `gqlc generate` exits 0 and the invariant gate says the surfaces match
— which, on its own terms, they do.

That posture was rejected on ADR 0025's precedent ("it emits a column no
decoder can fill at exit 0"), **not** on a test. `gqlc-35yu.15` records the
distinction in ADR 0027 so a reader does not go looking for the gate that
caught it.

## The question this bead has to answer first

Is declarations-only *deliberate*? There is a real argument for it: the
invariant is about the surface a **caller** writes against, and a caller cannot
write against an unexported receiver-less function. On that reading the gate is
correctly scoped and the residual belongs to a different gate.

The counter-argument is that "identical surface, one of which cannot decode"
satisfies the letter of the property while defeating its purpose. The whole
point of holding the surface invariant is that a caller can retarget without
rewriting; a struct that never fills does not survive retargeting.

Settle that before writing code. If declarations-only is deliberate, this
becomes a documentation bead plus a *separate* gate that asserts every emitted
decoder is reachable — which is the claim actually wanted. If it is an
oversight, widen the comparison.

## Prior art in this repo

`.13` built the shape for the second option: `internal/codegen/neo4j/corpus_test.go`
writes the generated package to a temp dir and compiles and **runs** it under
`GOPROXY=off` against a driver stub, asserting values rather than bytes. A
decoder that cannot fire is visible to a harness that runs it and invisible to
one that parses it.

## Acceptance

Whichever route: a mutation that makes an emitted decoder unfillable while
leaving its declaration identical must turn some gate red. The `wireEntity`
mutation above is a ready-made one — it is compile-valid, it reproduces in
seconds, and it is currently green.

Not filed by the `.15` implementer because it may be deliberate; ruled a bead
by the coordinator rather than a finding, since the design question outlives
the branch that surfaced it.
notes: PR #847 merged 2026-08-17 as 11a652ad. Independent round-3 review PASS, zero blockers (/tmp/factory/verdict-847-r2.md). GH #745 and this bead were already closed from a prior cycle and stay closed per the coordinator ruling; the Closes #745 line in the body was inert and closed nothing. Residue left open by design: gqlc-eo74, gqlc-9xy0, gqlc-2h9w, gqlc-mp9n, gqlc-rqu8. One report-only nit deferred to gqlc-* (nonReservedWords count stated as 46, actual 47).

Classification turned on where the holder was written rather than on the helper.

title: codegen/neo4j: two non-nullable list columns in one query redeclare the accumulator local 'acc'
description:
`writeListColumnDecodeIndent` in `internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go`
emits the list accumulator under a hardcoded name:

    acc := make(<GoType>, 0, len(<value>))

On the non-nullable arm that `:=` sits at the row-assembly block's own indent,
so a query projecting two or more non-nullable list columns emits two `acc`
declarations in one scope. The emitted file does not compile:

    ./queries.cypher.go:136:7: no new variables on left side of :=
    ./queries.cypher.go:136:10: cannot use make([]int32, 0, len(value1)) (value of type []int32) as []string value in assignment

Generation exits 0; the emitter's format gate only parses.

The nullable arm hides the defect because its `acc` is emitted inside
`if !isNil { ... }`, a scope of its own. So a query mixing one non-nullable
list column with any number of nullable ones is fine, and only two
non-nullable ones collide — which is why no fixture has hit it.

## Reproduction

Against a schema declaring `tags :: LIST<STRING> NOT NULL` and
`ranks :: LIST<INT32> NOT NULL`:

    // name: ListyColumns :many
    MATCH (l:Listy) RETURN l.tags AS tags, l.ranks AS ranks

`TestGoldenBuild` fails on the emitted file.

## Fix shape

Name the accumulator positionally, the way `valueName(i)` names the column
local and the way `writeSliceNarrow` suffixes its locals by depth. The file's
own comments already give the rule for exactly this class of bug —
`writeEntityFieldDecode`: "The local the value lands in is positional. A name
derived from the property is any identifier the schema author chose, including
one this scope already holds". The accumulator escaped it.

## Acceptance

A fixture projecting two non-nullable list columns in one query, whose golden
compiles under `TestGoldenBuild`; reverting to the hardcoded `acc` must redden
it.
notes: SEQUENCING (2026-08-03, epic coordinator): held until fix/neo4j-carrier-followups merges. Both fixes land in internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go, the same file that branch rewrites (carriesElemBare, walkListElemBody's ColumnProperty arm, walkListElemPlan's index gate). dcap's own fix shape — route writeSingleColumnDecodeIndent through ridesADriverCarrier, mirroring what carriesElemBare now does one axis down — only exists once that branch lands. Genuine territory collision, not a conflict-risk excuse. Staff both together as one branch afterwards; they are the same file and the same class.
close_reason: Closed

title: codegen/neo4j: a query column of ANY VALUE width emits GetRecordValue[any], which does not compile
description:
A query that projects a property whose declared width is `ANY VALUE` resolves to
a `ResolvedProperty` with `GoType "any"` and `Kind: codegen.ColumnProperty`. In
`internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go`, `writeSingleColumnDecodeIndent`
falls through for `ColumnProperty` to

    neo4j.GetRecordValue[any](records[0], "payload")

`any` is a member of neither `neo4j.PropertyValue` nor `neo4j.RecordValue`, so
that instantiation does not compile:

    any does not satisfy neo4j.RecordValue

Generation still exits 0, because the emitter's format gate only parses.

## Reproduction

Against a schema declaring `payload :: ANY VALUE`, add

    // name: BinPayload :one
    MATCH (b:Bin {id: $id}) RETURN b.payload AS payload

to a fixture and regenerate. `TestGoldenBuild` (and `just test-codegen-fence`)
fail on the emitted file.

## Why it is not caught today

No fixture projects an `ANY VALUE` property as a top-level query column. The
list-element case is now covered (gqlc-3kds added `schema_list_any_property`'s
query columns), but the scalar case is not.

## Fix shape

The entity path already has the lane: `writeShapelessFieldDecode` reads the
Props map directly rather than calling `GetProperty[T]`, gated on
`ridesADriverCarrier`. The query path has the equivalent lane in
`writeAnyColumnDecodeIndent` (`record.Get`). Route `ColumnProperty` with
`!ridesADriverCarrier(f.GoType)` to it, mirroring `carriesElemBare`'s
`ColumnProperty` arm on the element path.

## Acceptance

A fixture projecting an `ANY VALUE` property as a query column, whose golden
compiles under `TestGoldenBuild`; and the neo4j runtime corpus harness
(`internal/codegen/neo4j/corpus_test.go`) exercising the emitted method over a
record whose value is nil, asserting the caller is handed nil rather than a
decode error. Reverting the routing must redden the harness on the build.
notes: SEQUENCING (2026-08-03, epic coordinator): held until fix/neo4j-carrier-followups merges. Both fixes land in internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go, the same file that branch rewrites (carriesElemBare, walkListElemBody's ColumnProperty arm, walkListElemPlan's index gate). dcap's own fix shape — route writeSingleColumnDecodeIndent through ridesADriverCarrier, mirroring what carriesElemBare now does one axis down — only exists once that branch lands. Genuine territory collision, not a conflict-risk excuse. Staff both together as one branch afterwards; they are the same file and the same class.

title: conformance: a backend's sentinels are unnameable in a manifest, so no invalid fixture can cover one
description:
The conformance corpus can express a negative fixture for a shared-phase sentinel and cannot express one for a backend-local sentinel. invalid/*/manifest.json names its expected error through sentinelByName, whose lanes are built from three packages only: codegen., queryfile. and cypher.. Resolution runs through the hand-written sentinelIdent switch, and the conformance package deliberately imports no single backend — it resolves targets through the composed registry.

So age.ErrUnsupportedSchema and age.ErrUnsupportedQuery have no spelling a manifest can carry. A fixture naming either fails TestInvalid on the lookup ("unknown sentinel name %q"), not on the backend's behaviour, and TestSentinelReachability cannot see them at all.

CONSEQUENCE TODAY. Both AGE sentinels are held only by in-package tests under internal/codegen/age. That is real coverage, but it is not the corpus's, so the corpus's own claim to be the place a backend's refusals are recorded is false for every backend-local refusal. The gap is pre-existing; gqlc-35yu.15 hit it when deciding whether the multi-label refusal should gain an invalid/ fixture and concluded it could not, recording that in ADR 0027.

SHAPE OF THE FIX. Give the registry a way to publish a backend's sentinels — each registered target contributing a name-to-error map that the conformance harness composes into sentinelByName alongside the three existing lanes. That keeps the no-single-backend-import property, which is the constraint that makes the naive fix (import age in conformance_test.go) wrong.

Note the fix must also decide what TestSentinelReachability means for a backend sentinel: a per-target reachability requirement, or an opt-in, since not every target has a fixture for every other target's refusals.

title: ci: every live recipe selects tests by a hardcoded -run allowlist, so a new live test never runs
description:
Every live recipe selects tests by a hardcoded `-run` allowlist naming the
two top-level tests that existed when it was written:

    justfile:216  test-codegen-live:
      go test ... -run 'TestLiveSmoke|TestAGESessionInit' ./...
    justfile:221  test-codegen-live-neo4j:
      go test ... -run TestLiveSmoke -skip 'TestLiveSmoke/apache-age' ./...
    justfile:229  test-codegen-live-age:
      go test ... -run 'TestLiveSmoke|TestAGESessionInit' -skip 'TestLiveSmoke/neo4j' ./...

`go test -run` matches **top-level** test names, so a new top-level live
test is excluded from all three. It does not fail, it does not skip
visibly, it does not appear in the log at all — the package still reports
`ok` and the job still goes green.

On master the allowlist happens to be exhaustive:

    grep -rhoE "^func Test[A-Za-z0-9_]+\(t \*testing\.T\)" test/data/codegen/*.go

returns exactly `TestAGESessionInit` and `TestLiveSmoke`. **Nothing
enforces that.** The property the recipes depend on is maintained by
whoever happens to remember, and the failure mode when they do not is a
live battery that is green because it never ran.

## This is already live

`feat/age-edge-union-live` adds `TestAGERefusesRelationshipTypeAlternation`
as a top-level test in `test/data/codegen/live_age_dialect_test.go`, and
does not touch the recipes. That branch's central claim — that AGE 1.7.0
rejects relationship-type alternation, verified against a live container —
therefore has no execution path anywhere: not in PR CI, not in the
nightly, not under `just`.

It compounds with the AGE arm's gating. `live-smoke-age` is
`if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'` (`.github/workflows/codegen-live.yml:54`),
so the AGE half only runs on the nightly cron. A new top-level AGE live
test is thus excluded from the one job that would ever have run it.

## The nightly itself is real

Worth recording, because the sibling bead `gqlc-0oau` raises the adjacent
worry and this narrows it. `codegen-live.yml` fires on `schedule`
(cron `17 4 * * *`). Run `30794774319` on 2026-08-03 executed

    go test -count=1 -tags codegen_live \
      -run 'TestLiveSmoke|TestAGESessionInit' -skip 'TestLiveSmoke/neo4j' ./...

and reported `ok github.com/areqag/gqlc/test/data/codegen 12.677s`. The
container starts and the tests run. The defect is the selection, not the
schedule.

## Fix

Select structurally rather than by name. The recipes already have a
structural axis — the `codegen_live` build tag — and the arm split
(neo4j versus AGE) is what the `-run`/`-skip` pair is really encoding. A
recipe that names no test cannot go stale.

If a name-based split is genuinely needed for the arm separation, then
the exhaustiveness the recipes silently assume has to be **asserted**:
a test in the root module that parses `test/data/codegen/*.go` for
top-level `Test*` declarations and requires that set to equal the set the
recipes name. Set equality, not a count — it self-updates, and it catches
the declared-but-unselected case that a count cannot.

Note `-skip 'TestLiveSmoke/apache-age'` operates on **subtest** paths,
which is a different axis from the top-level `-run` and is not affected.

## Acceptance

Add a throwaway top-level live test that fails unconditionally. Confirm
it currently passes CI — that establishes the gate is watching nothing.
Then confirm the fix makes CI red naming it. Then remove it and confirm
green.

Found while auditing whether the nightly AGE battery had ever actually
executed, during the review round for gqlc-35yu.14. Pre-existing repo
condition; gqlc-35yu.14 is the first branch to trip it.
notes:
PR #882 (fix/live-recipe-structural-selection @ 771b7447), Closes #749. Close on merge, not before.

WHAT LANDED. internal/liverecipes reads the justfile's live `go test` command lines, the workflows that invoke them, and the top-level tests test/data/codegen declares (go/parser + go/build/constraint, so a commented-out func TestFoo is not a declaration). title: codegen: resolver.ResolvedType is not the closed sum prepare.go's switches assume
description:
`prepare.go`'s two catch-all arms — tagged `//gqlc:unreachable column-unknown-variant` and `//gqlc:unreachable list-elem-unknown-variant` — end their switch over `resolver.ResolvedType` by wrapping `ErrOutOfC6Scope` with `t.String()`.

`ResolvedType` is a sealed interface, but a nil interface value is not a member of any arm and reaches the default. Calling `String()` on it panics with a nil-pointer dereference before the `fmt.Errorf` that names the sentinel is ever evaluated.

Measured with an out-of-package caller assembling `codegen.Input` with `resolver.Column{Name: "x", Type: nil}` and calling `neo4j.New().Generate`: panic, not `ErrOutOfC6Scope`.

That is why both sites remain in §3 of `docs/specs/codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md` after gqlc-h4ug moved the reachable ones to §2: they are unreachable only because the guard that would report them crashes first. A branch that cannot return its sentinel because it faults is not a branch nothing reaches.

Fix: guard the nil case (either at the arm, or once at the top of the column/list-element walk) so the refusal is a wrapped `ErrOutOfC6Scope` naming the offending position. Then the two sites move to §2 with their own assembled-Input cases and their tags come off.
acceptance_criteria:
- A nil `resolver.ResolvedType` in a `Column` and in a `ResolvedList` element returns a wrapped `ErrOutOfC6Scope` naming the query and the position, not a panic.
- `column-unknown-variant` and `list-elem-unknown-variant` move from §3 to §2 of `docs/specs/codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md`, with assembled-Input cases in `internal/codegen/conformance/assembled_input_test.go` asserting the sentinel and the exact message.
- Their `//gqlc:unreachable` tags are removed and `TestSentinelTaxonomy` stays green.
notes:
# gqlc-edze — widened description (proposed; tracker owner to apply)

Current title still fits, but is narrower than the defect:

> codegen: the unknown-ResolvedType arms panic before they can return their sentinel

Suggested title:

> codegen: resolver.ResolvedType is not the closed sum prepare.go's switches assume

---

## Why the current description is incomplete

The bead says the two catch-all arms are unreachable because the guard
that would report them crashes first, and that they move from §3 to §2
once the nil case is guarded.

Both halves are now false, and `gqlc-h4ug` has landed the correction:

- **The arms are already reachable, and already return their sentinel
  cleanly.** `resolver.ResolvedType`'s unexported `isResolvedType()`
  marker seals the interface against *new implementations*. It does not
  seal it against the **pointer forms of the existing eight**: every
  variant declares both `isResolvedType()` and `String()` with **value
  receivers** (`internal/resolver/validated.go:97-364`), and a pointer's
  method set contains its value methods, so `*resolver.ResolvedNode`
  satisfies `ResolvedType` while `case resolver.ResolvedNode:` does not
  match it. The sum an out-of-package caller can inhabit has **sixteen**
  forms plus the nil; each of the three switches names **eight**.
  `t.String()` on a non-nil pointer dispatches to the value method, so
  the refusal completes as written.
- **The §3→§2 move is done.** `column-unknown-variant` and
  `list-elem-unknown-variant` are §2 rows in
  `docs/specs/codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md`, paid by assembled-`Input`
  cases using `&resolver.ResolvedNode{}`, and both `//gqlc:unreachable`
  tags are off. Those three acceptance criteria are satisfied and should
  be struck.

The nil panic is real and unfixed — but guarding nil alone leaves the
eight pointer inhabitants, which is the part the current criteria cannot
see.

## What is actually broken

**Two distinct defects at the same arms.**

1. **Nil panics at three reachable sites, not two.** The bead names the
   column arm and the list-element arm. The parameter assertion is a
   third: `prepare.go:626` calls `p.Type.String()` on the value that just
   failed the `ResolvedProperty` assertion. Confirmed by an
   out-of-package caller — a nil column, a nil list element and a nil
   param each panic with a nil-pointer dereference rather than refusing.
   Two further sites carry the same call behind a shadow
   (`prepare.go:705`, `prepare.go:879`); they are §3 today and would
   inherit the panic if their shadow ever moved.

2. **The sum is not closed.** Go offers no way to seal an interface
   against the pointer forms of its own value-receiver implementations,
   so "the switch names every variant, therefore the default is dead" is
   not an argument this codebase can make about `ResolvedType` — which
   is why §5.1 step 5 now tells a classifier to count *inhabitants*, not
   declarations. Decide the posture deliberately: either normalise
   pointer forms away at `Prepare`'s boundary so the switches see value
   forms only, or keep refusing them and treat the default arm as a
   permanent §2 branch. What is not acceptable is a default arm whose
   behaviour nobody chose.

## Corrected acceptance criteria

- A nil `resolver.ResolvedType` in a `Column`, in a `ResolvedList`
  element, and in a `ResolvedParameter` returns a wrapped
  `ErrOutOfC6Scope` naming the query and the position — not a panic.
  Three assembled-`Input` cases, one per site, each asserting the
  sentinel and the exact message.
- No `%s`/`String()` on a `ResolvedType` that has not been proven
  non-nil, at all five sites (`prepare.go:620`, `:626`, `:705`, `:879`,
  `:1050`).
- The posture on the eight pointer inhabitants is chosen and recorded:
  either they are normalised to their value forms before the switches
  run (and the existing `column-unknown-variant` /
  `list-elem-unknown-variant` §2 cases are re-pointed at the nil input,
  which then becomes what reaches those arms), or they stay refused and
  the §2 rows stand as written. Whichever is chosen, no row anywhere in
  the taxonomy argues that a `ResolvedType` switch is total because the
  interface is sealed.
- `docs/specs/codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md` §3's `param-type-invariant`
  and `column-type-invariant` rows drop their `(gqlc-edze)`
  parentheticals, since the nil panic they cite is gone. Their
  *conclusions* are unaffected — Phase A still shadows both — so the
  rows stay in §3.
- `TestSentinelTaxonomy`, `TestReachableBranchesAreReached` and
  `just test-codegen-fence` stay green, and every §2 case still names a
  distinct `prepare.go` line under mutation.

## Note on sequencing

This still lands after `gqlc-h4ug`. It edits the same `prepare.go` arms
and the same taxonomy rows, and it now also edits §2 cases `h4ug`
created.
MEASURED (2026-08-03, gqlc-h4ug round-6 review). Two facts that sharpen this bead's posture question.

1. All EIGHT typed-nil pointer forms fault, not only the nil interface. Go emits an explicit nil check for a value method reached through a nil pointer, so even the zero-sized (*resolver.ResolvedUnknown)(nil) panics: 'value method ...ResolvedUnknown.String called using nil *ResolvedUnknown pointer'. This closes, in the harsher direction, the open question of whether a typed nil panics or not depending on whether the method body dereferences. It always panics.

2. resolver.ResolvedList{Element: nil} also faults, at prepare.go:1050, with 'invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference'. That is a third carrier of the same defect beyond the five call sites this bead already names.

3. The premise is wider still: the marker seals ResolvedType against NOTHING. Go promotes an embedded type's unexported methods, so 'type embedNode struct{ resolver.ResolvedNode }' satisfies ResolvedType from any package and reaches prepare.go:620, :1050 and the parameter assertion cleanly, no panic. So the 'normalise pointer forms away at Prepare's boundary' option in this bead's description does NOT close the sum — an embedded form is neither a value form nor a pointer form. If the posture chosen is normalisation, it must be normalisation to the eight KNOWN value forms with an explicit refusal for everything else, not a pointer-to-value deref. See [[gqlc-856f]].
Round 3 (head 02f4161c): round 2's own justification for calling the witness list open was itself a false universal -- 'a struct embedding an embedder faults here too' -- carried in resolvedTypeName's doc comment, taxonomy §2:138, the test file's doc comment and the PR body. Measured with go test -overlay (nothing dropped in the tree): struct{ embeddedNode }{} ANSWERS 'node', because an embedder holding a variant by value gives the promoted String() a receiver to reach; the branch already witnesses that one level down as the value-embedder case. Corrected in all three gated carriers plus the PR body. The openness argument no longer rests on composition: faulting is a property of the String() a value dispatches, and ResolvedType is satisfiable by types codegen never sees. One measured composing shape that does fault is named instead -- (*embeddedNode)(nil), which declares no String() of its own. That qualifier is not decoration: (*T)(nil) where T embeds a variant by value AND declares its own pointer-receiver String() ANSWERS, measured, so the unqualified form would have repeated the defect a round later. Four witnessed shapes stands (nil interface, eight typed-nil pointer forms, nil embedded pointer, embedded ResolvedType); five resolvedTypeName call sites stands (grep -cE 'resolvedTypeName\(' = 6, five calls plus the declaration).

title: codegen/age: the offset-sidecar collision gate keys on the time.Time carrier, so admitting zoned TIME silently drops its coverage
description:
`rejectOffsetSidecarCollisions` (internal/codegen/age/errors.go) refuses
a schema that declares the property name the AGE backend derives for a
TIMESTAMP property's zone. It decides which properties derive a sidecar
by testing `f.GoType != goInstant`, i.e. by the Go carrier text
`time.Time`.

That test is right today only because TIMESTAMP is the sole admitted
width that derives a sidecar. The owner-approved encoding table on
gqlc-35yu.11 gives the same flat `<f>Offset` sidecar to an
offset-bearing TIME. TIME's carrier is not `time.Time` — it is
`dbtype.Time` on the neo4j targets, and whatever backend-invariant
temporal carrier eventually unblocks it here. So the day TIME is
admitted, the gate keeps compiling, keeps passing its own tests, and
silently stops covering the width that was just added. The schema that
declares both `startedAt :: TIME` and `startedAtOffset :: INT64` would
then generate a decoder that reads one key twice and re-zones the value
by the author's own property, which is the exact defect this gate was
built to refuse.

WHAT TO DO: key the gate on "this field derives a sidecar" rather than
on the carrier text. The cleanest spelling is a single predicate beside
`offsetProperty` that both the gate and `writeEntityFieldDecode`
consult, so a width that gains zoning gains collision-refusal in the
same edit and cannot gain one without the other.

The negative fixture
test/data/codegen/invalid/property_field_collision_offset_sidecar/ and
the `TestRejectsAnAuthorOwnedOffsetSidecar` sweep in
internal/codegen/age/age_test.go both pin the TIMESTAMP case and should
grow a row per zoned width as each is admitted.
notes: Round 2 (PR #848, head 45ae5930): the sweep's width walk was itself fail-open at 'const TypeFoo = PropertyType("FOO")' and 'var TypeFoo PropertyType = "FOO"' — this bead's own fail-open survived against either spelling. declaresAWidth now admits a PropertyType conversion and the walk reads var blocks; rows C/D kill by name. The sweep's carried figure is pinned by membership (require.ElementsMatch) rather than require.NotZero. Leave in_progress; close on merge — the coordinator holds the merge.

title: codegen/age: agtypeZone accepts any int64 as a UTC offset, so a foreign graph decodes into a fictional zone
description:
The emitted `agtypeZone` helper reads the `<f>Offset` sidecar with
`agtypeInt64` and hands whatever integer it finds straight to
`time.FixedZone("", int(offset))`. Any int64 is accepted. `1000000000`
seconds is a zone 31 years east of UTC, and the decoder returns it
without complaint; the caller gets a `time.Time` whose `Zone()` reports
a fictional offset and whose wall clock is decades off the instant it
was stored beside.

This is not a theoretical hole. The sidecar exists precisely because
gqlc does not write it — it is the interop affordance for a graph some
other tool populated (see the read-without-write note on gqlc-35yu.11).
So every value that ever reaches this helper comes from outside gqlc,
which is exactly the input a decoder should not trust. The one class of
malformed sidecar the helper does reject is a non-integer agtype, and
that rejection is incidental: it comes from `agtypeInt64`, not from any
decision about what an offset is.

The instant itself has the same shape of gap one level down —
`agtypeInstant` accepts any int64 micros, so a sidecar-free property
holding `9e18` decodes to a year in the 290-thousands rather than
failing — but that one is far less reachable, since gqlc does write the
instant.

WHAT TO DO: range-check the offset in the emitted helper and return an
error naming the property when it falls outside. The bound worth
picking is the one Go's own zone handling and ISO 8601 agree on:
strictly within +/- 24 hours, i.e. (-86400, 86400). Tightening further
to ISO 8601's actual range (-64800, 57600) is defensible but rules out
offsets no real zone uses, so it buys nothing and could refuse a graph
a future zone database would accept.

The test belongs in `internal/codegen/age/testdata/corpus_test.go.txt`,
beside `TestAgtypeZoneReadsAnOffsetInSeconds`, which already exercises
the malformed-agtype arm and runs the emitted helper for real rather
than reading its source.
notes:
Round 2 (PR #848, head 45ae5930): independent adversarial review returned REVISE on one blocker + 4 nits; all addressed. Blocker was in the round-1 B1 fix, not in this bead's bound. Bound itself measured clean both edges both directions by the reviewer. Leave in_progress; close on merge — the coordinator holds the merge.
CORRECTION (PR #848 round 3) to this bead's DESCRIPTION. Two claims in it are withdrawn; the defect, the bound and WHAT TO DO's first sentence all stand.

1. WITHDRAWN, false: 'The sidecar exists precisely because gqlc does not write it -- it is the interop affordance for a graph some other tool populated ... So every value that ever reaches this helper comes from outside gqlc.' gqlc derives no sidecar PARAMETER of its own, but the key is an ordinary property, and a query whose own text names it binds it through the emitted agtypeArgs. Measured with gqlc built at this branch head: a schema declaring (:Event {occurredAt :: TIMESTAMP}) beside (:Note {occurredAtOffset :: INT64}) generates rc=0, and in that ONE emitted package models.go:40 reads agtypeZone(props, "occurredAtOffset", value1) while queries.cypher.go:51 binds the same key through agtypeArgs -- both helpers declared in models.go. Across two packages on one label, one gqlc package writes the key and the other zone-reads it, which closes vertex identity. So a value reaching this helper may well be one a gqlc encoding produced. The bound is still correct, on the narrower ground that nothing here constrains the integer's origin -- not on the ground that the input is necessarily foreign.

2. WITHDRAWN, unsourced: 'Tightening further to ISO 8601's actual range (-64800, 57600) is defensible.' No source for that range was produced by the author or by two independent reviewers. The ranges implementations actually cite are +/-14:00 (XSD) and +/-18:00 (Java ZoneOffset), neither asymmetric. The shipped bound is (-86400, 86400) exclusive, which is what WHAT TO DO's first sentence already specified.

GH #735 mirrors this description; it was deliberately NOT hand-edited, so the correction lives here.

Still in_progress. Close on merge -- the coordinator holds the merge.

title: ci: shellcheck is not wired into CI, so the hooks' disable directives are comments
description:
`.githooks/bd-gh-sync:510` carries a load-bearing directive:

    # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # deliberate split
    bd github push $1

The unquoted expansion is **wanted** — the ids must become separate argv words —
and `gqlc-w4q9` added the id gate that makes it safe. Adversarial review
confirmed the split is load-bearing: quoting `$1` reddens the batching case and
the assertion "each bead id is its own argv word", which reports
`argv was: github|push|b-a1 b-a2|`.

So the directive documents a genuine, deliberate exception. But **nothing
enforces it**, because `shellcheck` is not installed on the development machine
and is not wired into CI. `just check-hooks` only verifies that `core.hooksPath`
points at `.githooks`; it does not lint anything.

The consequence is that every other SC-class defect in the hooks — the ones the
directive is carving an exception *out of* — is also unchecked. This repo has
already been bitten by three of exactly that class: a pipeline reporting only
its last command's status, `if cmd | tail -2; then` being unconditionally true,
and `${_l##*FAILED*}` matching both "contains" and "is empty".

A disable directive in a tree with no linter is a comment.

## Fix

Add `shellcheck` to CI over `.githooks/`. It must be a job that already exists
or, if a new one is genuinely needed, note that **GitHub derives required status
contexts from job ids** — adding a job means the branch-protection contexts need
updating in the same change, and renaming or splitting an existing job breaks
every open PR.

Folding it into the existing `lint` job is the lower-risk option and needs no
branch-protection change.

## Acceptance

Introduce a real SC2086 violation elsewhere in `.githooks/` and confirm CI goes
red naming the file and line. Then confirm the deliberate `disable` at `:510`
does **not** redden — that is the whole point of the directive, and a linter
that fails on the sanctioned exception is one nobody will keep.

Verify the violation currently passes CI first, so the gate is known to be
watching something.

Found during the adversarial review of `gqlc-w4q9`. Pre-existing repo
condition, not that branch's doing.

title: bd-gh-sync: the GH listing is a count over a set the script never witnessed
description:
`gqlc-w4q9` established the rule that **a count reaches the summary only if the
script enumerated the set behind it**, and applied it to both bead snapshots.
It was not applied to the GitHub listing.

`gh issue list --state open` answering a valid `[]` yields `stale=[]`, which
walks to `closed 0 of 0 stale GH mirror(s)` and exit 0 — a count over a set the
script never witnessed, which is the class the rule exists to close.

This is genuinely weaker than the bead case, which is why it was returned
non-blocking rather than promoted: an empty open-issue list is a legitimate
answer, so emptiness alone is not decidable as failure.

## But a witness exists

After a run that pushed **N > 0** new beads, `bd github push` has just minted N
open issues. An empty open listing in the same run is therefore a lost one, not
a true empty. That is a decision procedure for the case that matters, and it
costs one comparison.

## The same bead covers listing truncation

`--limit 500` and `--limit 1000` (both pre-existing on master) silently cut a
listing at the cap. A run that hits the cap produces `closed C of S stale` over
a **truncated** set — the identical defect, arriving by a different route, and
one that gets more likely as the repo grows. A listing that returns exactly the
cap is indistinguishable from one that was cut, unless the script asks.

## Fix

Two guards, one rule:
- If the run pushed N > 0 and the subsequent open listing is empty, the count is
  unwitnessed. Say so and do not exit 0 claiming success.
- If a listing returns exactly its `--limit`, treat it as truncated rather than
  complete — either paginate or refuse to count over it.

## Acceptance

Mutate the `gh` stub to return `[]` after a push of N > 0 and confirm the run
reports the unwitnessed count rather than `closed 0 of 0` at exit 0. Mutate it
to return exactly `--limit` records and confirm the run refuses to count.
Verify both currently pass silently first, so the tests are known to be watching
something.

Found during the adversarial review of `gqlc-w4q9`, returned non-blocking.

title: codegen/neo4j: the query-column path emits elem.(any), which is false for the null it exists to carry
description:
The neo4j emitter's **query-column** path emits `elem.(any)` when narrowing a
list whose element width is `ANY VALUE`. That assertion is false for exactly the
value the width exists to carry: `x.(any)` is **false when the interface value
is nil**. Demonstrated — `[]any{1, nil, "x"}` type-asserted element-wise to
`any` gives `ok=true, ok=false, ok=true`.

So a list containing a null decodes as a decode error rather than as a nil
element. AGE's `agtypeListOfAny` decodes the same value to `nil`, so the two
backends disagree at runtime on a value both are supposed to carry — which
`TestBackendInvariantSurface` cannot see, because it compares **declarations
only**.

## Reproduction

Add `RETURN b.bag, b.piles` to
`test/data/codegen/valid/schema_list_any_property/queries.cypher`. The emitted
`queries.cypher.go` contains `elem.(any)` and `elem4.(any)`.

## Why it is not caught today

No fixture routes an `ANY`-width list through a query column — the entity-property
path is covered, the query-column path is not. `gqlc-35yu.13`'s driver-carrier
census **does** catch this the moment a fixture reaches it, so the fix is a
fixture plus the narrowing correction, not new guard machinery.

## Fix

Narrow through the same driver-carrier rule the entity path uses: an `ANY`-width
element rides `[]any` and its elements need no assertion at all, because they are
already `any`. Emit the element directly rather than asserting it.

## Acceptance

Add the query columns above as a fixture. Verify the census names `elem.(any)`
as an offender **before** the fix, so the test is known to be watching
something, then fix the narrowing and confirm the emitted decoder returns a nil
element rather than an error for a list containing a null — asserted as a
**value** in `internal/codegen/neo4j/corpus_test.go`, which runs the emitted
bytes, not in a golden.

## Provenance

Pre-existing on master: `internal/codegen/neo4j/types.go` already recursed lists
and mapped `ANY VALUE` to `any`, and `internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go`
is untouched by `gqlc-35yu.13`.

Commit `eeab7ff` on that branch says this "is filed rather than baked into a
golden here". It was not filed — an adversarial review searched `bd list`, every
record in `.beads/issues.jsonl`, and everything created since 2026-08-02, and
found no such bead. This bead makes that claim true.
