title: codegen/age: decodeFunc's default arm decodes an unknown carrier as text, with no diagnostic
description:
`decodeFunc` (`internal/codegen/age/render_queries.go:547-559`) maps a carrier
type to the name of the `models.go` helper that decodes it. It names `bool`,
`int64` and `float64` explicitly and then has:

    default:
        return "agtypeString"

That `default` is a fail-open. It does not mean "everything else is a string";
it means "anything I was not taught about is a string". A carrier the AGE
backend gains later — a new numeric width, a byte slice, a composite — reaches
this arm and is silently decoded as text. There is no diagnostic, and the
emitted package still compiles, because `agtypeString` returns a `string` and
the field it is assigned to was typed from the same carrier table that
`decodeFunc` disagrees with. The failure surfaces at runtime, on real data, as
a wrong value or a decode error attributed to the wrong place.

Contrast `agtypeCarrier`, whose job is to *decide* the carrier. Here the
decision has already been made upstream, so `decodeFunc` is a total function
over a closed set — and a closed set is exactly the case where `default` should
be a refusal rather than a guess.

## Why this is not caught today

Every carrier currently reachable is one of the four named. So the `default`
arm is unreachable, which means no test exercises it and no test *can* fail
when it becomes reachable. This is the same shape as the other guards this
epic has been closing: green because it is looking at nothing.

## Fix

Make the switch exhaustive against the carrier set and refuse the unknown case
at generate time rather than emitting a guess — either a `codegen` sentinel
error returned up the emission path, or, if the emission path genuinely cannot
fail here, a panic naming the carrier, since an unnamed carrier at that point
is a generator bug and not a user error.

Then pin it: a test that adds a carrier to the carrier table and does not add
it to `decodeFunc` must go red. A test that merely asserts the four known
carriers map correctly does not close this — that is satisfiable by the table
it copies.

## Acceptance

Add a fifth carrier to whatever `agtypeCarrier` can return without touching
`decodeFunc`. Generation must fail, naming the carrier. Verify it does *not*
fail today first, so the test is known to be watching something.

Found during the adversarial review of `gqlc-35yu.13` and confirmed
pre-existing on master.

The real bound on the panic, now named: columnDecoder intercepts ColumnNode/ColumnEdge; the only column kind carrying a non-table text is ColumnEdgeUnion (prepare.go:855 interfaceName), stopped by edgeUnionReason ahead of Prepare for >=2 distinct labels and by phase A admitEdgeUnionCandidates (prepare.go:678) for what that arm stands aside for (<2 candidates -> ErrOutOfC6Scope; shared label -> ErrUnrepresentableEdgeUnion), both before phaseBDerive builds any Row. Temporal contributes no text at all (every arm ok=false -> ErrUnrepresentableTemporal in Prepare).

title: codegen: the edge-union sum type name is half author-chosen, so the emitted package scope is not closed
description:
Phase B builds an edge-union sum type as `interfaceName := q.Name + field`
where `field = rowFieldName(col.Name)` (internal/codegen/prepare.go, both
the ColumnEdgeUnion and the list-leaf arm). A query named ListActions
returning `r` therefore emits the package-level interface `ListActionsR`
and a marker method `isListActionsR`, and both halves of that name are
outside the generator's control: the method name comes from the query
file and the suffix comes from the author's RETURN clause.

That makes the emitted package's TOP-LEVEL scope not the closed
generator-owned set the method scope became on
fix/neo4j-param-name-capture. Two queries whose name-plus-column mangle
coincides collide:

    // name: ListActions
    MATCH (:Person)-[r]->(:Post) RETURN r
    // name: ListAction
    MATCH (:Person)-[sr]->(:Post) RETURN sr

both derive `ListActionsR`, so `gqlc generate` exits 0 and `go build`
reports "redeclared in this block". Not silent -- unlike the parameter
capture this is a compile error, which is why it was left out of that
branch -- but it is a generation that succeeds and produces a package
that cannot build, and the diagnostic names neither query.

Measured, not unmeasured. Two censuses on that branch bound it:

- internal/codegen/conformance/scope_test.go TestColumnNamesBindNothing
  holds all three targets to renaming every column moving no name the
  emission BINDS (arguments, receivers, results, body locals).
- internal/codegen/age/capture_test.go
  TestOnlyPackageLevelNamesFollowAColumnName holds the AGE corpus to the
  same thing, plus equality of what each method RESOLVES modulo the
  package-level declarations that moved. Its substitution is read off
  the two emissions' own declaration lists, so this residue is exactly
  the set of names it admits.

Closing it means either putting the sum-type name on the same collision
sweep the query-text const wants (see gqlc-dfcb's neighbourhood), or
making the suffix positional -- `<Method>Col0` -- which is a rename of a
generated PUBLIC type and so an API change with a golden-corpus-wide
diff. The census stays either way; only what it admits changes.
acceptance_criteria: Two queries whose `<Method> + rowFieldName(<column>)` mangle coincides either generate a compiling package or are refused at generate time with a message naming both queries and both columns; a fixture holds the colliding pair; and the guard goes red if the disambiguation is removed. The two censuses that bound the residue — TestColumnNamesBindNothing in internal/codegen/conformance/scope_test.go and TestOnlyPackageLevelNamesFollowAColumnName in internal/codegen/age/capture_test.go — stay, and the AGE one's declRenaming substitution narrows to admit nothing once the suffix stops being author-chosen.
notes: Promoted from a code comment by the adversarial review of gqlc-lhs3 (2026-08-03): both censuses carried a comment saying the residue 'is an API change and not this branch's', which is deferred work living only in a comment. Those comments now cite this bead.

title: spec: C1/C4/C5 still document the parameter-name-derived bare arg lhs3 removed
description:
The C1/C4/C5 specs still document the single-parameter signature as taking a
**parameter-name-derived** bare argument. That derivation is dead code, and the
name it derives is the capture vector `gqlc-lhs3` exists to close.

`docs/specs/codegen-stage-c1.md` §5.x `<param-list>` (lines 662-667) states the
rule in full: `paramFieldName(name)` → `MinAge` → lowercase → `minAge`. The
emitter does not do that. It emits `arg`, unconditionally, precisely so that no
author-chosen parameter name reaches the signature and captures a
generator-owned local.

So a reader implementing to spec reintroduces the vulnerability. This is not
cosmetic drift — it is a spec that documents the defect as the design.

## Sites

`docs/specs/codegen-stage-c1.md` — the authoritative section, per
`codegen-stage-c0.md:1112`, which routes "Method-signature naming rules (Params
vs bare arg…)" here:

- §3.1 line 243 — `func (q *Queries) PersonById(ctx context.Context, id int64)`;
  emitted is `arg int64`.
- §3.2 lines 273-275 — "single-parameter takes the bare typed arg". Shape right,
  name wrong.
- §5.x `<param-list>` lines 662-667 — the whole `<bareParam>` derivation rule.
  Dead.
- §5.x `<paramsMap>` line ~678 — "One parameter:
  `map[string]any{"<rawName>": <bareParam>}`". Emitted is `arg`. Note the map
  **key** is still the raw name and correctly so; only the value moved.
- §5.5 worked example lines 1203-1204 — `PersonName(ctx context.Context, id
  int64)` / `map[string]any{"id": id}`.
- §9 fixture table line 1152 — "single-param bare arg (`func (q *Queries)
  PersonName(ctx, id int64)`)".

`docs/specs/codegen-stage-c4.md` — lines 362, 403, 838. Line 838 is inside the
`WriteQuerier` **interface** member, so the drift is in a declared surface, not
only in prose: `RemovePerson(ctx context.Context, id int64) error`.

`docs/specs/codegen-stage-c5.md` — lines 438, 996: `PersonAction(ctx, id
int64)`, `GetAction(ctx, since int64)`.

## Separately, §4.6 is falsified

`codegen-stage-c1.md` §4.6 lines 513-529 — "Why `<methodName>QueryText` consts
do not participate in the sweep" — rests on the claim that "a duplicate at this
axis would already imply a duplicate method-name collision the exported sweep
catches first". `gqlc-igs4` is a worked counterexample: schema label
`FooQueryText` plus `// name: DecodeFoo` collides a generator-owned const with a
generator-owned func, no method name is duplicated, and the axis §4.6 defers to
never sees it. The corresponding code comments were corrected on `lhs3`'s
branch; the spec was not.

Fix §4.6 to state the hole, or to state the disambiguation once `gqlc-igs4`
lands. Do not restate `gqlc-igs4`'s argument here — cite it.

## Why this recurs

Nothing holds these specs against the emitter. Every `func (q *Queries) …`
signature in the specs is a claim about emitted bytes that the golden corpus
already contains, and no test compares them. Consider whether the worked
examples can be extracted and diffed against a golden, or a fixture named from
the spec section — and if that is not tractable, say so explicitly in the fix so
the next drift is expected rather than surprising.

Acceptance: no spec under `docs/specs/` shows a single-parameter query method
taking a parameter-name-derived argument; §4.6 states what is true about the
QueryText const namespace; and either a check exists that reddens when a spec
signature diverges from the emitted one, or the specs carry a note recording
that they are unfenced prose and why.

title: codegen/age: the Scalar type table has zero corpus reach
description:
AGE's `Scalar` type table has **zero** corpus reach. It is checked only by a
hand-written mirror of itself.

Reproduction (from `gqlc-9n6t`'s review): replace all six AGE `Scalar` arms in
`internal/codegen/age/types.go` with garbage — `MUT_bool`, `MUT_int64`, and so
on — and run

    go test -count=1 ./internal/codegen/conformance/ -update

**Zero goldens change.** `TestValid`, `TestDoubleRun`, `TestGoldenBuild` and
`TestBackendInvariantSurface` all stay green. The only test that fires is
`internal/codegen/age/types_test.go:TestTypeMapScalar`, which is a hand-written
copy of the table it is checking — so it asserts the table equals itself and
would move happily alongside any edit to it.

`ScalarBool`, `ScalarInt`, `ScalarFloat` and `ScalarString` are *served* by AGE,
so this is not a case of nothing being reachable. No valid fixture enrols an AGE
target on a query projecting a bare scalar **expression** column. Property
columns take a different path (`Property`, not `Scalar`) and are well covered,
which is why the gap is easy to miss.

This is another instance of the pattern this epic keeps turning up: a check that
is green because it is looking at nothing. It is pre-existing — `9n6t` neither
caused it nor worsened it — but `9n6t` added the claim that the type tables are
"total, and on a ground that can be checked", and on AGE the ground is not
checked end to end.

Fix: enrol at least one AGE-targeted valid fixture per served `Scalar` arm,
projecting a bare scalar expression column (e.g. `RETURN 1`, `RETURN 'x'`,
`RETURN 1.5`, `RETURN true`, or the same via a function call whose return type
resolves through `callProjectionType`). Then the golden diff is the check and
`TestTypeMapScalar` stops being the only thing standing between a wrong arm and
a green build.

Acceptance: mutating any served AGE `Scalar` arm reddens the conformance suite
through a golden diff, not only through `TestTypeMapScalar`; and the mutation
survives `-update` (regenerating must not make it green, because the emitted Go
must stop compiling or stop matching the invariant surface).

title: codegen/age: list expression columns still refused though .13 built the decode path
description:
`gqlc-35yu.13` taught the AGE backend to serve list-valued *properties*. It did
not lift the refusal on list-valued *expression* columns: `resolver.ResolvedList`
is still listed in `unservedColumn` for `apache-age-pgx-v5`.

That refusal was correct when AGE had no list decode path at all. It now has
one — agtype carries arrays natively, which is precisely why `.13` was
tractable — so the refusal outlives its reason.

The gap is visible as a backend asymmetry, which is the property this project
most cares about: a query returning `collect(p.name)` or a list literal generates
on the neo4j targets and is refused on AGE, so the Go surface a caller writes
against *does* vary by backend for that column kind. `TestBackendInvariantSurface`
does not catch it because the AGE side never generates at all.

Not folded into `.13` because `.13`'s scope was properties, and the expression
path reaches `ResolvedList` through `callProjectionType` rather than through a
schema property — different provenance, different width reasoning. Worth its own
bead precisely so the width argument gets made rather than assumed: a property's
element type comes from the schema and is therefore known, whereas a
`collect()`'s element type is inferred, and the inference may admit element types
the decode path cannot represent. The refusal may narrow rather than disappear.

Acceptance: a list *expression* column either generates on AGE with the same Go
surface the neo4j targets emit, or is refused for a reason that names the
element type it cannot represent rather than the column kind. Either way
`ResolvedList` stops being an unconditional entry in AGE's `unservedColumn`, and
a fixture pins whichever verdict lands.

title: codegen: a relationship type the schema does not declare is narrowed away without a diagnostic
description:
A query naming a relationship type the schema does not declare is accepted
silently. gqlc narrows the candidate set to the declared subset and leaves the
query text verbatim (ADR 0005), so the emitted code is well-typed over the
declared types while the *server* may return edges of the undeclared one.

Surfaced on `gqlc-35yu.14`, where this is exactly what makes the edge-union
dispatch's `default:` arm reachable — and there it is legitimate. It models
**schema drift**: the graph grows a relationship type ahead of the GQL schema,
and the sealed interface correctly has no member for it, so the row fails at
runtime with a clear error rather than decoding into the wrong arm.

The problem is that the same silence covers a **typo**. An author who writes
`ACTED_INN` gets no diagnostic at generate time — only a runtime failure on
rows that will never arrive, or worse, a query that quietly matches nothing.
Drift and typo are indistinguishable to gqlc today.

They are not indistinguishable in principle: drift means the query names a type
the schema lacks *and* the author expects rows of it; a typo means the same
shape with no such expectation. gqlc cannot read intent, but it can say what it
did — narrowing the candidate set is a decision the author should be told about.

Fix: emit a diagnostic (warning, not refusal — refusing would break the drift
case the `.14` fixture depends on) naming each relationship type in the query
that the schema does not declare, and stating that it was excluded from the
candidate set. Refusing is wrong here; silence is also wrong.

Acceptance: generating `edge_union_undeclared_relationship_type` still succeeds
and still reaches the `default:` arm live, but names the undeclared type on
stderr, and a test holds that message.

title: [bug] codegen/age: the capture guard parses only .cypher.go, so cross-file emitted names are unswept
description:
The AGE capture guard parses only `.cypher.go` — `emitQueryFiles` filters to that
suffix — so package-level declarations emitted into `db.go` and `models.go` are
never seen, even though the generated package is one Go package and a query
method's body can resolve them.

Demonstrated by the `gqlc-gjqo` reviewer at `8f80a46`: adding
`const gqlcDefaultGraph = "gqlc"` to `render_db.go` plus a reference to it from
the `.cypher.go` body emits a package that compiles (`just test-codegen-fence`:
0 issues) with **both** capture guards green at exit 0.

## Why this is not already covered

`capture_test.go:322` says capturing a cross-file name "is a hard failure of the
generated package rather than a silent one (gqlc-ni66)". That is true **today**
and **by accident**. The current cross-file package-level set is
`ErrNoRows`/`ErrMultipleResults` (typed `error`), `DBTX`/`Queries` (types), `New`
(func), and `maxGraphNameBytes` (untyped int, unreferenced from `.cypher.go`).
Every one is loud when shadowed by a `string` parameter because of how it
happens to be typed — not because anything prevents a future `string`-typed
cross-file declaration.

A `string`-typed one is exactly the silent case: it type-checks, and the caller's
runtime value silently becomes whatever the emitted body uses it for. That is the
same shape as the `<bare>QueryText` const, which is the worst instance of this
whole class and the reason it blocked `gqlc-35yu.10`.

**Not covered by [[gqlc-ni66]]**, despite the comment's pointer: ni66 is the
*loud* signature-binder class (`q`, `ctx`, receiver). It does not carry the silent
cross-file class. **Not covered by [[gqlc-3o3p]]** either, which is the
lift-the-sweep-to-neo4j axis.

## Why it was not fixed on gqlc-gjqo

gjqo is scoped to shape coverage *within* a backend's `.cypher.go` emission, and
it closed that. The reviewer notes a per-method free-identifier diff would detect
the cross-file class cheaply, but it would go red on findings belonging to other
beads, so folding it in would have coupled three separate fixes on one branch.

## Scope

Widen the guard's parse set beyond `.cypher.go` to the whole emitted package, so
the reachability check is over the package's real scope rather than one file's.
Expect it to go red on constructs owned by `gqlc-ni66`; sequence accordingly or
scope the new assertion to the silent (string-typed) subset.

Also: correct the `capture_test.go:322` comment, which currently asserts a
structural guarantee the code does not have. (A one-line wording fix is being
taken on the gjqo branch itself; this bead owns the actual detection.)

Acceptance: a `string`-typed package-level declaration emitted into `db.go` or
`models.go` and referenced from a `.cypher.go` method body is caught by the
capture guard, and the catch survives `go test ./internal/codegen/conformance/
-update`.

title: [bug] bd-gh-sync push path keeps the id-quoting hazard the pull path just closed
description:
The *pull* path in `.githooks/bd-gh-sync` was hardened on `gqlc-63y`'s branch:
ids are batched by hand rather than through `xargs`, refused by name when they
carry characters that would re-parse (quotes, spaces, leading dashes), and the
summary reports what was actually pulled rather than what failed to fail.

**The push path was left exactly as it was.** It still does the equivalent of
`bd github push $_ids` under `xargs`, so:

- an id containing a quote or a space re-parses and aborts the batch;
- an id with a leading dash arrives as a flag rather than a value;
- `|| true` swallows the non-zero, so the batch silently pushes nothing and the
  run still reports success.

That is the same defect class the pull path just closed, on the arm that
*mutates GitHub* rather than the one that reads it.

Why it was not folded into `gqlc-63y`: push has no summary contract to assert
against — the pull fixes are all anchored on "the summary must say what
happened", and push says nothing at all today. Closing this properly means
first deciding what push's success/failure contract is, which is a design
question rather than a hardening one, and it does not belong riding on a branch
that was already on its fourth round.

title: vuln: the ROOT module's in-package tests are still outside govulncheck's call graph
description:
`govulncheck` does not analyse the in-package test variant of a package. Anything
imported only by an in-package test drops out of the call-graph analysis with no
diagnostic and no non-zero exit.

`gqlc-rohp` established this mechanism, proved it with a single-variable A/B, and
closed it in the **nested** module (`test/data/codegen`) by converting the live
battery to `package fixtures_test` — 9 modules scanned became 54.

**The root module — the one that ships the compiler — still has it.** 34
in-package test files versus 16 external. Reproduced in this repo by the
adversarial reviewer: planting a `yaml.Unmarshal` call into
`internal/schema/gql/propertytype_test.go` (`package gql`) gives
`No vulnerabilities found`, exit 0; the identical call in a new file declaring
`package gql_test` gives exit 3 with a call trace.

Seven packages have testify/rapid/godog reachable **only** from in-package
tests — 23 files:

    internal/cli                  (3)
    internal/codegen              (2)
    internal/queryfile            (1)
    internal/resolver             (3)
    internal/schema/gql          (12)
    internal/schema/gql/annexd    (1)
    internal/schema/gql/isobnf    (1)

The subtlety that makes this worth a bead rather than a footnote: `-test` at
root **does** raise the scanned module count 31 → 42, so godog/testify/rapid
appear in the scanned set. That is what makes the gate look closed. But module
presence in the set is not what determines the exit code — call-tracing from
those 23 files is absent, so the root half can go green over a *called*
vulnerability.

Deliberately NOT done on `gqlc-rohp`: converting 34 files touches every package,
may require exporting internals purely to satisfy a scanner, and would be a
large diff riding on a CI-plumbing branch. `rohp` instead states the residual
plainly in the justfile comment and points here.

Scope: convert root in-package test files to external test packages, package by
package, so the root scan reaches the same call graph the nested one now does.
Where a test genuinely needs unexported access, say so and leave it — the goal
is to shrink the residual and know its size, not to reach zero by exporting
things that should stay private.

Acceptance: plant a called vulnerability reachable only from a root in-package
test and confirm `just vuln` exits non-zero. It does not today.
notes:
SEQUENCING RULING (2026-08-03, epic gqlc-35yu coordinator): held, not deferred indefinitely. This bead converts 34 root in-package test files across internal/cli, internal/codegen, internal/queryfile, internal/resolver, internal/schema/gql, internal/schema/gql/annexd and internal/schema/gql/isobnf. Five branches are in flight editing tests in internal/codegen, internal/codegen/age, internal/codegen/neo4j and internal/codegen/conformance right now (35yu.11, 35yu.14, 35yu.15, h4ug, the neo4j carrier follow-ups). A package-level test-package conversion rewrites the package clause of files those branches are actively adding to, so this is a genuine territory collision, not a conflict-risk excuse. Its siblings gqlc-nsq4, gqlc-pig9 and gqlc-k22l touch only justfile recipes, .github/workflows/vuln.yml and test/data/codegen/go.mod, so they are being staffed now instead. Take m5rc once the 35yu epic's last bead merges, when the codegen tree is quiet.

## Prose finding from the fix/vuln-gate-walk-and-fence review (PR #813, 2026-08-17)

justfile (master, ~line 692; unchanged by that branch) says of vuln-root-residual:

    "Third-party" is anything outside the main module whose first path element
    contains a dot, which is what puts a package in a vulnerability database at
    all; .TestImports is exactly the in-package test variant's import set.

The last clause is false as stated, measured against `go list`:

    go list -f '{{.TestImports}}' ./internal/resolver
      -> imports of the _test.go files only (19 paths)

    go list -test -f '{{.Imports}}' for `internal/resolver [internal/resolver.test]`
      -> a strict SUPERSET: the same 19 plus the package's own non-test imports
         (sort, strconv, ... )

`.TestImports` is the import set of the in-package TEST FILES, not of the test
VARIANT package. The variant's import set is the union of the package's own
imports and the test files'.

The CODE is right and the comment is wrong. The package's own non-test imports
are already inside govulncheck's closure via the non-test package, so counting
them in a "reachable only through the in-package variant" residual would inflate
it. `.TestImports` is the correct field for the metric; only the sentence
describing it needs the one-word repair ("the in-package test FILES' import
set").

Filed here rather than fixed on that branch because the line predates it and is
outside its diff.

title: codegen/neo4j: the decoder-local guard probes only STRING and FLOAT32, so a new emitter arm fails open
description:
`TestNoDecoderLocalTakesAPropertyName` (added by `gqlc-ak39`) is the best test
in that change: it emits a decoder, reads the local scope off the emission, and
asserts scope **equality** rather than scope disjointness. That shape is why it
could not be blessed away by `-update` — the adversarial reviewer reverted the
renderer and confirmed the test stayed red through a full golden regeneration.

But `decoderProbeSchema` only declares properties of two widths: STRING and
FLOAT32. The doc comment claims

  "a local a decoder gains later is held by this without anyone remembering to
  add it"

which is true only for locals reachable from those two types plus the
nullable/narrow arms. A future emitter arm for LIST, or a new temporal carrier,
that introduced (say) an `elem` local would never enter `declared` and would
never be probed. The guard would stay green while the class reopened.

This is the same failure mode as [[gqlc-gjqo]] on the AGE side — a guard that is
structural on one axis and enumerated on another, so it defends the shapes it
was written alongside and silently exempts the rest. Filing it separately
because it is a different guard in a different backend, but the two should
probably be fixed with the same idea.

Fix: widen `decoderProbeSchema` to one property per emitted `GoType`, so the
probe's coverage is derived from the type table rather than from whatever the
author happened to think of. Then the doc comment is true as written.

Acceptance: add a new emitter arm with a fresh local reachable only from a type
absent from the current probe schema, and confirm the guard goes red. Today it
does not.
notes:
Round-3 head is fa5dade344adeb08abb557206fa6c1eb65f6dd05 (was 428dfb84). Comment-only again: `git diff -U0 428dfb84..fa5dade` is 29 changed lines, 0 non-comment.

Blocker fixed: decoder_test.go:394 "one property per width the type table admits" -> "per SCALAR width". typeMap.Property recurses on Kind()==KindList so the type table admits a list at any depth, while decoderProbeWidths stops at two. Measured the gap first-party on disk in a detached worktree at 428dfb84 (md5-verified restores, `go test -c -o /dev/null` screen, anchored -run, 0 'no tests to run', 0 blank-named FAILs):
- ARM C (probe widened to depth 3, emitter clean) rc=0 -> the type table does admit depth-3 widths.
- ARM A (emitter binds a property-named local in writeSliceNarrow's recursive arm under `depth >= 1`, probe as shipped) rc=0, 0 FAILs; FULL REPO SUITE rc=0, 20 packages ok, 0 FAIL lines.
- ARM B (both) rc=1, 25 named FAILs / 23 leaf subtests under TestDecoderSuite/TestNoDecoderLocalTakesAPropertyName {acc0 acc1 elem0 elem1 elem2 err i0 i1 i2 narrowed nested0 nested1 node ok out rel s v v0 v1 v2 value0 value0s}, "a property name reached the decoder's scope". So ARM A's rc=0 is a real gap, not a dead mutation. render_models.go md5 c224e7d6 -> 31b6bceb, matching the round-2 reviewer's byte-for-byte.
Census backing the word "scalar": declared=31 constants, scalarWithCarrier=22, probeScalars=22, equal=TRUE, listWithCarrier=[TypeList], noCarrier=8, probeWidths=66=22x3.

Sweep for a fourth copy of the predicate: grepped both decoder_test.go and neo4j_test.go for every|each|all|any|"the type table"|admits|"per width"|carrier|backend|width|never|cannot|cover over comment lines, then targeted greps for "type table" / admit / "carrier for" / "per width". Four "the type table" sites in decoder_test.go (:40, :141, :149, :394) and ZERO in neo4j_test.go. Only :394 was the unqualified predicate; :40 already said "scalar", :141/:149 are round-2's fixed sentence and the explicit depth-limit disclosure. No fourth copy of that claim exists.

The sweep did find three OTHER claims the file's own code falsifies, all fixed here, two of them in the one function comment round 2's census did not cover:
- :93 "Every entity declares exactly one property" -> "No entity declares more than one property". Census: nodes {0 props: 1, 1 prop: 132}, edges {1 prop: 132}; the Endpoint node the edge arms attach to declares zero. Witness row: "node Endpoint declares 0 properties, not exactly one".
- :427 emitModels inherited the same "every entity" phrasing; now names the probe schema.
- :456 "the edge-union markers take no argument and hold no body" — out-of-tree AST probe: `func (X) isY() {}` gives Recv!=nil=true, Body==nil=FALSE, len(Body.List)=0, so the fn.Body==nil arm never sees them and fn.Recv!=nil is what excludes them.
N1 taken: :153 dropped "over that set" (direction A runs over all 66 probe widths, not the 23 in that set).
N4 declined, both sites, per the round-2 reviewer's own call: :70's contrast is mild and :212-215 is a sharp-edge warning worth keeping.

title: bd-gh-sync: a held bead deleted between snapshots is silent
description:
`.githooks/bd-gh-sync` takes two `bd list` snapshots around the pull and warns
when a bead that was held out of the pull changed anyway — the detector that
catches a concurrent writer (typically `bd hooks run post-merge` replaying JSONL
over newer DB state) clobbering state the sync deliberately protected.

At `:239` the comparison skips any `bid not in after`. So a held bead that is
**deleted** between the two snapshots produces no warning at all: it vanishes
silently, and the run reports as healthy.

Found in the round-3 adversarial review of `fix/bd-gh-sync-state-fidelity` at
`d25d947`. Ruled out of scope for that branch, which was already carrying two
blockers plus three promoted findings.

Deletion is the most destructive thing that can happen to a held bead, and it is
the one transition the detector is blind to. The skip is presumably there to
avoid false positives from beads legitimately absent from the second snapshot —
so the fix is not simply to drop the guard, but to distinguish "absent because
deleted" from "absent because it was never in scope", which means the detector
needs to reason about the set of ids it actually held rather than about the
snapshot intersection.

Note this interacts with [[bd-gh-sync-postcondition-blind]]: if the second
snapshot fails to load at all, every held bead is "not in after" and the whole
detector goes quiet. Fix that one first or this one's test will be built on
sand.

Acceptance: a test where a held bead is deleted between snapshots must produce
a warning on the last line. Verify by mutation that the test bites.
close_reason:
Closed by branch fix/bd-gh-sync-pull-witness at 0c13ddcb (not yet pushed). Commit c41b12fb 'a held bead deleted between the pull's snapshots is not silent', with 861fbf29 carrying the deleted bead's record tag through to the summary.

Adversarial review of the branch returned PASS; the deletion path is covered by the assertion census and by recorded mutants that all exit 1. See gqlc-nvjz for the full evidence list and gqlc-tvv7 for the residue.

title: codegen: the capture guard is shape-enumerated, so unswept shapes fail open
description:
gqlc-35yu.10's commit message describes its capture guard as "structural, not
enumerated" — i.e. it claims to catch any future generator-owned declaration
rather than a fixed list of known-bad names.

The adversarial review found the claim is half true. The *name* side is
structural (it sweeps whatever the emitter declared, it does not compare
against a list). The *shape* side is enumerated: the sweep only ever runs over
the three hand-built emission shapes in `emitParamBatch`. It never sees

  - `*Params` structs (multi-parameter methods)
  - `*Row` structs (multi-column projections)
  - entity returns
  - edge-union returns
  - temporal returns
  - list returns

Concretely: a capturable declaration emitted under a `len(p.RowFields) >= 2`
branch passes the guard green, because no swept shape has two row fields.

So the guard defends the shapes it was written alongside and silently exempts
every other one. That is the same failure mode this epic has hit repeatedly —
fixtures shaped so the bug cannot appear — just moved up a level from the
implementation to its guard.

Fix: drive the sweep from the codegen fixture corpus rather than from
hand-built shapes, so every shape the corpus already exercises is swept
automatically and new fixtures are covered on arrival with no test edit. If
that is impractical, the fallback is to enumerate the shapes explicitly AND add
a test that fails when a new shape is added to the emitter without being added
to the sweep list — an unenumerated shape must not fail open.

Acceptance: add a capturable declaration behind a `len(p.RowFields) >= 2`
branch in the emitter and confirm a test goes red. Today it does not.

Related: [[F2]] (the sweep is AGE-only) is the other axis of the same gap —
this bead is about shape coverage within a backend, F2 is about backend
coverage. Both should be settled before the guard is described as structural
anywhere.

Blocked on [[gqlc-35yu.10]] merging.
close_reason: Closed

title: codegen: the capture guard is AGE-only — neo4j emitters are unswept
description:
gqlc-35yu.10 introduced a structural guard —
`TestNoEmittedNameTakesAQueryParameterName` — which sweeps the emitted file for
generator-owned declarations that a query parameter could capture. It is a real
test: the reviewer added an unprotected package-level declaration to the
emitter without telling the test, and it failed on 3 subtests.

But **all of that machinery lives in `internal/codegen/age/age_test.go`**. The
neo4j backends have no equivalent, which is how [[F1's defect]] survived .10's
review green.

`TestBackendInvariantSurface`
(`internal/codegen/conformance/conformance_test.go`) cannot backstop this: its
`declaredSurface` helper skips non-TYPE `GenDecl` nodes
(`conformance_test.go:610-616`), so emitted consts and vars are not part of
"surface" as it defines them. The capture class is precisely about consts and
vars.

Two ways out, and the choice is part of the work:

1. Lift the sweep into a backend-agnostic helper (somewhere under
   `internal/codegen/` proper, not under `age/`) and run it from each backend's
   test package. Keeps per-backend fixtures, shares the analyser.
2. Extend `declaredSurface` to include CONST/VAR `GenDecl`s and let
   `TestBackendInvariantSurface` carry it. Cheaper, but changes what
   "surface" means for every other assertion that helper feeds, so it needs a
   careful read of the callers first.

Whichever is picked, the acceptance criterion is the same: an unprotected
generator-owned declaration added to the *neo4j* emitter must turn a test red.
Verify by mutation, not by reading.

Blocked on [[gqlc-35yu.10]] merging (the machinery to lift does not exist on
master until then).

title: codegen/neo4j: query body locals are capturable by a query parameter name
description:
Every neo4j query body declares locals with hard-coded literal names in
`internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go`: `records`, `out`, `err`, `record`,
`row`, `value`, `valuePtr`, `acc`, `isNil`, `ok`. A single-parameter query
method names its Go argument after the `$param` the query author wrote, so any
query binding one of those names lands a second declaration of it in the same
scope.

Found by the adversarial review of gqlc-35yu.10 at c476707. That bead added
`codegen.Unshadowed` and routed AGE's body locals through it (`bodyLocal`), so
the AGE arm is now safe. **The neo4j arms were not given the same treatment** —
there is no neo4j analogue of `bodyLocal`, and zero references to
`Unshadowed`/`ParamLocal`/`QueryTextConst` anywhere under
`internal/codegen/neo4j/`.

Reproduction shape (a fixture binding `$out` or `$err`) emits non-compiling Go
on BOTH neo4j-go-v5 and neo4j-go-v6:

    no new variables on left side of :=
    cannot use make([]string, 0, len(records)) (value of type []string) as string value

This is a loud compile failure, not the silent injection class — which is why
it was ruled non-blocking for .10 rather than reopening a passed review.

**Not covered by [[gqlc-ni66]]**: ni66 is scoped to the *signature* binders
(`q`, `ctx`) — names the method header declares. These are *body* locals, a
different scope and a different declaration site.

It also contradicts .10's own backend-invariance rationale: the same query text
now compiles on AGE and fails on neo4j, which is exactly the property
`TestBackendInvariantSurface` exists to defend.

Fix is small (~10 lines): route neo4j's body locals through
`codegen.Unshadowed`, the function .10 just introduced, the same way
`internal/codegen/age` does. `Unshadowed` returns the name unchanged when there
is no collision, so existing goldens should not move — a golden diff on this
change is a signal that something else is wrong.

TDD: red first. Add codegen fixtures binding `$out` and `$err` (at minimum) and
assert the neo4j goldens compile, before touching the renderer. A green run
against the current renderer means the fixture is not actually reaching the
declaration site.
notes:
SHARPENED BY THE gqlc-ak39 REVIEW (2026-08-02). The reviewer reproduced this end to end through the built CLI and the framing in the description undersells it on one axis and overstates it on another.

The collision site is writeMethodSignature (internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go:227) and paramsMapLiteral (:403), both spelling a single query parameter with codegen.LowerFirstRune(p.ParamFields[0].Field). So the capture happens in the METHOD SIGNATURE, not only in the body:

  func (q *Queries) ByCtx(ctx context.Context, ctx string) (N, error)    // ctx redeclared in this block
  func (q *Queries) ByQ(ctx context.Context, q string) (N, error)        // q shadows the receiver; q.db.run fails
  func (q *Queries) ByRecords(ctx context.Context, records string) (...) // records, err := q.db.run(...) type error

The first two belong to gqlc-ni66 (signature binders q and ctx). The third is this bead: the signature parameter collides with a BODY local. Same emitter, same line, two beads — coordinate rather than fixing half.

Also: the AGE arm has the signature half identically at internal/codegen/age/render_queries.go:126 and :263. gqlc-35yu.10 fixed AGE's body locals via codegen.Unshadowed but did NOT fix the signature, so ni66 is open on both backends, not just neo4j.
MANAGER RULING (2026-08-02): fixed jointly with gqlc-ni66 on branch fix/neo4j-param-name-capture, because the ak39 review established they are the same two emitter lines (writeMethodSignature and paramsMapLiteral).

The approach in this bead's description — routing generator-owned names through codegen.Unshadowed — is SUPERSEDED. Rejected because the surface a rename-on-collision scheme must cover is unbounded: ni66's notes show it includes fmt, every decode<Entity> helper, agtypeEntity/Span/Object/Property/NullableProperty. You cannot rename fmt without aliasing the import, and the decode<Entity> set varies with the user's schema. A reserved-name list is exactly the failure mode that produced this bug (AGE's set was raw/label/props/out/err and missed the carrier argument).

Instead: the emitted Go parameter name stops deriving from the query parameter name and becomes generator-owned, mirroring what gqlc-ak39 (375594e) did for decoder locals. No author-chosen identifier enters the emitted file's scope at all, so the class CLOSES rather than shrinking, and the guard can assert scope EQUALITY rather than disjointness — the assertion -update cannot bless away.

Cheap because: Go parameter names are not part of the call site (callers pass positionally); the multi-parameter form already binds a generator-owned name; and *Params/*Row fields keep deriving from the query parameter names, so the author-facing vocabulary survives where it is structurally uncapturable. Also closes the $_ case, where paramFieldName("_") returned "" and gofmt rejected the empty identifier with a misleading message.
ROUND-3 BLOCKER, derived by the epic manager 2026-08-03 after the reviewer was killed mid-probe by a quota limit.

The round-3 scope probe sweeps only the SINGLE-parameter signature arm. The multi-parameter arm is unreached, so the fence does not cover it.

Evidence. The killed reviewer left a compile-valid mutation in the worktree, on an axis distinct from round 2's. Round 2 mutated the single-param arm (textDerivedArg). This one mutates the multi-param arm, in BOTH emitters:

  internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go writeMethodSignature default: and paramsMapText
  internal/codegen/age/render_queries.go   writeMethodSignature default: and argsMapText

    func multiArg(p codegen.Query) string {
        if len(p.ParamFields) > 1 {
            return codegen.LowerFirstRune(p.ParamFields[0].Field)
        }
        return codegen.ParamArg
    }

replacing codegen.ParamArg at the ', %s %sParams' signature site and at the 'access = codegen.ParamArg + "." + f.Field' site. So the Params struct argument is named after the first parameter the query author wrote.

I ran it: go test -count=1 -run Scope ./internal/codegen/conformance/ => ok, 2.989s. The probe PASSES. The mutation also regenerated 28 golden files under -update, so the corpus blesses it too.

Root cause, and why it is the round-2 finding one level up: every query in the probe census carries at most ONE parameter. Confirmed by extracting parameter sigils from scope_test.go — $_, $records, $q, $param, $fmt, $err, $ctx, $agtypeArgs, each appearing once, none co-occurring. So the census never reaches writeMethodSignature's default: arm nor the len(p.ParamFields) > 1 branch in paramsMapText/argsMapText. Round 2's B1 was 'the census's axis is column shape, and the vulnerability lives on a shape the census does not build'. This is the same sentence with PARAMETER ARITY substituted for column shape.

Not a live vulnerability today: shipped code emits codegen.ParamArg unconditionally in the multi-param arm, and the Params argument is a struct type, so capturing the string-typed QueryText const would not type-check. The exposure is a body LOCAL — a two-parameter query whose first parameter is named elem, rel, raw, ok, acc, narrowed or decoded would shadow the emitted local under the mutation. The fence exists to stop that being reintroduced, and it would not.

Fix: the census must vary parameter ARITY and parameter NAME, not only column shape. At minimum one multi-parameter shape per decode arm whose first parameter is named after a generator-owned local, so the default: signature arm and both map-access branches are swept. Then re-run the multiArg mutation above and require it red.

The reviewer's mutation was left uncommitted when the agent died. I have recorded it here verbatim and restored the worktree to 8de415f, so nothing is lost.
close_reason: Merged in PR #742 (squash c6d0321..). The single-parameter Go argument is now generator-owned (arg), while the wire key stays the author's name. TestParameterNamesBindNothing closes every parameter index at once and reads no golden.

title: bd-gh-sync: trailing-block deletion is indistinguishable from a GH append without a timestamp
description:
The append-only eligibility rule (`gh_body.startswith(desc)`, landed on gqlc-63y) closes three of the four ways GitHub could be behind bd and still be pulled — re-indent, reorder, and de-dup all now HOLD. It cannot close the fourth, and no rule over the two bodies can:

  bd description: "line one"
  GH body:        "line one\nline two"

is byte-identical in shape whether GitHub APPENDED "line two" (the case --prefer-github exists to serve, pinned by the `b-ahead` fixture in .githooks/tests/bd-gh-sync-test.sh, which the suite requires to pull) or bd DELETED a trailing block. Two states cannot distinguish an addition on one side from a deletion on the other. That needs a third input — the classic two-way vs three-way merge problem.

RULING (manager, 2026-08-01): I ruled for append-only during the gqlc-63y refix; the implementer implemented it verbatim, then correctly pushed back that this row is undecidable under it, pinned the residual with a passing test (`trailing-block deletion is indistinguishable from a GH append (known)`) and a comment naming the collision, rather than asserting a HOLD that would have to be weakened later. That was the right call — I accepted the disagreement rather than forcing a fix that would have to lie. Filing it here instead of smuggling a design change into that branch.

FIX: add the third input. Both sides already carry one — `bd list --json` emits `updated_at` (confirmed present alongside created_at/started_at), and `gh issue list --json` can emit `updatedAt`. title: bd-gh-sync: --prefer-github write-back fidelity is unverified
description:
Two things could not be established during the bd-gh-sync review without mutating the real corpus, and both are load-bearing for the eligibility rule:

1. Does `bd github sync --pull-only --prefer-github` write the GH body back VERBATIM? If it normalizes at all (whitespace, line endings, markdown), every pulled bead becomes permanently not-in-sync and the corpus-rewrite failure mode reopens SELF-SUSTAININGLY — each run re-selects what the last run touched. Evidence against: 261/270 beads currently match byte-for-byte and have been through unscoped pulls. Suggestive, not proof.

2. Does --prefer-github clobber the fields the eligibility rule never compares — priority, issue_type, assignee, labels, design, acceptance_criteria, notes, parent? 46 beads carry acceptance_criteria, 75 carry notes, 10 carry design. For 261 beads desc == body exactly, so bd maps description<->body 1:1 and those fields have no GH counterpart to read back from — the reassuring reading, but an unverified one.

SAFETY: this MUST be answered in a scratch repo with a throwaway bd DB and a throwaway GH repo. Never against the real corpus. That constraint is why it was deferred rather than answered in review.

PROVENANCE: 'could not verify without violating the safety rules' section, bd-gh-sync adversarial review (2026-08-01).

title: codegen: no test holds allSentinels against what Prepare can actually return
description:
internal/codegen has no reachability fence for its sentinel set. Nothing asserts that a sentinel in allSentinels is still returned by any construct, and — after gqlc-h4ug — nothing audits the "deliberately unreachable" section of the taxonomy doc either.

Demonstrated during the gqlc-h4ug review. Three coordinated edits make a live sentinel disappear with the entire codegen tree still green:

  1. drop ErrUnrepresentableEdgeUnion from allSentinels
  2. move its §1 row in docs/specs/codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md to §3
     with the text "Silenced by fiat."
  3. delete its two invalid fixtures

  go test -count=1 ./internal/codegen/...
  ok internal/codegen | ok .../age | ok .../conformance | ok .../neo4j

while prepare.go:671 still returns that sentinel for
MATCH (x:Person)-[r:LIKES|WROTE]-(y:Post) RETURN r.

With the fixtures left in place the conformance sweep does object
(unknown sentinel name "codegen.ErrUnrepresentableEdgeUnion"), so this is
not a one-edit escape. It is still an escape.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD AND NOT PART OF gqlc-h4ug. h4ug fences drift between the doc and allSentinels: consistency. This is a different axis — whether allSentinels corresponds to anything the code still does. h4ug's fence is structurally incapable of seeing it, because every one of its three directions compares the document to the slice or the slice to the declarations, and all three agree with each other after the edits above. I ruled it out of that bead deliberately rather than let its scope grow; recording that here so the exclusion is not read as an oversight.

Note also that h4ug's §3 gives this gap a sanctioned, official-looking home it did not previously have. That is an argument for doing this bead reasonably soon after h4ug lands, not an argument against h4ug.

THE COUNTER-MEASURE ALREADY EXISTS IN THIS REPO, in another package. internal/schema/gql/sentinel_coverage_test.go declares TestAllSentinelsAreReachable, which runs the parser and reads errors off the wire, and its own rationale says why: a sentinel that stays in allSentinels while the construct it guards stops being reached silently passes TestSentinelReachability. internal/codegen has no equivalent. Read that test first and follow its shape rather than inventing one.

Scope note: the honest form of this drives Prepare (or Generate) with real inputs and collects which sentinels actually come back, then holds that set against allSentinels. That is more work than a static check and is the entire point — a static check is what the three edits above defeat.

Found by the adversarial review on gqlc-h4ug, filed as non-blocking there by manager ruling.

title: resolver: edge closure does not narrow plural endpoints it pins
description:
Under ADR 0022 a labelled node binding that several declared types satisfy binds
plural (nodeCands). Phase C then closes each touching edge over the endpoint
cross-product. When that closure commits a SINGLE EdgeKey, the key names one
node type on each end — so the pattern's endpoints are determined — but
closeEdge writes only edgeTypes/edgeKeys. The node bindings stay plural.

Reproduction (test/data/resolver/invalid/satisfy_plural_edges_reversed.gql
declares Person, Person&Employee, Company and exactly one WORKS_AT edge,
Employee&Person -> Company):

  MATCH (p:Person)-[r:WORKS_AT]-(c:Company) RETURN p
    -> ErrAmbiguousLabel: p is satisfied by more than one declared node type

  MATCH (p:Person)-[r:WORKS_AT]-(c:Company) RETURN p.employeeId
    -> ErrUnknownProperty: p.employeeId missing on plural-satisfying type Person

Both refusals are wrong on the facts: the only declared WORKS_AT edge has
Employee&Person on its source side, so p cannot be the bare Person type. The
first is pinned by invalid/plural_endpoint_whole_entity_after_edge_closure.cypher.

This is a precision gap, not a soundness one — the resolver refuses queries it
could accept and generates nothing wrong for the ones it takes. Widening is
non-breaking (ADR 0006), which is why gqlc-kph4 pinned the current answer
rather than changing it.

Shape of the fix: after Phase C commits, intersect each plural endpoint's
candidate set with the node types the committed candidates put on that
endpoint's side — the same per-edge contribution rule Phase B already applies
to unlabelled bindings (R3 spec 4.5.2), extended to labelled plural ones. Note
a binding can sit on both sides of an undirected candidate set, so the
contribution is a union across sides before the intersection across edges.
Re-running the pinned fixture must then flip it to accepted, and the fixture
moves from invalid/ to valid/.
notes:
2026-08-17 land run: PR #806 (https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/pull/806) opened at 40ce99a7 and squash auto-merge armed. lint, test, tidy, actionlint, live-smoke, codegen-fence all SUCCESS. govulncheck FAILURE, and it is NOT this diff: go.mod pins go 1.26.5 and the 2026-08-17 stdlib advisories (GO-2026-6089/6088/5942/5026 and the three called ones) are all fixed in 1.26.6, so every PR touching a .go file is red. That is gqlc-9322, whose fix commit ba46263f exists on local branch build/go-1266-toolchain and is unpushed. Once it lands on master, re-run the vuln job on PR 806 — the pull_request checkout uses the merge ref, so it picks up the bumped go.mod without a new commit on this branch — and auto-merge fires.

Final commit 40ce99a7 is comment-only: it retracts two prose claims that the six open follow-up beads falsify. The spec called the witness predicate's OPTIONAL arm §4.4.3's demotion gate 'spelled the same way'; DemoteNullability exempts an OPTIONAL edge in a proven group and this arm does not (gqlc-o8oc). readsLeftToRight's doc implied the right-to-left reading is irrelevant on a directed close; endpointContribution applies it regardless (gqlc-pv0u).

Re-verified first-party at 40ce99a7: both halves of the Phase B conjunction killed independently by named tests with go build green first — dropping the covering conjunct reddens TestAnInferredEndpointIsTrustedOnlyWhenItsOwnEndsWereEnumerated + TestInvalid; dropping witnessesItsEndpoints reddens that test plus TestPhaseBAsksTheWholeWitnessPredicateNotOneArmOfIt. No fake REDs.

title: codegen: a query parameter named q or ctx collides with the emitted signature itself
description:
Every backend emits query methods as `func (q *Queries) Name(ctx context.Context, <param> T)`. The single-parameter form names its Go argument after the query parameter the author wrote, so a query binding `$q` or `$ctx` puts that name into the same scope as the receiver or the context argument.

Reproduced against apache-age-pgx-v5 at b9feaa6 (manager probe, out of tree):

    // name: ByQ :one
    MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.name = $q RETURN p.name

emits

    func (q *Queries) ByQ(ctx context.Context, q string) (string, error)

and `go build` reports

    ./queries.cypher.go:187:44: q redeclared in this block
            ./queries.cypher.go:187:7: other declaration of q

This is LOUD — it is a build failure of the generated package, not the silent wrong-value class that gqlc-35yu.10 fixed with `bodyLocal`. That is why it was not promoted to blocking on that bead. It is still a defect: a legal query text makes gqlc emit a package that does not compile, with no diagnostic from gqlc itself, and the author has no way to know which parameter names are reserved.

It is not AGE-specific. Both neo4j targets emit the same receiver and the same `ctx` argument, so the collision is in the shared signature shape and should be fixed once, for all backends.

`bodyLocal` deliberately does not reach this: it keeps *body* locals clear of the signature, and here the collision is between two things the signature itself declares. Note the receiver name is NOT part of the exported surface — `func (qq *Queries) ByQ(ctx context.Context, q string)` has an identical declared surface — so renaming the receiver away from a colliding parameter is available without moving the backend-invariant signature. `ctx` is the harder half, because TestBackendInvariantSurface compares declared signatures and the parameter name may be part of what it holds; check that before choosing.

Two candidate shapes, both worth weighing:
  1. Rename the generator-owned identifiers out of the way (receiver, and ctx if the surface test permits), the same move gqlc-35yu.10 made for body locals. Keeps every query text legal.
  2. Reject the query at generation time with a clear error naming the reserved parameter. Cheaper, but tells an author their query is unwritable for a reason that is purely an artefact of Go codegen.

Prefer 1 if the surface test allows it; fall back to 2 only for the residue 1 cannot reach.

Whatever is chosen must be pinned by a test in the same property-based style as TestNoBodyLocalTakesAQueryParameterName in internal/codegen/age/age_test.go, which reads the names off an emission rather than listing them, and must cover all three backends rather than AGE alone.

Found by the manager's own probe during verification of gqlc-35yu.10, not by that bead's review.
notes:
BROADENED after the gqlc-35yu.10 review round 2, which mapped this class properly.

The bead as filed covered only $q and $ctx — collisions with the signature's own receiver and context argument. The real class is wider: a single-parameter method's argument can shadow ANY package-level identifier the emitted body REFERENCES, not just the two the signature declares.

Confirmed reachable, all emitting non-compiling Go at exit 0:

  $fmt              -> fmt.Errorf undefined (type string has no field or method Errorf)
  $ctx              -> ctx redeclared in this block
  $q                -> q redeclared in this block
  $agtypeArgs       -> cannot call agtypeArgs (variable of type string)
  $agtypeString     -> same
  $decode<Entity>   -> same
  $_                -> generation FAILS with a misleading error:
                       "format failure: querier.go: 8:32: missing parameter type"
                       because paramFieldName("_") returns "", so an empty
                       identifier is emitted and gofmt rejects it. The message
                       names gofmt and a column, and says nothing about the
                       parameter that caused it.

NOT in this bead, because gqlc-35yu.10 fixes it: the <bare>QueryText const. That one is silent rather than loud — it is string-typed and cypherStmt takes a string, so the shadow type-checks and the caller's runtime value becomes the statement text. That asymmetry is the whole reason it blocked .10 and these do not: every collision listed above is a compile failure of the generated package, which the author hits immediately.

$_ is worth separating from the rest. It is not a shadow at all — it is an empty identifier reaching gofmt — and it is the only one where GQLC ITSELF fails rather than emitting bad Go. It may want a different treatment (reject with a clear message naming the parameter) even if the shadows get renamed.

Scope note for whoever takes this: .10 establishes the pattern for the silent half, on both backends, including growing the emission test to walk REFERENCED identifiers rather than declared ones. Read that commit first — the closed-set test technique is the reusable part, and this bead should extend the same walk rather than enumerate a second list. A list is what let the QueryText const survive a fix aimed at exactly it.

Found by the adversarial review on gqlc-35yu.10; the $_ case and the specific error strings are from that review's mutation testing.
close_reason: Merged in PR #742. MidOfThree plan plus set-equality arm census closes the middle-of-parameter-list blind spot in TestEmittedScopeIsGeneratorOwned.

title: resolver: undirected edge closure under plural endpoints has no corpus coverage
description:
gqlc-35yu.9 made the candidate set an edge binding closes to a set (dedupe in
edgeProbes, internal/resolver/resolve.go). That changes behaviour on a path the
valid corpus never walks: an undirected edge binding whose endpoints are still
PLURAL when the edge closes.

The dedupe was justified and tested for the singular self-loop case (srcs and
tgts each one key, src == tgt, so the reversed orientation reproduces the
forward key). Under ADR 0022 plural endpoints there is a second way two probes
name one key: overlapping srcs/tgts produce (A,B) twice with A != B. The
postcondition still holds — the result is a set either way — but nothing in the
corpus exercises it. satisfy_singular.gql is the only plural-satisfaction
schema and it declares no edges, so no fixture reaches this combination at all.

Two things are unpinned:

1. The dedupe's effect on the R3 §4.6 candidate-count dispatch when endpoints
   are plural. §4.6 reads the count to decide singular / edgeUnion / ambiguous.
   Pre-.9 a duplicate inflated that count; post-.9 it does not. No fixture
   measures which verdict the path now reaches.

2. On that path, committing the edge type no longer narrows the endpoints, so
   the source and target bindings stay plural after edge closure. That is a
   newly reachable resolver state — the spurious ambiguity error used to mask
   it by refusing the query first. Whether downstream phases (Phase A
   admission, entity naming) are correct with plural endpoints surviving edge
   closure is untested.

Fix: add a plural-endpoint schema that declares edges (or extend
satisfy_singular.gql), and fixtures for the undirected × plural combination on
both sides of the §4.6 dispatch — one that should close singular, one that
should reach edgeUnion. Then confirm item 2 is either fine or a real defect.

Not blocking .9: the change is a strict improvement on the paths the corpus
does walk, and the mutation test (dropping the dedupe) fails five guards across
two packages. This is a gap in what holds it, not a known break.
notes:
=== kph4 findings and forks ===

MEASURED FIRST. New schema valid/schemas/satisfy_plural_edges.gql (Person,
Person&Employee, Company; one WORKS_AT from Employee&Person; FOUNDED from both
person types) plus invalid/schemas/satisfy_plural_edges_reversed.gql (same,
with REVIEWED declared Person->Company, Employee&Person->Company AND
Company->Person). Probed before deciding anything.

ITEM 1 — the count dispatch under plural endpoints.

  (p:Person)-[r:WORKS_AT]-(c:Company)   -> case B, ResolvedEdge (one candidate)
  (p:Person)-[r:FOUNDED]->(c:Company)   -> case D, edgeUnion of two candidates
  (p:Person)-[r:FOUNDED]-(c:Company)    -> ErrAmbiguousEdgeOrientation   <-- BUG

The third was a real defect, not a gap. Both candidates run Person-ish ->
Company; nothing about them is an orientation. The directed twin closes to the
byte-identical candidate set and case D types it, so the direction marker was
flipping accept/reject on a set it does not change, and the sentinel's own
advice ("write a directed arrow") named a fix that alters nothing.

FORK: what should case C's guard be?
  (a) leave it, fix only the message      — rejected: the accept/reject split
      between the directed and undirected twins survives, and it is arbitrary.
  (b) refuse the directed twin too        — rejected: contradicts ADR 0022.
      Plurality came from the label expression, and 0022 already ruled that
      satisfaction is satisfaction; the union is the honest reading. It also
      contradicts case D, which has emitted that union since R3.
  (c) case C fires only on a SWAPPED PAIR — taken. `swappedEndpoints` scans for
      two candidates {A,L,B} and {B,L,A}: the ones that disagree about which of
      the pattern's endpoints is the source. That is the fact the sentinel is
      named for, and it is what case C's rationale argues about ("does the
      pattern refer to authors reviewing books, or books reviewing authors?").
      Candidate count was only ever a proxy for it, exact while endpoints were
      singular.

The dedupe from .9 stays load-bearing under (c): an undirected self-loop's two
probes are one key AND a swapped pair with itself, so without the dedupe
undirected_self_loop_single_label still reaches case C. Verified by re-running
.9's mutation — same five guards across two packages still fail. Two further
mutations verified: reverting to count-only fails 3 guards; scanning only the
first candidate pair fails ambiguous_edge_orientation_plural_endpoints.

ITEM 2 — plural endpoints surviving edge closure. NOT a downstream defect.

Confirmed by running codegen.Prepare end-to-end on the plural schema. A plural
node binding cannot cross the resolver boundary at all: RETURN p and RETURN *
are refused (ErrAmbiguousLabel) and property projection intersects to a plain
ResolvedProperty, so Phase A sees nothing new on the node axis, and Phase Z is
schema-driven (it already demands an explicit Name for the multi-label type).
The edge axis does newly produce a union whose members share one label — Phase
A refuses exactly that with ErrUnrepresentableEdgeUnion and names the endpoint
constraint that fixes it; the distinct-label plural union generates fine. No
new codegen fixture: both land on code paths the codegen corpus already covers
(unrepresentable_edge_union_shared_label).

WHAT ITEM 2 DID TURN UP — filed as gqlc-0tft, deliberately not fixed here.
Closing WORKS_AT to its single key proves p is Employee&Person, but closeEdge
records only the edge tables; the endpoints are never narrowed. So RETURN p is
refused as ambiguous, and RETURN p.employeeId as unknown, on a binding the
schema pins. Precision loss, not unsoundness — the resolver refuses queries it
could accept and mistypes nothing. Widening is non-breaking (ADR 0006), so kph4
pins the current answer (invalid/plural_endpoint_whole_entity_after_edge_closure)
rather than changing it; gqlc-0tft flips that fixture when it lands.

CONTRADICTS THE BEAD: the bead frames item 1 as unmeasured and item 2 as the
suspect. It is the other way round — item 1 held the defect, item 2's downstream
is correct, and the gap item 2 exposed is one the bead does not mention.

SPEC: R3 4.4 (endpoint cross-product in the signature, loop and set-property
rationale — it still described singular endpoints and named only the self-loop
reason for the dedupe), 4.6 (verdict table, swapped-pair definition, two new
rationale blocks), 3.2, 3.5, 5.1, 2.2, 6.3.
HANDOFF 2026-08-01 (session quota halt). Adversarial review of 188b63f returned FAIL: swappedEndpoints tests an EXACT syntactic swap (a.Source==b.Target && a.Target==b.Source) but its own doc comment claims the broader semantic predicate 'candidates that disagree on which pattern endpoint is the source'. Under ADR 0022 plural satisfaction those differ, so a real orientation ambiguity is now ACCEPTED where the parent refused it. Counterexample: REVIEWED declared Author->Book and Book->Author&Editor; the undirected pattern is accepted, while its DIRECTED twin closes to ONE candidate — i.e. the commit deleted the refusal in exactly the case where its own prescribed remedy (write the arrow) works. RETURN r is backstopped two stages later by codegen ErrUnrepresentableEdgeUnion, but RETURN r.rating is caught by nothing and generates compiling Go.

Refix was IN PROGRESS when the session halted. Five UNTRACKED fixture files are on the branch and are correct — keep them:
  test/data/resolver/invalid/schemas/satisfy_plural_edges_reversed_subtype.gql
  test/data/resolver/invalid/ambiguous_edge_orientation_reversed_subtype.cypher
  test/data/resolver/invalid/ambiguous_edge_orientation_reversed_subtype_property.cypher
  test/data/resolver/valid/plural_endpoint_reversed_subtype_directed_closes_singular.cypher
  test/data/resolver/valid/schemas/satisfy_plural_edges_reversed_subtype.gql
internal/resolver/resolve.go was NOT yet modified. Remaining: replace the predicate (classify each candidate by which pattern endpoint set its Source came from; refuse when both classes non-empty; skip keys whose Source is in both sets — closeEdge already holds srcs,tgts), fix spec sections 3.5/4.6/5.1 which assert the syntactic and semantic definitions are the same thing, add require.Equal pinning the two identical union goldens (currently asserted by NOTHING and machine-written, so -update absorbs any divergence), fix the stale doc comment at internal/resolver/errors.go:67-72, make the predicate enforce its own KeyLabels precondition, and add one codegen conformance fixture pinning that this newly-admitted class dies at ErrUnrepresentableEdgeUnion.

Reviewer measured the replacement predicate keeps every accept this bead wanted (plural_endpoint_undirected_edge_union still passes) with one fixture message-string edit.
close_reason: Closed

title: codegen: an entity named Queries collides with type Queries in db.go — exit 0, non-compiling Go
description:
A schema declaring a node or edge type whose Phase Z entity name is "Queries" makes
codegen emit `type Queries struct` twice in one package: once in db.go (the handle
every backend emits) and once in models.go (the entity struct). `gqlc generate` exits
0 and the emitted package does not compile.

Found by Linus during review of gqlc-35yu.9. Reproduced on both apache-age-pgx-v5 and
neo4j-go-v5, and pre-existing on master bd29f01 for neo4j, so this is not introduced
by the AGE work.

Repro: NODE TYPE Queries (p :Person { ... }) -> db.go:31 and models.go:14 both declare
type Queries.

Same defect class as gqlc-ak39 (emitted identifiers colliding with identifiers the
template already holds), and same reason it was not fixed on the AGE branch: the fix
churns the neo4j goldens. There is an existing identifier-collision taxonomy —
test/data/codegen/invalid/identifier_collision_* — and this belongs in it.

Fix shape: extend the Phase B/Z identifier-collision sweep to reserve the names db.go
declares (Queries, and whatever else the handle template emits), with an invalid
fixture per reserved name. Consider doing this together with gqlc-ak39, since both are
"a user-chosen identifier lands in a scope the template already occupies" and a single
sweep covering emitted-template identifiers would close both classes at once.
close_reason: Closed

title: codegen/age: entity properties of LIST or ANY width refuse the whole schema
description:
gqlc-35yu.9 gave the AGE backend an entity surface, which made the schema's
whole property table reachable: codegen.Prepare's Phase Z builds an entity
struct for every node and edge type in the schema, and it fails on the first
property whose width the backend's TypeMap refuses.

age.typeMap.Property refuses LIST and ANY, because the emitted decode
vocabulary is one helper per agtype scalar and a field of either width would
have no helper to fill it. The consequence is wider than the field: a schema
declaring `tags :: LIST<STRING>` on any node type now fails AGE generation
with ErrUnrepresentableWidth even for a batch of pure scalar queries that
never touch it. Before .9 the same schema generated, because AGE emitted no
entity structs at all and only the query's own columns were checked.

test/data/codegen/valid/schema_list_property is the shape in question; it is
enrolled for neo4j-go-v5 only, where the field emits as *[]string.
acceptance_criteria:
- age.typeMap.Property admits LIST whose element width has a scalar carrier,
  at whatever nesting depth, and the emitted entity field is the same Go type
  the neo4j target emits for it.
- Emitted list decode is unit-tested against captured agtype list text in
  internal/codegen/age/testdata/corpus_test.go.txt, including a nested list, a
  narrow element width, and an element of the wrong agtype scalar.
- schema_list_property is enrolled for apache-age-pgx-v5 and passes the golden
  and compile gates.
- ANY is decided separately and explicitly: either an agtype-value decoder
