title: ci: the AGE arm's only gate is a nightly that can fail silently or stop firing
description:
gqlc-35yu.8 moved the Apache AGE live arm off the PR critical path: job
live-smoke-age in codegen-live.yml runs on schedule and workflow_dispatch
only. That trade was deliberate -- PRs are not charged for AGE containers --
and it is sound only while the nightly is actually a gate. Two things weaken
that.

No failure alerting. A red nightly notifies GitHub's default recipient, the
last committer to the cron file, and nothing else. Nobody owns it. An AGE
regression can sit on master indefinitely with every PR green, because no PR
runs the AGE arm.

Scheduled workflows stop firing. GitHub disables cron-triggered workflows
after 60 days with no repository activity. The gate would then be off with no
signal at all -- the failure mode is silence, not a red check.

There is a third, narrower hazard worth closing at the same time: a SKIPPED
check satisfies a required status context on GitHub. live-smoke-age is
correctly absent from master's required list today, but if it were ever added
it would be permanently green on every PR, because it skips on pull_request.
gqlc-35yu.8 leaves a comment on live-smoke recording that its job id is the
required context; the mirror-image warning belongs on live-smoke-age.

Options, roughly in order of cost: route nightly failure somewhere owned;
have a failed nightly open or reopen an issue so the signal is durable; add a
liveness assertion that the AGE job ran at all recently, so disablement is
itself detectable.

Found by Linus as NB3/NB5 in round-2 review of gqlc-35yu.8, alongside the
blocking branch-protection defect. Non-blocking for that bead -- the arm and
its wiring are correct; what is unowned is the signal they produce.

title: vuln: govulncheck never scans the codegen_live dependency tree
description:
`just vuln` runs `govulncheck ./...` untagged and against the ROOT module only. Two consequences, both meaning the live battery's dependencies have never been scanned:

1. Untagged: files behind //go:build codegen_live are outside the default build configuration, so govulncheck does not load them. gqlc-3eyw fixed exactly this blindness for golangci-lint and go vet by putting the tag in .golangci.yml — govulncheck reads neither that config nor the tag, so it is the one gate that inherited nothing from that change.

2. Root module only: the live battery lives in the NESTED module test/data/codegen, which has its own go.mod. The root go.mod has no require or replace on it, so `go list ./...` at root emits zero packages from that tree. Its dependency graph — testcontainers-go, the neo4j Go driver, docker/docker and their transitive trees — is invisible to the root scan by module boundary, independent of build tags.

That dependency set is large and network-facing. It is test-only and never ships in a user binary, which is why this is P2 and not P1, but it does run in CI with credentials in the environment.

FIX: extend the vuln recipe to cover both axes — the codegen_live tag and the nested module — mirroring how test-codegen-fence already reaches into test/data/codegen. Prove it the way gqlc-3eyw proved its claims: demonstrate the scan reports a known-vulnerable pin before trusting a green result.

PROVENANCE: raised as NIT 3 in the gqlc-3eyw adversarial review (2026-08-01), out of scope there. Verified by grep: no direct govulncheck invocation exists outside the just recipe.
notes:
Design forks resolved while fixing the scan (all conclusions measured, govulncheck v1.6.0, DB 2026-07-27):

1. The bead premise was incomplete. Adding -tags codegen_live and scanning the nested module is necessary but NOT sufficient. Measured: with the battery as package fixtures (in-package tests), `govulncheck -tags codegen_live -test ./...` in test/data/codegen scanned 9 modules — pgx, neo4j v5/v6, x/text, x/sync, pgpassfile, pgservicefile, puddle. testcontainers, moby/docker, otel and x/crypto were still absent. Cause: govulncheck keys loaded packages by import path, so the in-package test variant `p [p.test]` collides with plain `p` and loses; anything only that variant imports drops out of the scanned module set with no diagnostic. Isolated in a minimal module with a single-variable A/B (identical deps, identical flags, only `package v` vs `package v_test` changed): in-package reported nothing, external reported the vulnerability with a call trace.

2. Chose to convert the live battery to `package fixtures_test` rather than work around the scanner. Alternatives rejected: (a) -mode=binary on `go test -c -tags codegen_live` output — measured dead, `go version -m` shows a test binary embeds zero dep records, so binary mode saw 1 module and found nothing; (b) -scan module — measured worse, 7 modules, it is derived from loaded packages too, not from go.mod requires; (c) adding a tagged non-test file that imports testcontainers purely to widen the graph — a decoy with no other reason to exist. The conversion is free here: the nested module non-test files (include.go, contract_age.go) export nothing and the battery references none of them. Effect measured: 9 -> 54 modules scanned.

3. Positive control, as the bead asked. Pinned golang.org/x/crypto to v0.30.0 via replace (MVS floor from testcontainers-go v0.43.0 is v0.51.0, so a require edit cannot downgrade it; source mode honours replace, verified separately — -scan module does not). Before the conversion that pin produced ZERO findings. After, it produced 7 called vulnerabilities from 2 modules. The scan is now demonstrably capable of failing.

4. The scan was red on the real tree, not just hypothetically. Once the live tree became visible it reported 6 called vulnerabilities, exit 3: GO-2026-5970 (x/text v0.37.0, reached via pgx.Connect) plus GO-2026-5013/5017/5018/5019/5020 in x/crypto/ssh v0.51.0, all reached via testcontainers.GenericContainer. Only the x/text one was visible through the drivers; the other five needed the package conversion. Fixed by bumping the nested module to x/text v0.39.0 and x/crypto v0.52.0 (go mod tidy also moved x/sync v0.20.0 -> v0.21.0). Gate is now exit 0.

5. Added a guard to test-codegen-fence asserting no live file declares `package fixtures`. Reasoning: the fix silently depends on a source convention with no compiler or tool enforcement, and this bead exists precisely because a required gate was silently scanning nothing. Put it in the fence because that is the only always-run required job over the nested module — `just vuln` itself only runs on dependency changes, so a guard there would not fire on a PR that only changed the package clause.

6. Root module also got -test (previously godog, testify, rapid, gherkin, messages and go-memdb were unscanned: 32 -> 43 modules). Measured clean.

7. Residual, all uncalled so the gate is green by govulncheck design: GO-2026-5158 (otel v1.41.0, imported not called), GO-2026-5932 (x/crypto/openpgp, no fix available), GO-2026-5841 (klauspost/compress v1.18.5, required not imported). Not bumped — churn on indirect deps with no reachable exposure.

NO JOB IDS CHANGED. The govulncheck job id in .github/workflows/vuln.yml is untouched, no job added, renamed or split, so the required status contexts (lint, test, tidy, actionlint, govulncheck, live-smoke, codegen-fence) are all still produced. The workflow change is confined to the dependency-change detection paths, which now also diff test/data/codegen/go.mod and go.sum.
HANDOFF 2026-08-01. Branch fix/govulncheck-live-tree clean at 0475cdb. Adversarial review was dispatched and DIED ON SESSION QUOTA before returning a verdict — NO VERDICT EXISTS, do not merge. Re-dispatch.

Manager verification already done (do not redo): job ids are IDENTICAL between f1fd981 and the branch in BOTH .github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/workflows/vuln.yml, so no required branch-protection context was silently deleted — this was the highest-stakes check because GitHub derives a check context from the job id and a rename blocks every future PR repo-wide. Dependency bumps confirmed real in test/data/codegen/go.mod (x/crypto 0.51.0->0.52.0, x/sync 0.20.0->0.21.0, x/text 0.37.0->0.39.0), and 'just vuln' exits 0 on both modules.

Still UNREVIEWED and the highest-value attacks for the next reviewer: (a) does the live battery still actually RUN after the package clause changed to fixtures_test in live_age_session_test.go / live_age_test.go / live_neo4j_test.go / live_test.go — an external test package loses access to unexported identifiers, so it could compile-and-skip while still printing ok; always -count=1 since Go serves a cached ok in 0.2s without starting a container and a real run is ~18-25s; (b) reproduce the positive control independently (pin x/crypto low via replace, confirm the gate goes red, restore exactly); (c) can vuln.yml's widened change-detection still fail open — what changes the dependency graph WITHOUT touching the four listed go.mod/go.sum files; (d) does the new 'package fixtures' guard in test-codegen-fence actually fire, and is its file-matching narrow enough to be escaped by a live file in a subdirectory.
close_reason: Merged as PR #725. govulncheck now scans both modules under -tags codegen_live with -test; the nested battery converted to package fixtures_test to escape the x/vuln p [p.test] path collision (9 -> 54 modules). Six called vulnerabilities found and fixed (x/text v0.39.0, x/crypto v0.52.0). Two guards added: a fence assertion that no live file declares package fixtures, and a ratchet on the root module's residual blind set. vuln.yml's dependency probe no longer fails open. Both go directives bumped to 1.26.5 after the first real scan found 5 called stdlib vulnerabilities. ADR 0026.

title: codegen: TypeMap.Temporal has no rejection channel, so an unrepresentable temporal silently generates 'any'
description:
`internal/codegen/typemap.go:13` gives `Property` a rejection channel and denies one to `Temporal`:

    Property(pt graph.PropertyType) (goType string, ok bool)   // ok=false -> ErrUnrepresentableWidth
    Temporal(k resolver.Temporal) string                        // documented 'Total over the closed enum'
    Scalar(k resolver.Scalar) string                            // documented 'Total over the closed enum'

'Total over the closed enum' was true while neo4j was the only backend. AGE falsifies it: agtype carries no temporal scalar, so there is no faithful Go carrier for ANY temporal kind. Surfaced during gqlc-35yu.6.

## The failure mode is silent wrong code, not an error

With no way to say 'I cannot carry this', the AGE TypeMap returns `"any"` for every kind (`internal/codegen/age/types.go:84-86`). A query projecting a temporal expression against AGE therefore generates a column typed `any` that no decoder can fill — code that compiles, passes the fence, and is meaningless at runtime. Compare the `Property` path, which refuses at generate time with `ErrUnrepresentableWidth` naming the offending width. Same class of gap, opposite outcome, purely because of the missing bool.

Generate-time refusal is the established posture in this codebase for 'this backend cannot represent that'. Temporal expressions escape it by accident of interface shape, not by decision.

## Reachability

Unreachable at C0 (no query methods emitted), which is why gqlc-35yu.6 ships with the hole open and a comment acknowledging it. It becomes reachable as soon as query methods exist for AGE — gqlc-35yu.7 onward — and it is squarely load-bearing at gqlc-35yu.11, which decides the temporal encodings.

## Shape of the fix

Widen to `Temporal(k resolver.Temporal) (goType string, ok bool)` mirroring `Property`, route ok=false to a sentinel naming the kind (either reuse the unrepresentable family or add a sibling), update the neo4j TypeMap to return ok=true unconditionally, and let AGE return ok=false until the temporal arm commits an encoding. Mechanical apart from the sentinel choice.

Audit `Scalar` at the same time — it carries the identical 'Total' claim. AGE appears to cover the scalar enum today, so it may be genuinely total; confirm rather than assume, and if it is total, say WHY in the doc comment instead of restating the claim that just failed for Temporal.
acceptance_criteria: TypeMap.Temporal exposes a rejection channel; a temporal projection against a backend that cannot carry it fails at generate time with a sentinel naming the kind, proven by a negative fixture; no backend returns a placeholder Go type for a kind it cannot decode; the Scalar totality claim is either verified and justified in the doc comment or given the same treatment.
notes:
=== ADDITIONAL SCOPE (from gqlc-35yu.6 round 4, 2026-08-01): Temporal has no drift fence either. ===
internal/codegen/age/types.go declares:
    func (typeMap) Temporal(resolver.Temporal) string { return "any" }
It IGNORES ITS ARGUMENT. There is no switch, so the exhaustive linter has
nothing to hold: resolver can GAIN a Temporal kind and nothing in the age
package notices. Property and Scalar both switch and are exhaustive-linted, so
this is the one type-map entry with no growth coverage at all.

Folded here rather than filed separately because the fence and this bead's
rejection channel are the same edit: once Temporal can refuse a kind it has to
branch per kind, and the branch is what the linter holds.

Related: gqlc-fb4a adds domain-sweep fences (ElementsMatch against a canonical
enumeration) to the type-map tables in both backends, which is the SHRINK half
of the same problem. It deliberately leaves Temporal to this bead.

Reachability note: harmless while AGE emits no query methods. gqlc-35yu.7 is
where query methods first appear for AGE, and its notes already carry the
guardrail forbidding enrolment of any fixture with a temporal projection for
apache-age-pgx-v5 until this lands.
=== REACHABILITY CLAIM CORRECTED (manager, verified 2026-08-01 during .7 review) ===

The Reachability section says the silent-'any' hole "becomes reachable as soon
as query methods exist for AGE -- gqlc-35yu.7 onward". That is FALSE. .7 ships
query methods and the hole stays shut. Surfaced by the .7 reviewer; I verified
it in the .7 worktree rather than taking the report's word.

typeMap.Temporal has exactly two callers, prepare.go:752 and prepare.go:998,
both inside codegen.Prepare. For AGE, nothing reaches Prepare with a temporal
in it, because .6 reordered generate() so rejectUnservedQueries runs BEFORE
Prepare, and unservedColumn (age/errors.go:78) rejects on both channels:
  - resolver.ResolvedTemporal is named in the reject arm outright, alongside
    ResolvedList, so a temporal projection and a list of temporals both go.
  - a temporal-WIDTH property goes through scalarWidth (errors.go:131), which
    is `ty, ok := typeMap{}.Property(pt); return ok && ty != "any"` -- so a
    width the AGE Property table refuses OR types as "any" is rejected too.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD. The defect is real but it is LATENT, not live: no
query that reaches Prepare on the AGE path can carry a temporal, so no user can
currently generate the meaningless `any` column this bead describes. It becomes
live at gqlc-35yu.11, which lifts the rejection when it commits the temporal
encodings. Fix it BEFORE .11 lands the encodings, not urgently as a shipping
bug. The [BUG] type and the "silent wrong code" framing are both still accurate
about the interface shape; they overstate the current exposure.

The ADDITIONAL SCOPE note below is UNAFFECTED and is now the stronger half of
this bead: Temporal ignoring its argument means resolver can gain a kind and
the age package notices nothing. That drift gap is live today regardless of
whether the value is reachable, because it is about growth, not calls.

Also settled by the same review, so it is not re-opened here: .7 correctly
enrols NO temporal fixture for apache-age-pgx-v5, and the absence is fenced
rather than merely observed -- there are positive tests pinning both rejection
channels ("a temporal column is dropped" pinning `column "t" projects
temporal(date)`, and TestTypeMapPropertyRejectionReachesTheCaller pinning
ErrUnrepresentableWidth for TIMESTAMP). Those two tests are what will go red if
.11 lifts the rejection without widening the interface, so they are this bead's
tripwire. Do not delete them when widening -- change them deliberately.
IN-FLIGHT WORK PRESERVED (2026-08-02): worktree /home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc-9n6t-temporal, branch fix/typemap-temporal-rejection, base dc89506, UNCOMMITTED. Agent killed mid-task by a quota limit, not by a failure. Dirty set spans the rejection channel end to end: internal/codegen/{typemap,prepare,errors}.go plus both backends' types.go and the conformance test, plus a new untracked invalid fixture test/data/codegen/invalid/unrepresentable_temporal_date_column/. Do not discard; read the diff before resuming.

title: lint: build-tagged code (codegen_live) is outside every lint gate
description:
`.golangci.yml` sets no `build-tags`, so golangci-lint analyses only the default build configuration. Every file behind `//go:build codegen_live` — today `test/data/codegen/live_test.go` and `live_neo4j_test.go` — is invisible to `just lint` and to `just test-codegen-fence` (whose `go build ./...` / `go vet ./...` are also untagged).

Scope the damage accurately: COMPILE and behaviour coverage do exist, because `.github/workflows/codegen-live.yml` runs the real `just test-codegen-live` against docker on every PR. What is missing is LINT coverage specifically. So the failure mode is not broken code shipping — it is that the tagged files silently diverge from the standards the rest of the tree is held to, and nobody finds out.

Surfaced during gqlc-35yu.4. Running `golangci-lint run --build-tags codegen_live` in the nested module reports 10 issues against that bead's new seam: 8 x ireturn, 2 x thelper. (An earlier draft of this description said 8 issues / 6 ireturn; the measured inventory in the NOTES is authoritative and was confirmed a third time during review.) The pre-refactor baseline was coincidentally clean, so nothing regressed against a gate that was running — the gate was never running.

## Why this is not just 'set build-tags and fix them'

The two linters disagree with the code for opposite reasons and need opposite treatment:

- `ireturn` fires on the adapter constructors and per-fixture querier accessors. Returning an interface IS the seam that lets one scenario body serve N backends; that is the point of the bead, not an accident. Needs an allow-list entry, not a code change.
- `thelper` wants `t.Helper()` on the scenario bodies. Adding it would mark them as helpers and push require-failures up to the caller — destroying the failure-pointing that gqlc-35yu.4 carries as an explicit acceptance criterion, and that the pre-refactor file's inlined bodies existed to preserve. Satisfying this linter would make the suite worse. Needs suppression for scenario bodies.

So the resolution is a config decision with a rationale, not a mechanical cleanup, which is why it is its own bead rather than scope creep on .4.

## Growth

gqlc-35yu.8 adds the AGE live adapter arm behind the same tag. Every bead after it that touches live code widens the unlinted surface. Cheaper to settle the config before .8 than after.
acceptance_criteria: just lint (or an equivalent gate) analyses codegen_live-tagged files; the ireturn allow-list covers the adapter seam with a recorded reason; thelper does not fire on scenario bodies and the failure-pointing acceptance criterion of gqlc-35yu.4 still holds — proven by breaking an assertion and showing the failure points at the scenario's own line.
notes:
Schedule opportunistically alongside gqlc-35yu.7, i.e. after .4 merges and before .8 starts. Not a blocking edge on .8 (see the note there), but the cost grows once .8 lands more tagged code.
=== MEASURED INVENTORY (manager, 2026-08-01, on branch test/codegen-live-battery @ 23384c3) ===
Ran the tagged config by hand so whoever picks this up does not have to:
  cd test/data/codegen && golangci-lint run --build-tags codegen_live
  branch: 10 issues — ireturn 8, thelper 2
  master: 0 issues
So the entire delta is created by .4's seam, and it is two linters, not a
long tail. This is a small allow-list job, not a cleanup job.

ireturn (8) — every one is a seam accessor returning one of the package's own
interfaces: startNeo4jV5/startNeo4jV6 returning harness; (*neo4jV5).scenario
and (*neo4jV6).scenario returning backend; and the four
mixedReadWriteBatch()/manyColMany() accessors returning the querier
interfaces. These returns ARE the mechanism that lets one scenario body run
against N backends, and Linus separately confirmed the alternative (structs of
function fields) would dodge 6 of the 8 hits while destroying the compile-time
exhaustiveness the interfaces buy. So: allow-list, do not refactor.

thelper (2) — oneAndExec and manyWithParams, the scenario bodies. thelper wants
t.Helper() on both. DO NOT SATISFY THIS ONE. t.Helper() marks the frame as a
helper, which pushes every require-failure up to the battery loop and collapses
all scenario failures onto one line. .4 carries 'a failing assertion points at
the scenario, not the battery' as an ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, proven by deliberate
injection. Satisfying thelper would silently revoke a shipped guarantee.
Suppress it for this package.

Net shape of the fix: ireturn gets an allow-list; thelper gets suppressed with
a comment saying why. Both scoped to test/data/codegen, not global.
=== REVIEW OUTCOME + MANAGER VERIFICATION (2026-08-01) ===
Adversarial review: PASS, no blocking findings. Every load-bearing claim in the
commit message was tested by breaking it, from a pristine tree left
byte-identical to the reviewed commit.

The two checks that mattered most, because they are what a path-scoped
exclusion would have failed:
  - identically-NAMED type planted in the ROOT module still fires ireturn.
    The regex is anchored to the qualified name, so production cannot be
    weakened by a name collision.
  - reachable UNLISTED interface return planted inside live_test.go fires;
    a listed one is silent. The exemption is per type, not per file.

Also settled: no global side effects from run.build-tags. Four-way measurement
(root x nested, pre-change x shipped) run with --max-issues-per-linter=0
--max-same-issues=0, because the DEFAULT 50/3 TRUNCATION WOULD HAVE HIDDEN A
DELTA. All four zero. Zero //go:build !codegen_live files exist anywhere, so
the tag is strictly additive -- nothing dropped out of any analysis.

MANAGER VERIFICATION (did not take the review's word): worktree confirmed clean
of all review scratch (git status --porcelain empty, no probe files anywhere),
then re-ran every gate myself after go clean -testcache -- test, lint (0),
fence (0), actionlint all green, and the live suite FORCED with -count=1 gave a
real 18.077s two-arm container run with four scenario subtests. A cached `ok`
has already handed me one false PASS this epic, so an unforced live result is
not evidence.

NITS ACTIONED BEFORE THE PR EXISTED (commit amended, so no fixup noise):
  N1 .golangci.yml overclaimed `just fmt` as an entry point the tag affects.
     It is not: golangci-lint fmt is FILE-based, not package-load-based, and
     produced byte-identical diffs under both configs. It was never blind.
     Comment and commit message both corrected.
  N2 "the guarantee cannot be revoked quietly" was half true. nolintlint
     catches the ADDITIVE mistake (add t.Helper(), keep the directive). It
     does NOT catch the wholesale one: add t.Helper() AND delete the
     directive and every gate is green. Claim narrowed; the prose at
     live_test.go:81 is named as the remaining guard.
  N4 this bead's DESCRIPTION said 8 issues / 6 ireturn. Corrected to
     10 / 8 ireturn to agree with the measured inventory.

NIT DEFERRED, NOT DROPPED: N3 -> filed as gqlc-rohp. `just vuln` is the one
gate that inherited nothing from this bead -- govulncheck runs untagged AND
root-module-only, so the live battery's dependency tree (testcontainers, the
neo4j driver, docker/docker) has never been scanned by anything.

title: codegen/age: temporal encodings per spike table, gated on live round-trips
description:
Implement the spike-validated temporal encoding table in the AGE backend: param encode + decode helpers for TIMESTAMP/DATE/DURATION/zoned types (fallback table pending spike: timestamp=epoch-micros integer, date=ISO string, duration=ISO-8601 string, zoned=offset-preserving string). The Go surface stays identical to the neo4j target (time.Time etc.) — only the wire representation differs, owned entirely by emitted helpers. Any type the spike marked unfaithful becomes a generate-time first-offender error naming property, type, and backend, extending the existing unrepresentable-width taxonomy (invalid fixture per errored type).

Gates are live, not just golden: per encoding, a round-trip scenario (write via :exec, read back, require.Equal on the original value) AND an ordering probe (WHERE n.ts > param returns the correct subset) where the encoding claims ordering. Duration claims no ordering (not totally ordered even in neo4j) — its gate is component-faithful round-trip only.

Document the convention in the generated package doc header: encoded values are a gqlc convention; other tools reading the graph see the raw encoding.
acceptance_criteria: Temporal fixtures enrolled for AGE pass goldens; live round-trip + ordering scenarios green per encoding; unfaithful types have invalid fixtures proving the generate-time error; zoned round-trip preserves the offset (not normalized to UTC) with a test pinning it.
notes:
=== SPIKE gqlc-35yu.5 OUTCOME — THE ENCODING TABLE THIS BEAD IMPLEMENTS ===
Owner-approved 2026-07-31. Full ordering battery + captured output in
gqlc-35yu.5.

AGE has NO native temporal types (prior CONFIRMED empirically, not just from
the header enum). No temporal casts exist — the full pg_cast table is captured
in the spike. The only temporal function is timestamp(), which returns epoch-
MILLIS (note: millis, not micros — do not confuse it with the encoding below).

FINAL TABLE:
  timestamp/instant | epoch-MICROS int64                     | CONFIRMED
  date              | ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, zero-padded   | CONFIRMED
  duration          | total-MICROS int64                     | AMENDED
  zoned datetime    | TWO int64 props: <f> epoch-micros      | AMENDED
                    |   plus <f>Offset offset-seconds        |
  calendar duration | no faithful encoding — months/years    | generate-time
                    |   are not a fixed micro count          |   error

THE GATE IS ORDERING, NOT ROUND-TRIPPING. Both amended encodings round-tripped
fine and still failed; that is exactly why they were amended:
  - duration as ISO-8601 string sorted P1D, PT10H, PT1H, PT2H, PT90M, and
    WHERE v > 'PT2H' returned only PT90M (1.5h) — one false positive and two
    false negatives.
  - zoned as an offset-preserving string returned an 07:00Z row for
    WHERE v > '...08:00+00:00'.
  - zoned as a map {t,o} ALSO sorts wrong (jsonb key order) AND would force
    gqlc to rewrite user ORDER BY. The FLAT SIDECAR was chosen because it
    keeps the sort key as the property itself, so user ORDER BY passes through
    untouched. Preserve that property.
So every encoding here needs a live ORDER BY + range-predicate test, not just
an encode/decode round-trip test.

date stays a STRING by owner decision despite agtype string comparison using
DB COLLATION rather than byte order (readability in the stored graph wins;
ISO dates are fixed-width digits and hyphens). If a collation is ever found
where ISO dates misorder, that reopens this — worth one explicit test.

STILL OPEN, NOT COVERED BY THE SPIKE: time-of-day encoding. Resolve it in this
bead, using the same ordering battery.

The encoding table it was implementing is the owner-approved spike result and is SETTLED — do not relitigate it:
  timestamp / instant  -> epoch-MICROS int64            (CONFIRMED by live spike)
  date                 -> ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' zero-padded  (CONFIRMED)
  duration             -> total-MICROS int64            (AMENDED)

  time-of-day          -> STILL OPEN, to be resolved inside this bead

The gate is ORDERING, not round-tripping. Evidence from the spike: ISO-8601 duration strings sort P1D, PT10H, PT1H, PT2H, PT90M and 'WHERE v > PT2H' returns only PT90M. Offset-preserving zoned strings return an 07:00Z row for 'WHERE v > ...08:00+00:00'. The flat sidecar was chosen because it keeps the sort key as the property itself, so a user ORDER BY passes through untouched.

Resuming now. The successor is told to judge the inherited diff on its merits rather than assume it is correct.
=== TIME-OF-DAY DECIDED (the one open row) — 2026-08-03 ===
TIME / LOCAL TIME = microseconds since midnight, int64, in
[0, 86_400_000_000). Offset-bearing TIME normalises to UTC before
counting and carries its offset in the same flat <f>Offset sidecar
the zoned datetime uses; LOCAL TIME carries no sidecar.

Rationale, on the bead's own gate (ordering, not round-tripping): a
non-negative fixed-range integer is ordered by agtype's integer
comparison exactly as chronology within a day, so ORDER BY n.t and
WHERE n.t > $t are answered correctly with the author's text run
verbatim (ADR 0005) — same argument that carried ENC1 and the amended
duration encoding live, one width down. UTC-normalising is not
optional: an offset-preserving count makes two spellings of one moment
compare unequal, which is the exact defect that killed the
offset-preserving zoned-datetime string in this spike. The day-boundary
wrap a UTC normalisation can produce is a property of the width (a bare
time of day has no date to carry into), not of the encoding.

The table is now complete:
  timestamp/instant | epoch-MICROS int64                   | CONFIRMED
  date              | ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, zero-padded | CONFIRMED
  duration          | total-MICROS int64                   | AMENDED
  zoned datetime    | <f> epoch-micros + <f>Offset secs    | AMENDED
  time / local time | micros-since-midnight int64,         | DECIDED
                    |   UTC-normalised, + <f>Offset        |
  calendar duration | none — generate-time error           | PERMANENT

=== WHAT LANDED (81d2205 on feat/age-temporal-encodings) ===
Only TIMESTAMP is served. typeMap.Property admits graph.TypeTimestamp ->
time.Time; encode via agtypeMicros / agtypeNullableMicros, decode via
agtypeInstant, zone via agtypeZone reading the flat <f>Offset sidecar.

typeMap.Temporal still refuses ALL SIX kinds and that is deliberate. An
earlier working tree admitted TemporalDateTime; reverted. A temporal
*expression* column exists only because the query called a temporal
constructor, and AGE 1.7.0 has none (date/datetime/localdatetime/
duration/toTimestamp all "function does not exist"; one hit in 348
ag_catalog functions, age_timestamp, an epoch-MILLIS integer that is not
a temporal value). Admitting a kind emits a compiling method the server
rejects at run time — worse than the failure ADR 0025 built the channel
to prevent. No `default` arm in either Temporal switch, so `exhaustive`
with default-signifies-exhaustive: true remains the growth fence.

=== CARRIER, NOT ENCODING, IS WHAT BLOCKS THE OTHER FOUR ===
DATE, TIME, LOCAL TIME and DURATION have settled encodings (above) and
still refuse in Property, because every other backend spells them with a
neo4j driver type (dbtype.Date / dbtype.Time / dbtype.LocalTime /
dbtype.Duration) and a pgx package cannot declare one without making the
caller-facing surface vary by backend. TIMESTAMP is admitted precisely
because time.Time is what neo4j spells it with too. Unblocking the other
four is a backend-invariant temporal carrier, not more encoding work.

=== KNOWN GAP: THE OFFSET SIDECAR HAS NO WRITE PATH ===
agtypeZone is the read half only. gqlc binds the instant alone; writing
<f>Offset would need gqlc to inject a $<name>Offset parameter into the
author's CREATE/SET, which ADR 0005 forbids, and an auto-bound parameter
does not resolve anyway (confirmed: a non-property parameter fails C6
scope). A graph that wants its original zone back must name the sidecar
in its own query text. Documented in the emitted helper docs. Value
written through gqlc reads back at the same instant, in UTC.

=== LATENT NEO4J BUG FIXED IN PASSING ===
neo4j render_queries.zeroValueText routed a single-column :one over a
stored temporal property to `default: return "0"` — the ColumnTemporal
arm above it is the kind a temporal *expression* takes, and a projection
of a stored property is ColumnProperty. No fixture had run a :one over
one, so the emitted `return 0, err` had never had to compile. Both neo4j
targets affected; six carrier arms added.

=== MUTATION SWEEP: 18/18 ARMS KILLED BY GOLDEN DIFF ===
Every encoding arm mutated to a compile-valid wrong value, goldens
regenerated, diff confirmed, mutant reverted. Three arms initially
SURVIVED for want of corpus reach and two fixtures were added to close
them: timestamp_projection (entity with a single NON-nullable instant,
and queries that project instants while binding none) and
timestamp_nullable_param (a batch binding a nullable instant and nothing
else temporal). Both enrolled in all three targets.

=== LIVE TESTS ARE UNVERIFIED LOCALLY ===
timestamp_property_roundtrip has a codegen_live scenario across all
three arms: four instants under non-chronological ids (pre-epoch, the
epoch, one carrying micros, year 9999), asserting column and
whole-vertex round trip, nil for an unwritten nullable instant, an
ORDER BY that must disagree with insertion order, a strict > at the
epoch, and a comparison resolving to the microsecond. Docker was
inaccessible in the environment that wrote it; `go vet -tags
codegen_live ./...` is clean but the suite has NOT been run. Someone
with docker must run `just test-codegen-live-age` before this closes.
=== REVIEW ROUND 1 CLOSED — 2026-08-03 ===
Three blockers, all fixed on feat/age-temporal-encodings.

B1 THE BRANCH WAS RED IN CI. `just test-codegen-fence` failed at HEAD:
timestampRoundtripQuerier was missing from the ireturn allowlist in

B2 THE FLAT <f>Offset SIDECAR COULD COMMANDEER AN AUTHOR-OWNED PROPERTY
NAME. A schema declaring takenAt :: TIMESTAMP beside takenAtOffset ::

by the author's value; the STRING variant compiled but could never

B3 12 OF 26 MUTANTS SURVIVED. Every mutant that died, died on

title: codegen/age: write path — :exec methods and write-param coverage
description:
The :exec cardinality for AGE: CREATE/SET/DELETE query emission through the same server-side param mechanism, zero-column cypher() invocation shape (AGE still requires an AS projection clause — the spike corpus documents the zero/one-column form), and command execution over DBTX.Exec. Completes param-encoding coverage for every property type the scalar stage admits, on the write side.

TDD: red goldens first; the live battery's mixed read-write scenarios (write via :exec, re-read via :one/:many, delete, confirm ErrNoRows) enabled for the AGE arm — these already exist backend-invariantly from the live-refactor bead.
acceptance_criteria: Write-path fixtures enrolled for AGE pass golden + compile gates; mixed read-write live scenarios green on the AGE arm; :exec on a projection-shaped query still rejected by shared admission (existing invalid fixtures run under the AGE target).
notes:
MANAGER NOTE AT START (2026-08-01).

Branch feat/codegen-age-write-path, worktree gqlc-35yu10-write, cut from
cdd09ca (post-.9).

Correction to this bead's own description before anyone acts on it: it says
"the spike corpus documents the zero/one-column form". It does not. I read
gqlc-35yu.5 end to end — it captures the temporal encoding table with ordering
evidence, the param mechanism with server-log proof of server-side binding, and
the agtype result-text corpus for reads. Every cypher() invocation recorded
there projects at least one column from a RETURN. There is no CREATE, SET or
DELETE anywhere in it, and so no evidence for what the AS clause must look like
when the Cypher body returns nothing.

So the write invocation shape is NOT settled by prior work and must not be
assumed from the AGE docs alone. Establish it live against the pinned image
first (apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8... — PostgreSQL 18.1, AGE 1.7.0), record the
exact statement and observed output in this bead the way .5 did, and only then
emit against it. The specific things unproven: the column-definition list AGE
demands for a RETURN-less body, whether a write body may project columns at
all, and what pgconn.CommandTag carries back for a cypher() call (AGE's write
happens inside a set-returning function, so the tag is the SELECT's, not the
CREATE's — if RowsAffected is meaningless the emitted :exec must not pretend
otherwise).

Two drop reasons in internal/codegen/age/errors.go unservedReason() are what
this bead removes: "writes to the graph" (Validated.Statement ==
resolver.StatementWrite) and ":exec returns no rows to decode"
(CardinalityExec). They are separate axes and they come off separately — a
:many that writes and returns rows is a different shape from a :exec that
writes and returns none. Whichever this bead does not serve must keep its drop
reason and keep its invalid fixture.

STANDING CONSTRAINTS, unchanged: string interpolation of user args is banned
unconditionally — only the graph name may be interpolated, escaped and
length-checked; everything else binds. No AI attribution in any commit or PR.

LIVE EVIDENCE (2026-08-01), apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8... — AGE 1.7.0 on
PostgreSQL 18.1. Probes were scratch (psql scripts + two pgx v5 programs);
nothing shipped. The three unproven questions, answered.

(1) The column-definition list for a RETURN-less body must be EXACTLY ONE
ag_catalog.agtype column.

  no AS clause:
    SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher('writeprobe', $$ CREATE (:P {n:1}) $$);
    ERROR:  a column definition list is required for functions returning "record"
  AS () :
    ... $$) AS ();
    ERROR:  syntax error at or near ")"          -- zero columns is not expressible
  two agtype columns:
    ... $$) AS (v0 ag_catalog.agtype, v1 ag_catalog.agtype);
    ERROR:  column definition list for CREATE clause must contain a single
            agtype attribute  (SQLSTATE 42804)
    HINT:   ... cypher($ ... CREATE ... $) AS t(c agtype) ...
  one non-agtype column:  same 42804.
  one agtype column: OK, zero rows returned.

  The same 42804 (text unchanged, still saying "CREATE clause") is what a
  RETURN-less DELETE and a RETURN-less SET give for a two-column list. So the
  emitted shape is "v0 ag_catalog.agtype" whatever the write clause is.

(2) A write body MAY project, and then the list must match the RETURN arity
exactly; a mismatch either way is
    ERROR:  return row and column definition list do not match
  Verified for CREATE ... RETURN p / RETURN p.n, SET ... RETURN p / RETURN
  p.name, MERGE ... RETURN r, DETACH DELETE ... RETURN 1. The existing
  recordShape (one v<i> per RowField) was therefore already correct for
  write-with-projection; only the zero-RowFields case was new.

(3) pgconn.CommandTag is the enclosing SELECT's, not the write's. Measured
through pgx v5.10.0 Conn.Exec:

    CREATE 1 vertex,  bound params      -> "SELECT 0"  RowsAffected=0
    CREATE 3 vertices in one statement  -> "SELECT 0"  RowsAffected=0
    DELETE 2 vertices                   -> "SELECT 0"  RowsAffected=0
    SET on 2 vertices                   -> "SELECT 0"  RowsAffected=0
    DELETE matching nothing             -> "SELECT 0"  RowsAffected=0
    CREATE (p:P {n:5}) RETURN p.n       -> "SELECT 1"  RowsAffected=1
    MATCH (p:P) RETURN p.n  (3 rows)    -> "SELECT 3"  RowsAffected=3

  RowsAffected is the projected row count and nothing else. It cannot tell
  "created three vertices" from "matched nothing". DECISION: the emitted :exec
  returns error alone and discards the tag. Justified twice over — the
  measurement above, and TestBackendInvariantSurface, since the neo4j targets
  emit Method(ctx, ...) error for :exec. A RowsAffected in the AGE signature
  would have broken the surface invariant AND lied.

OTHER LIVE FINDINGS

- All four non-interpolating pgx QueryExecModes (CacheStatement,
  CacheDescribe, DescribeExec, Exec) work on writes. SimpleProtocol — the one
  interpolating mode — fails closed on the write path:
    ERROR:  third argument of cypher function must be a parameter (SQLSTATE 22023)
  Note for the next reader: a QueryExecMode must be passed as the FIRST query
  argument to pgx, not the last; passing it last gives a misleading
  "mismatched param and argument count" (pgx v5 conn.go:41).
- An injection payload bound as a write value is stored as data. Payload
  {"name": "a$gqlc$, $1) AS (v0 ag_catalog.agtype); DROP TABLE canary; --"}
  round-tripped intact and the canary table survived.
- A pgx Query of a RETURN-less write whose rows are never drained still applies
  the write.
- An inline property map matched against a JSON-null parameter matches nothing;
  AGE drops null properties at write time, so no stored vertex carries one.
- MERGE (p:Person {id:9})-[r:AUTHORED|LIKES]->(q:Person {id:10}) RETURN r
    ERROR:  syntax error at or near "|"
  Independently confirms gqlc-35yu.14: AGE 1.7.0 has no relationship-type
  alternation. edge_union_write_projection is still enrolled for AGE (its
  sibling edge-union READ fixtures already are, and the golden/compile gates
  hold the emission); .14 remains the open P1 for the missing live coverage.

CORRECTION TO THE MANAGER NOTE ABOVE. The claim "There is no CREATE, SET or
DELETE anywhere in it" about the gqlc-35yu.5 spike is false. Section C9 of that
spike says verbatim: "Write without RETURN -> ZERO ROWS, but the AS(...) list
still needs exactly one agtype column, e.g. AS (v ag_catalog.agtype)." The
corpus-graph setup in Q3 is a RETURN-less CREATE ... $) AS (v agtype); C8(c)
holds CREATE (n:NullProp {a:1, b:null}) RETURN n and MATCH (n:NullProp) SET
n.a = null RETURN n; C10 holds a RETURN-less CREATE (x:A:B {n:1}). The spike's
C9 answer agrees exactly with what was re-measured here. The manager was right
about the second half though: the probe evidence for the projection question
and for CommandTag genuinely was absent, and CommandTag is the one that changed
a design decision, so the live work was necessary regardless.

DESIGN FORKS TAKEN

- :exec returns error, tag discarded. See (3).
- One statement composition path for reads and writes (writeStatement), so the
  graph name stays the only interpolated thing and it stays inside the escaped,
  length-checked cypherStmt. Writes bind through $1 exactly as reads do.
- write_exec_temporal_param deliberately NOT enrolled for AGE: the type table
  has no TIMESTAMP carrier, so it stays with gqlc-35yu.11.
- Two unit tests had used "a write" as their stand-in for an unserved query
  (TestUnservedQueriesOutrankUnrepresentableWidths in the age package, plus the
  CLI-surface tests TestRunApacheAgeRejectionIsASentinel and
  TestGenerateApacheAgeRejectsQueriesItCannotServe). Writes are served now, so
  each moved to a list-projecting query, which is the narrowest axis AGE still
  refuses. The CLI ones needed a schema of their own: a LIST on the shared
  fixtureSchema would fail the AGE arm of the driver-vocabulary sweep on the
  width sweep instead.

GATES: just test / just lint / just test-codegen-fence / just actionlint /
just test-codegen-live all green. The AGE arm now runs
mixed_read_write_batch: exec + re-read live (arms table flipped writes: true,
which TestLiveSmoke asserts against the harness type, so the arm cannot
silently drop the write scenarios).

MANAGER CORRECTION (2026-08-01), same day, before review.

I have re-read it at gqlc-35yu.5 lines 751-752 and confirmed. C8(c) and C10

before writing the claim into a bead where it would be read as established.

What survives from the note, and what the implementer confirmed was genuinely
unproven and worth the live work:

  - Whether a write body may PROJECT columns. It may; the AS list then matches
    the RETURN arity exactly. C9 covers only the RETURN-less case.
  - What pgconn.CommandTag carries. It is the enclosing SELECT's, not the
    write's: CREATE of 3 vertices, DELETE of 2, and a DELETE matching nothing
    all report "SELECT 0". RowsAffected is the projected-row count and nothing
    else. This changed a design decision — the emitted :exec returns error
    alone and discards the tag, which is also what keeps its signature
    identical to the neo4j targets.

So the probing was worth doing on its own merits, and the corrected lesson is
about how I established the premise, not about whether to measure.

MANAGER FINDING, PRE-REVIEW (2026-08-01). BLOCKING. Reproduced myself before
ruling; not taken from anyone's report.

The AGE query body declares locals named stmt, args, rows and err. A query
with exactly ONE parameter emits that parameter under a name taken from the
query text — writeMethodSignature's `case 1:` arm emits
codegen.LowerFirstRune(p.ParamFields[0].Field). The two namespaces are the
same block, so a parameter the author happens to name $stmt collides with the
composed statement.

Reproduced with a two-file fixture, one query, no other content:

    MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.name = $stmt RETURN p.name

emits, for apache-age-pgx-v5:

    func (q *Queries) PersonByStmt(ctx context.Context, stmt string) (string, error) {
        stmt, err := q.cypherStmt("$gqlc$", personByStmtQueryText, "v0 ag_catalog.agtype")
        ...
        args, err := agtypeArgs(map[string]any{"stmt": stmt})
        ...
        rows, err := q.db.Query(ctx, stmt, args)

The caller's argument is overwritten by the composed SQL on the line after it
arrives, and the SQL text is then bound as the value of $stmt. The caller's
value is never read. PersonByStmt(ctx, "Alice") searches for a Person whose
name is the entire generated SQL statement.

THIS COMPILES. `go test ./internal/codegen/conformance/ -update` reports ok,
the golden is written, the compile gate passes, every one of the five gates is
green. There is no error at generate time and none at run time — the query
simply returns the wrong answer forever.

Typed differently it is only a compile error: the same query written against an
INT64 property gives "cannot use q.cypherStmt(...) (value of type string) as
int64 value in assignment". So the failure mode is decided by the property's
width, and the silent one is the STRING case, which is the common one.

NOT a general codegen defect. neo4j-go-v5 emits, for the identical fixture:

collides. This is AGE's alone, because AGE's body opens by declaring the
composed statement.

The property held: no identifier the emitted body declares may be one the
caller's query text could have chosen.

Scheme. paramLocal(p) returns the single identifier in an emitted method's
signature that the query text chose -- LowerFirstRune(ParamFields[0].Field) for
the one-parameter form, and "" otherwise, because the two-or-more form passes a
Params struct under this package's own name and the zero-parameter form
contributes nothing. bodyLocal(p, name) appends "_" while name equals that.
Every local the query bodies declare now goes through it: stmt, args, rows, out,
err, decoded, narrowed, and the positional raw%d / value%d / label%d.

Why it cannot collide. The loop's exit condition is the non-collision property
itself, so the scheme does not depend on guessing which names a query text can
produce -- $value0 and $raw0 are both producible and both are in the fixture.
It terminates on the first pass, since a signature contributes at most one
query-chosen identifier, but the loop is what makes the result unconditionally
clear rather than clear by that argument. The mangled names cannot collide with
each other either: each family is disjoint and nothing emits a literal trailing
underscore.

backend-invariant surface and neo4j emits the same one; the fix is entirely on

So the caller's runtime string becomes the statement text. Fixed on BOTH backends per the scope ruling: neo4j had the identical hole
at render_queries.go 179/332/380 (:exec and the read path are two
separate reference sites there, one each). Verified by regenerating the

Test, and this is the part that mattered. The old declaredIdents
collected only AssignStmt/ValueSpec/RangeStmt binders, so bodyLocalsOf
was structurally blind to a shadowed package-level name and the test

set is now every identifier the emitted file mentions, walked off the
syntax tree -- 45 of them, including the three QueryText consts, none
enumerated by hand.

The verdict is structural rather than a name comparison:
requireNothingDeclaredIsCaptured asserts that every package-level name
the emitted file declares is a free identifier of some method. Capture
has exactly one signature -- the declaration stays, the body still spells
the name, and the name now resolves to the parameter, leaving the
declaration referenced by nobody. Asserting reachability never has to
know what the emitter chose to call anything, which is what makes the set
closed rather than enumerated: a package-level name added later is held
by the same assertion.

Out-of-scope names stay out without special-casing. fmt, agtypeArgs,
agtypeString and decode<Entity> arrive from an import or another file of
the package, so they are not package-level declarations OF THIS FILE and
the assertion does not fire on them; capturing one is a compile failure
of the generated package anyway. ctx and q are signature binders, so they
never enter the free set. That is gqlc-ni66's territory, and the
asymmetry is real: the query-text const is the only silent one, because
it is string-typed and lands where a string is expected.

title: codegen/age: entity columns — vertex/edge agtype decode into entity structs
description:
Entity-typed columns for the AGE backend: decode agtype vertex/edge composite text (id/label/properties per the spike corpus, including the ::vertex / ::edge suffixes) into the SAME entity structs phase Z names for every backend — the Go surface is backend-invariant; only the decode source differs. Covers node-entity and edge-entity columns and the edge-union scope at parity with the neo4j impl (whatever the shared admission in phase A admits for the target). Emitted decode helpers live in models.go beside the scalar ones.

TDD: red goldens per enrolled fixture first; live entity-read scenarios added to the shared battery (they run on the neo4j arms too — battery stays backend-invariant).

notes:
MANAGER RULING ON FORK B (the LIST/ANY refusal), verified empirically before
ruling.

The implementer disclosed this himself as "a real regression and it is
structural". He was right that the behaviour changed, and right to say so
loudly. I reproduced it in both directions rather than take it on report.

Method: enrolled test/data/codegen/valid/schema_list_property for
apache-age-pgx-v5 and reduced its query batch to a single scalar read
(RETURN e.id), so the LIST property is declared in the schema and touched by

  master bd29f01                -> ok, generation SUCCEEDS
  branch feat/...entity-columns -> FAIL, "unrepresentable property width:
                                   entity \"Event\" property \"tags\" has
                                   LIST<STRING>"

So it is real and user-reachable: the AGE driver is offerable from `gqlc init`,

RULED NOT A DEVIATION, and not blocking on the design. gqlc-35yu.11's own
description specifies this exact shape for this exact class:

  "Any type the spike marked unfaithful becomes a generate-time first-offender
   error naming property, type, and backend, extending the existing
   unrepresentable-width taxonomy (invalid fixture per errored type)."

A schema-wide first-offender error naming property and type IS the epic's
declared taxonomy. What master did was not a better behaviour, it was silence:
AGE emitted no entity surface at all, so the schema's property table was never
consulted. .9 makes it reachable, and reachable means the taxonomy applies.

BLOCKING ON COVERAGE, however. As shipped the change is invisible: no fixture
exercises it, schema_list_property is neo4j-only, so nothing in CI states the
new behaviour, nothing would catch a later change to it, and gqlc-35yu.13's

the same breath as the rule -- "invalid fixture per errored type". Required for

backend as well as the property and type, which the current message does not.

gqlc-35yu.13 stays open but is re-scoped: it is not that the refusal is wrong,
it is that its blast radius is the whole schema rather than the queries that
reach the property. A future implementer must not read .13 as licence to make
unrepresentable widths generate silently again.

RULED AGAINST LINUS ON WHERE TO FIX. He proposed an AGE-local gate in
internal/codegen/age/errors.go on the grounds that it churns zero neo4j goldens. I
verified that claim is true, and that a SHARED gate also churns zero goldens — master's
suite is green and TestGoldenBuild compiles every golden, so no existing valid fixture
has duplicate-label candidates. Given equal churn, the shared fix is strictly better:
neither backend can represent this. An AGE edge and a neo4j relationship both carry one
label/type plus properties and endpoint ids, never endpoint labels, so two edge types
sharing a label are indistinguishable from the column value alone on both. An AGE-local
gate would knowingly leave neo4j emitting non-compiling Go while this bead claims to
have established a backend-invariant surface.

DISTINGUISHED FROM gqlc-ak39. ak39 was deferred because fixing it rewrites ~77 neo4j
goldens on an AGE-owned branch. This one rewrites none. The deferral rationale does not
transfer.

Also blocking, from Linus's non-blocking list, because AGENTS.md binds on both:
- the wiredEntity doc comment claims "Only wireEntity builds one, so an entity the wire
  has no form for cannot reach an emission". That is a package-internal convention, not

- TestBackendInvariantSurface skips receiver-less functions on the unchecked premise

Accepted as non-blocking: the AGE live arm runs 4 scenarios to neo4j's 5
(mixed_read_write_batch is the write path, which is bead .10).

Manager follow-ups from this round, filed separately: an entity named Queries collides
with type Queries in db.go on every backend (pre-existing, cross-backend); narrow-width

(edge-union dispatch has no live coverage) is raised in priority — this defect is direct

LINUS ROUND 4: VERDICT FAIL. He conceded the placement ruling and closed blocking item
2, then found that the round-4 gate OVER-REFUSES. Reproduced by me, and the root cause
is deeper than he diagnosed.

DEFECT: an undirected edge pattern whose endpoints share a label makes the resolver
append the SAME schema.EdgeKey twice, because edgeCandidates (internal/resolver/
resolve.go:477) tries both orientations and for src==tgt both orientations are one key.
The round-4 gate reads that repeat as two indistinguishable candidates and refuses.

My repro, schema with two self-loop edge types under DISTINCT labels:
    DIRECTED EDGE TYPE Likes (:Person) -[:LIKES]-> (:Person),
    DIRECTED EDGE TYPE Wrote (:Person) -[:WROTE]-> (:Person)
    MATCH (x:Person)-[r:LIKES|WROTE]-(y:Person) RETURN r

  branch 95dd0b2, apache-age-pgx-v5 -> REFUSED: "candidates Likes and Likes both carry
      edge label \"LIKES\"". The message names one entity twice and prescribes a remedy
      that cannot be followed: both endpoints are already pinned to :Person.
  master bd29f01, neo4j-go-v5 -> 4 cases emitted, LIKES twice and WROTE twice,
      non-compiling.
  master bd29f01, apache-age-pgx-v5 -> refused as out of scope.

That last line is what makes it blocking rather than pre-existing. On AGE this branch is
what introduces edge-union support, and an undirected self-loop union is mainstream. A
capability that refuses it does not meet this bead's acceptance criterion.

LINUS'S PROPOSED FIX SITE IS WRONG, AND I RULE AGAINST IT. He said to dedupe in
closeEdge and NOT in edgeCandidates, because R3 spec 4.6 case C detects the single-label
undirected self-loop off the pre-dedupe length. He read the verdict table and not the
rationale under it. docs/specs/resolver-stage-r3.md, case C rationale, says verbatim:

  "Person -> FOLLOWS -> Person where the reciprocal ... is also declared: the same key,
   so there is no ambiguity. The genuine double-match case requires distinct
   source/target label sets in the two directions."

The pre-dedupe length IS the bug. The implementation contradicts its own spec, and I
confirmed that on master with a single self-loop edge type:

    DIRECTED EDGE TYPE Likes (:Person) -[:LIKES]-> (:Person)
    MATCH (x:Person)-[r:LIKES]-(y:Person) RETURN r
  master bd29f01 -> ambiguous edge orientation: edge "r" matches both
      Person-[LIKES]->Person, Person-[LIKES]->Person

One key listed twice, from a query the spec says is unambiguous. So deduping in
edgeCandidates is the spec-correct fix and closes three things at once: this spec
violation, the duplicate-case non-compiling emission on neo4j, and the branch's new
over-refusal.

I verified the dedupe does not weaken genuine case C. Both resolver fixtures pinning
ErrAmbiguousEdgeOrientation (test/data/resolver/invalid/ambiguous_edge_orientation*.cypher)
use Person/Post, so the two orientations are two DISTINCT keys, the set stays at size 2
after dedupe, and case C still fires.

SCOPE RULING: in scope and blocking. The branch caused the over-refusal, so it fixes it;
you do not ship a regression you introduced and file a bead for it. The correct fix
happens to be ~10 lines in the resolver and also closes a documented spec violation.

Also blocking: the valid corpus contains ZERO undirected multi-label edge patterns. That
blind spot is why round 3's duplicate-case defect and round 4's over-refusal both reached
review, and it is why golden churn kept measuring zero. A valid fixture for the
undirected self-loop union is required.
MANAGER VERIFICATION OF ROUND 5 (cc9d21e), independent.

The over-refusal is fixed at the root. edgeProbes now dedupes by whole schema.EdgeKey
(membership-only map, never iterated, first-occurrence order); edgeCandidates is that
set filtered by s.Edges; describeTriedEdges reuses edgeProbes rather than rebuilding
the enumeration, so the two can no longer drift. Carmack found a third instance of the
duplication in describeTriedEdges that neither Linus nor I had spotted, and fixed it in
the same seam.

Verified by me:
- My exact repro is now a valid fixture (edge_union_undirected_self_loop, verbatim
  schema and query) and emits a clean two-case switch — LIKES then WROTE, once each —
  under BOTH apache-age-pgx-v5 and neo4j-go-v5.
- Zero existing goldens modified. git diff --name-status 95dd0b2 cc9d21e shows every
  golden path as an addition; the only modified non-source file is
  test/data/resolver/valid/schema.mapping.json, which registers the new fixtures.
- unrepresentable_edge_union_shared_label and its _list companion are still red for the
  right reason (LikesFwd and LikesRev are distinct keys, so the dedupe leaves both and
  the round-4 gate still fires).
- Both ambiguous_edge_orientation fixtures still fail with ErrAmbiguousEdgeOrientation.
- Mutation test, mine: deleting the dedupe fails FIVE independent guards across two
  packages — TestEdgeFailMessagesListEachTriedKeyOnce, TestEdgeUnionKeysAreASet, both
  new resolver valid fixtures, and TestConformanceSuite. The fix is braced.
- Gates on cc9d21e: just test PASS, just lint PASS (0 issues), just test-codegen-fence
  PASS (0 issues), just actionlint PASS.

SPEC EDIT ACCEPTED. I had told him not to edit the spec if the spec was right and the
code wrong. He found that a DIFFERENT passage was itself wrong and said so with the
quote rather than complying quietly, which is what I asked for. R3 section 4.4 claimed
"Duplicate EdgeKeys are impossible by construction — the same (label, orientation) pair
generates the same key exactly once". The postcondition is right and the proof is false:
it counts probes, not the keys they name, and (S,T) and (T,S) are two probes but one key
when S == T. He corrected the false lemma, kept the postcondition, left section 4.6 case
C's rationale untouched, and documented the two new fixtures in the coverage sketch.
That is the correct scope.

ROUND 6: REVIEWER VERDICT PASS at cc9d21e. Merged as PR #670, closing #624.

Review took six rounds (three FAILs). What the FAILs found is worth recording,
because two of the three were not AGE defects at all — the AGE work was the
first thing to walk paths that were already broken.

Round 1 FAIL, decoder-local shadowing. A schema property named err/label/out/
props/raw emitted a redeclaration and `generate` still exited 0, because the
format gate only parses. Fixed structurally: every local an emitted decoder
declares is positional. I verified it by deleting the golden and regenerating
byte-identical, then building an 11-hostile-name fixture the implementer had
not seen. The same defect exists on neo4j (I reproduced it on master bd29f01,
6 compile errors) — deferred as gqlc-ak39, since fixing it churns ~77 neo4j
goldens on an AGE-owned branch.

Round 3 FAIL, duplicate-label edge union emitting a duplicate switch case. I
ruled against the reviewer on placement: he wanted it AGE-local, I put it in
the shared admission phase. Neither backend can represent it — an edge value
carries its label and its properties, never its endpoint types — and churn is
zero either way. Reproduction detail worth keeping: the ANONYMOUS edge form was
already refused by Phase Z; only the named DIRECTED EDGE TYPE form got through.

Round 4 FAIL, the gate I ordered OVER-REFUSED. Two self-loop edge types under
DISTINCT labels, queried undirected, were refused as sharing a label — naming
one entity twice and prescribing an unfollowable remedy. The reviewer proposed
a fix site and I found it backwards: he said do not dedupe the enumeration
because R3 §4.6 detects ambiguity off the pre-dedupe length. But §4.6's own
rationale (case C) says the same key in both orientations is unambiguous, so
the pre-dedupe length IS the bug and §4.4's lemma asserting duplicates are
impossible was simply false. Confirmed independently on master: a single
self-loop edge type already gave `ambiguous edge orientation: edge "r" matches
both Person-[LIKES]->Person, Person-[LIKES]->Person`. Fixed by deduping in the
enumeration; §4.4's lemma corrected rather than worked around.

The implementer then found a third instance himself — describeTriedEdges
rebuilt the same enumeration for ErrUnknownEdge's message and repeated keys for
the same reason. Both now read one enumeration.

Independent verification at cc9d21e before authorizing merge: zero MODIFIED
goldens (git diff --name-status 95dd0b2..cc9d21e — every golden path is A);
the new fixture emits one case per declared type on both targets; both
unrepresentable_edge_union fixtures still red with the right sentinel; both
ambiguous_edge_orientation fixtures still red. Mutation test: deleting the
dedupe fails FIVE guards across two packages. Five gates green including
`sg docker -c 'just test-codegen-live'`.

Non-blocking items from round 6 filed as gqlc-kph4 (P2 — the plural-endpoint ×
undirected edge-closure path has zero corpus coverage, and round 5 changes
behaviour there) and gqlc-monh (P3 — rationale text incomplete or reaching

Method note for later beads: the reviewer's PASS was accepted only after
reading his actual verdict and re-running the evidence. Twice in this bead the
reviewer's diagnosis was right and his prescribed fix was wrong. A FAIL is
information about where to look, not an instruction.
