title: chore(ci): add live-smoke to master's required status checks
description:
gqlc-rvw (PR #323) landed the CODE half of promoting codegen-live to
PR-blocking — the workflow now runs on every PR. But the CONFIG half is
missing: master's branch-protection required_status_checks.contexts is
still [lint, test, tidy, actionlint, govulncheck]. \`live-smoke\` (the
codegen-live workflow's job name) is NOT in the required list, so it
runs but doesn't block auto-merge.

Proof (PR #323 itself): the live-smoke job was still IN_PROGRESS when
auto-merge fired at 05:37:22Z. Job completed successfully at 05:37:32Z
(10s later) — but had it failed, the merge would have happened anyway.
Wall-time on the runner was 63s (setup-go + setup-just + docker + both
arms in parallel).

Fix (one-line via the GH API):

  gh api -X PATCH \\
    repos/areqag/gqlc/branches/master/protection/required_status_checks \\
    -f 'contexts[]=lint' -f 'contexts[]=test' -f 'contexts[]=tidy' \\
    -f 'contexts[]=actionlint' -f 'contexts[]=govulncheck' \\
    -f 'contexts[]=live-smoke'

Verify: after apply, \`gh api repos/areqag/gqlc/branches/master/protection\`
should include \`live-smoke\` in contexts. Then any PR whose live-smoke
job FAILS will block auto-merge.

Alternative: do this via the GitHub UI at
https://github.com/areqag/gqlc/settings/branches — edit the master rule,
add \`live-smoke\` to required status checks.

This is a shared-infrastructure config change, not a code change — needs
owner action (or explicit owner sign-off before an agent runs the API
call).

Descends from: gqlc-rvw (which shipped the code half in PR #323).
close_reason: Applied via gh api PATCH — master's required_status_checks.contexts now includes live-smoke alongside the existing 5 checks. Verified via GET on branches/master/protection. Any future PR whose live-smoke job fails or is still in-progress will now block auto-merge. The gqlc-rvw promotion is fully complete — both the code half (on.pull_request trigger, PR #323) and the config half (required-checks list).

title: master-guard claude-pre-bash hook false-positives on worktree commits
description: The PreToolUse master-guard hook (.githooks/claude-pre-bash:31) resolves the branch via 'git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD' in the hook's own pwd (the Bash tool's persistent cwd), not the git command's actual target. A 'git -C <worktree> commit' (or a command that cd's inside the worktree within the same call) targeting a feature branch is denied when the session cwd sits on master. Observed 2026-07-14 during gqlc-ls8.2 (commit-5 halt in .claude/worktrees/ls8-2-cypher). Workaround: persistently cd the Bash tool into the worktree so the hook resolves the right branch. Fix direction: make the hook resolve the branch at the command's effective target — parse 'git -C <path>' and leading 'cd <path> &&' from tool_input.command before rev-parse. Needs its own PR + review; do NOT patch mid-loop.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #310 (squash 6a83f0e). PreToolUse master-guard rewritten as a python3 analyzer: effective-target resolution (cd/pushd chains, -C joins), quote-aware heredoc stripping, substitution-body recursion, shlex tokenization kills prose false positives; symbolic-ref fallback covers unborn HEADs. 29-case harness wired into just test (CI parity). Adversarial Linus review: PASS after 2 SHOULD-FIXes applied.

comments.author: antranig-yeretzian
comments.text: Second finding (2026-07-14, same ls8.2 halt): the hook also has a FALSE NEGATIVE. Regex at line 25 requires the word git immediately followed by the word commit, so the form [git -C <path> commit ...] does not match at all and is never branch-checked — this is how the ls8-2 worktree commits (c4deb99..6f2b2c1) landed before the halt. Empirically verified: the bare form and the cd-compound form MATCH (then branch-check the hook pwd -> false positive for worktree work); the -C form passes unchecked. Also noted: the hook matches the raw command string including quoted literals and prose (a for-loop echoing the bare form as a string was denied; so was a bd-comment command whose prose contained it). Fix should: (1) parse -C / leading-cd to resolve the command's effective target dir, (2) branch-check THAT dir, (3) ideally ignore quoted literals. Interim team ruling for ls8.2: worktree commits proceed via the -C form — target branch is cypher-collection-sink, the hook's stated intent (block commits on master/main) is preserved, and repo git hooks (core.hooksPath pre-commit gates) still fire normally. This interim allowance dies when this bead's fix lands.

title: cypher-collection-sink spec §5 phase-ordering fix (Rev 3)
description: Rev 3 (9843af7) hoists the addParameterUse sink gate from Rev 2's Phase D bundle into a new Phase B.5 that MUST land before any Phase C handler migration. Rev 2 (452c6b7) shipped a phase-ordering bug: its §5 bundled l.fail and addParameterUse into Phase D (post-migration), but every Phase-C handler (Match/With/Set/Delete/Remove) has a reach path into addParameterUse via mineWhere/collectSetItem/typeExpressionMining. Dropping the Match guard during Phase C surfaced the leak: TestMustParse/exists_body_mixed_limit_skip_and_where_params (inline require.Equal, no -update path) went red because $threshold picked up a spurious PropertyUse via EnterOC_Match → mineWhere → pairAddSub → addParameterUse. Fix shipped as three commits: b5e206d (Phase B.5 sink gate, observably-nil at then-current stack tip), 764dcd8 (Match migration re-run under the gate, now green), 9843af7 (spec Rev 3: revision-history stanza with failure narrative, §3.4 approved-map correction, §5 restructure with Phase B/B.5/D). Note: an earlier attempt to formalise this fix committed as b126e87 with a misleading subject and a stanza that falsely claimed Rev 2 had already contained the fix; that commit was amended into 9843af7 after linus-2 grill against git receipts (git show 452c6b7 verifies Rev 2 shipped bundled Phase D, not Phase B.5). Close as part of the eventual chore(beads) close-out PR for gqlc-ls8.2, do NOT create a separate close-out PR just for it.
close_reason: Shipped inside the gqlc-ls8.2 stack (b5e206d Phase B.5 gate, 764dcd8 Match re-migration, 9843af7 spec Rev 3), merged to master via PR #305 per this bead's close-out instruction. GH mirror #284 closed manually.

title: cypher parser tests: migrate hand-built shape expectations into the golden corpus
description: internal/query/cypher/parser_test.go (3,657 lines). query.Query has two faces (Go API and JSON wire, ADR 0008) and the parser tests pin both by hand: ~400 hand-built expectation values (oneBranch/oneWriteBranch/must helper constructions) duplicate shape facts the 3,199-file golden corpus already pins mechanically. Every additive model axis (ay9's 100-golden rebaseline was one -update) also costs manual edits across this file — the maintenance outlier of the whole test suite per the 2026-07-12 test-topology audit. BLOCKED BY gqlc-ls8.2: same package; start with a fresh team stacked on ls8.2's branch after its Linus PASS.
design: Migrate shape-pinning cases into the golden corpus (new fixtures where a TCK golden does not already cover the case); keep hand-built construction only where it IS the point — adversarial inputs, smart-constructor invariants, property tests. Wire-face goldens become the single shape-pinning surface; the Go-face tests shrink to invariants. Team decides the migration split in a docs/specs/ design doc, grilled by Linus BEFORE code. Careful: this is test architecture — parser source must not change (except possibly test helpers).
acceptance_criteria: No parser source changes (internal/query/cypher/*.go non-test untouched, modulo test helper files). Coverage does not shrink: every deleted hand-built case is either demonstrably covered by an existing golden or gets a new golden fixture. Property tests and sentinel-reachability sweep untouched and green. TCK counts unchanged. just test / fmt-check / lint green. parser_test.go materially smaller; a model-change rebaseline is one -update plus zero manual expectation-table edits.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #308 (squash-merged 2026-07-17, merge sha on master). parser_test.go 4,151 -> 3,528 lines (-623, ~15.0%); 42 shape-mirror pins migrated to golden corpus (34 sig-less + 8 sig-equal), sole sig-divergent pin retained; permanent dual-invariant TestMustParseGoldenTwins + harvestExecutingScenarios; goldens byte-identical; TCK counts unchanged; zero parser source changes. comments.author: antranig-yeretzian
comments.text: Team ls8-5 spun up (carmack-3 implementer, linus-3 reviewer), worktree ls8-5-goldens @ cypher-golden-migration, base master 05cb728. linus-3 oriented with independent census: parser_test.go is 4,151 lines (bead's ~3,657 stale); true migration surface is 190 mustParse cases (157 helper-built + 33 raw Query literals) — the bead's ~400 conflated per-binding must() constructor calls with cases. comments.author: antranig-yeretzian
comments.text: Spec round 1: FAIL from linus-3 at 3538a90. Spec claimed ~140 Class-A deletions; linus-3's mechanical census found 43 true shape-mirrors, 4 verbatim-TCK-but-skiplisted, 112 authored (no golden possible; TestGoldenOrphans + mustParse doctrine forbid minting authored goldens). title: cli: extract the generate pipeline (config file -> []File) from runGenerate
description: internal/cli/generate.go (334 lines). title: codegen: prepare commits every render decision; render stops re-deriving resolver types
description: internal/codegen/{prepare.go (847), types.go, render_queries.go (853), render_models.go}. The EdgeKey canonical-order discipline between prepare.go and render_queries.go is coupled by comment (spec §5.5), not structure. title: cypher parser: one collection sink replaces 14 per-handler subqueryDepth guards
description: internal/query/cypher/listener.go (+expr.go, pattern.go, call.go). The invariant 'bindings/refs/effects inside EXISTS { ... } never enter the outer query part' is enforced by 14 separate 'if l.subqueryDepth > 0' guards (listener.go:237,254,273,294,369,394,494,531,556,576,589,604,621,678) — every present and future Enter* handler must remember the guard, and a forgotten one produces a phantom binding the resolver types with the wrong scope (the exact failure ADR 0003's Stage-11 note names). ADR 0008's amendment history shows the cost: the 33k.3 EXISTS-param precision fix needed three sweep passes plus an idempotence guard.
design: Deepen the mutable listener state into one collection-sink module (a scope stack): handlers write bindings/returns/effects/params unconditionally; the sink routes to the outer part or discards, so suppression is decided at one seam instead of fourteen call sites. This preserves ADR 0003 Stage-11's invariant and its chosen posture (structural enforcement, not name-collision rules) — it concentrates enforcement, it does not re-litigate. Team decides the concrete interface in a docs/specs/ design doc, grilled by Linus BEFORE code. Wire shape must not move.
acceptance_criteria: All 3,199 parser goldens byte-identical (no -update). TCK acceptance suite: same pass/pending counts, zero failed. Referential-integrity and binding-uniqueness property tests green. Sentinel reachability sweep green. just test / fmt-check / lint green. cypher.New / Parse exported API unchanged. title: resolver: deepen the carried scope — branchState becomes a scope module
description: internal/resolver/resolve.go (1,977 lines). The carried scope — what a query part knows about each binding across a WITH — is one concept scattered over ten parallel maps in branchState (resolve.go:88: exportedNodeTypes, exportedEdgeTypes, exportedEdgeKeys, exportedEdgeCands, exportedEdgeBindings, exportedNullableBinding, exportedOptionalGroup, exportedResolvedTypes, exportedCallTypes, exportedOrder). title: codegen: testcontainer-backed live smoke test for generated repositories
description:
Owner-flagged idea (2026-07-11): spin up a real neo4j v5-community via testcontainers-go and verify that the emitted repository code actually queries a live driver — not just type-checks against v5.28.4.

Scope suggestion (per C1 orchestrator brief):
- internal/codegen/live_test.go with build-tag codegen_live so CI stays opt-in.
- Testcontainer running neo4j:5-community.
- Steps:
  1. Generate a repo from a valid fixture (probably many_col_many for a decent surface).
  2. Compile the generated package into a small test binary.
  3. Seed the neo4j with a few known rows.
  4. Run the test binary against the live db.
  5. Assert :one and :many methods return the expected data (Row struct field values, ErrNoRows, ErrMultipleResults).

Rationale for deferring past C1:
- The goldens and just test-codegen-fence already prove the emitted code compiles + lints under the pinned driver — the type-check gap is closed.
- Adding testcontainers introduces a Docker dep and CI-time increase that changes the character of the internal/codegen test suite (pure Go today).
- The gap this closes is 'compiles + lints' vs 'actually queries' — real, but not blocking C1's DoD. Better to land it as its own PR cycle with the Docker-CI wiring done deliberately.

Priority: medium — worth doing before v1 GA so the emitted-code contract is battle-tested against a real driver.

NUMBER assignable-from INTEGER-or-FLOAT then becomes a subset/assignability walk over those records. Same attribution family as gqlc-fvo (Use→Part) — consider deciding both together.

title: Resolver: undirected edge two-orientation trial + multi-match semantics
description: Post-freeze resolver contract handed off by Stage 5 (gqlc-7z6). An EdgeBinding with directed=false has NO authoritative orientation: the parser records endpoints in textual order only. The resolver MUST form TWO candidate schema.EdgeKeys (source->target AND target->source) and accept the binding if EITHER resolves against the directed-only schema. OPEN QUESTION (spec cypher-query-parser-stage-5.md §9): the trial can match zero, one, or TWO distinct directed edge types (schema has both A->B and B->A with the queried label) — define whether a double match is ambiguous, a union, or an error, and whether the resolver must report WHICH orientation(s) matched (which may require widening the marker bool->enum, cheap pre-consumer). Lives downstream of resolver bead gqlc-0mx and the freeze gqlc-cta.
notes: Linked to resolver stage R3 (gqlc-0mx.5) at the freeze (2026-07-03): the undirected two-orientation trial + double-match decision is R3's core design question; this bead carries the accumulated context.
close_reason: Decided and implemented in R3 (spec PR #95 §3.5/§4.6, code PR #96): resolver forms both orientation candidates; single-type single-hop undirected double-match => ErrAmbiguousEdgeOrientation (author disambiguates with directed arrow — no | union opt-in was written); multi-type >=2 matches => ResolvedEdgeUnion with canonically ordered EdgeKeys; matched orientation(s) inspectable from EdgeKey.Source/Target — no parser marker widening needed, query.Query freeze respected.

title: bd-gh-sync: a comment names a .beads/redirect mechanism that exists nowhere
description:
A comment in `.githooks/bd-gh-sync` explains how a worktree without its own beads DB reaches the main clone's, and attributes it to a `.beads/redirect` file.

The round-2 reviewer looked for that file and found none anywhere on the machine. It then confirmed the CONCLUSION directly — `bd show` from a DB-less worktree does reach the main clone — so the comment's claim is right about the outcome and wrong (or at least unwitnessed) about the mechanism.

Same shape as gqlc-z8ay and the memory note on mechanisms named in passing: the sentence was arguing the outcome, so the outcome got checked and the mechanism leaned on to say it did not.

Fix: either find the real mechanism (bd's own discovery walk is the likely answer) and name it, or state the outcome without attributing it.

title: bd-gh-sync tests: two guards whose deletion nothing detects, and a fixture missing the GIT_ env scrub its siblings carry
description:
Three residue items from the round-2 adversarial review of PR #1037. None blocked the merge; all are suite-integrity gaps.

1. Deleting EITHER `win_check` call in the timing fixture is undetected — the suite stays green. A guard nothing observes is a guard that can be removed by accident.

2. The concurrency fixture lacks the `unset "${!GIT_@}"` scrub its three sibling fixtures carry. The reviewer proved both halves: the leak has a real cost if it lands, AND it is unreachable on git 2.55, and the row fails closed anyway. So this is consistency, not a live hole — but the asymmetry with three siblings is the kind of thing that reads as deliberate when it is not.

3. `git worktree add` in the fixture lacks the `-c core.hooksPath` its neighbouring `git commit` has, and it DOES fire `post-checkout`. Given gqlc-7ijy (agent worktree creation is the identified writer of core.hooksPath drift) and the hooks-drift tripwire now installing a `post-checkout` arm, a fixture that fires real `post-checkout` unpinned is a future flake.

title: justfile house rule 3: two prose qualifiers narrower or looser than the measurements behind them
description:
Non-blocking residue from the round-7 review of PR #1031 (merged as 359e48f8). Both concern the SIGPIPE/pipefail house rule now on master in the justfile; the rule itself is sound, these are two prose seams.

1. The rule says the readable safe case is 'a single write() of AT MOST the pipe capacity', and gives as its reason that 'the write lands with the reader alive'. That reason is false above capacity — but so is the qualifier's necessity. Measured in review, holding write-count at 1 and match position at line 1 and varying only size across a fcntl-confirmed 65536-byte capacity: 65,536 / 131,072 / 1,048,576 all returned rc 0 in 60 of 60. At 16x the writer genuinely short-wrote (`wrote=131072 of 1048576`) and the pipeline still returned 0, because a partial write to a closed pipe returns a COUNT, not SIGPIPE. So the 'at most the pipe capacity' bound is stricter than anything measured, and the reason given for it does not hold in the region it excludes. The sentence is scoped below capacity so it is not false, but it advertises a limit that is not the real one.

2. The measurement table says the safe two-write case has the match on the last LINE; the sentence generalises it to the last WRITE. Those coincide only for the producer that was measured (one write per line). A producer batching several lines per write makes them come apart, and the rule is stated in terms of writes.

Fix is prose only, on master's justfile, and should carry the short-write measurement rather than just dropping the bound.

title: close hook: the close arm's reachability list omits the unterminated-heredoc case
description:
A `bd close` on a line following an UNTERMINATED heredoc is classified `no-close-seen`, hook=allow.

Measured (round-5 review of PR #1029, residue row R4):
- `cat <<EOF.txt > /dev/null` / `notes` / `bd close gqlc-x -r "Closed at <orphan>."` -> `no-close-seen`, allow.
- Terminated control -> DENY.

This is a DISCLOSURE gap, not a new mechanism: the header already discloses it for the `git commit` arm (the tokenizer consumes the rest of the input as heredoc body). What is missing is that the close arm's own 'reaches / does not reach' list does not name it, so a maintainer reading that list concludes the close arm is unaffected.

Fix is a line in the close arm's list plus a pinning row, so the omission cannot silently return.

title: tmpreap: the private tmpreap recipe is invokable with arbitrary flags
description:
`just tmpreap <root> -check` runs (verified). [private] only hides a recipe from --list, so `just tmpreap /tmp -apply` is an unlisted apply path.

Not an escalation over `just tmp-reap apply` — and as of round 2 the tool itself refuses -apply outside a designated temporary directory — but the read-only guarantee that tmp-report advertises rests on tmp-report having no {{args}}, not on anything in tmpreap. Worth stating in the recipe comment, or splitting the private recipe into a report arm and an apply arm.

title: tmpreap: the archive preserves text files, not tree structure
description:
Empty directories, symlinks, fifos, modes beyond Perm(), ownership and xattrs are not in the tarball. Restoring an archived scratch dir gives you its text files, not its tree.

Either document this in the -archive flag help and the tmp-reap recipe comment, or carry directory and symlink headers. The tool now prints what it could not archive (round 2), which covers the file-content half; this is the structure half.

title: justfile: {{mode}} is raw-interpolated into the tmp-reap shell case header
description:
The tmp-reap recipe uses quote(root) two lines away but interpolates {{mode}} unquoted into `case "{{mode}}" in` and into the error echo.

Two crafted payloads were tried in review and BOTH failed — the second raw interpolation in the error echo re-breaks the parse, so bash exits 2 without executing. That is accidental defence, not a guard.

Fix: mode={{quote(mode)}} into a variable, then case "$mode" in.

title: resolver: commit()'s empty-intersection comment states a consequence its own named pin falsifies
description:
Round-2 review finding N7 on PR #1032 (bead gqlc-sxzj), found by the reviewer. Landed on master in b09b27ac.

`resolve.go`'s `commit()` comment AND PR #1032's commit body both say that substituting on a length-0 intersection 'would ACCEPT queries master refuses', and name `invalid/unlabelled_optional_hop_empty_intersection.cypher` as the pin.

Measured, it does not. Mutation MU-D (substitute on a length-0 intersection) across all 12880 corpus cells produces 0 DIFFERENT VERDICT and 2 DIFFERENT SENTINEL. The named fixture goes refuse ErrUnknownLabel -> refuse ErrUnknownEdge ('unknown edge: Company&Large-[HAS_DESK]->Desk'). Refuse either way.

The gate IS genuinely pinned — the fixture's `ErrorIs(ErrUnknownLabel)` is what dies — and the SAFETY property holds: this branch cannot accept on an empty intersection. Only the stated *consequence* is wrong.

There is a structural reason to expect it is always wrong: the very edge that emptied the intersection is still in the pattern, and it fails edge validation against whatever `attainable` substituted. So the second line of defence catches it before any accept.

Fix: correct the comment to claim what is true and pinned (the sentinel moves, the refusal stays) rather than a verdict change that cannot happen. Same genre as round 1's N3, which was fixed properly; this is its neighbour.

Note the commit-body half is unrecoverable — this repo squash-merges with squash_merge_commit_message=BLANK, so the branch commit body never reached master. Only the in-tree comment can be corrected.

Source: /tmp/lead/verdict-sxzj-r2.md, Non-blocking residue, N7.

title: resolver: the plural writer omits the resolvedCovers delete its two siblings both write
description:
Round-1 review finding N6 on PR #1032 (bead gqlc-sxzj), re-verified in round 2, declined by scope.

The new plural writer at resolve.go:1227 omits the `delete(t.resolvedCovers, ...)` that BOTH its siblings write:
  - the singular arm 25 lines above
  - `BindNodeCands` at scope.go:203

and both siblings carry comments arguing explicitly FOR writing the unreachable line, in the words 'so the absence is asserted rather than assumed'. The plural arm is the one writer that does not, and nothing says why.

Unreachable today, re-verified: `inferUnlabelled` filters names already in `resolved`/`nodeCands` out of `pending` (resolve.go:1077-1089), and a name leaves `pending` on the round it commits. So it changes no answer today.

Fix is either the one-line delete plus the sibling comment, or a comment on the plural arm saying why it deliberately differs. The current state — three writers, two with a justification comment and one silently without — is the part worth closing.

Source: /tmp/lead/verdict-sxzj-r2.md section 5 row N6.

title: ADR 0026: two prose claims carry their scope 200 lines away or not at all
description:
Both found by the Linus review of gqlc-agt0 (/tmp/lead/verdict-agt0-r1b.md, residue item R-c), both still present, and neither in scope for a PR that touches no docs.

(i) `docs/adr/0026-govulncheck-cannot-see-in-package-tests.md:256` says the check is "run on every invocation", unscoped. The justfile scopes the same claim inline at justfile:1526-1530: "How often that is in CI is the `vuln` job's own path filter, not this line." The ADR should carry the same qualification.

(ii) `docs/adr/0026-govulncheck-cannot-see-in-package-tests.md:241` asserts that "`...and the go standard library:` is exactly and only the unplaced rendering". Its version scope sits ~200 lines away at :439-443 ("that is a property of this version, not of the pattern"). This is the house "no universals in prose claims" shape: a reader at :241 gets a universal with no way to know it is version-bound. Move the scope inline.

title: codegen/conformance: requireCensus refuses on three arms but its comment and message say 'either/both directions'
description:
`internal/codegen/conformance/specfence_test.go` — `requireCensus` refuses on three distinct arms (duplicated, lost, undeclared), while the surrounding doc comment and the failure message it prints both frame the reconciliation as "either/both direction(s)".

A reader who hits the refusal and counts directions from the prose gets a different shape than the one the function implements. Two-directional framing over a three-armed check.

Cosmetic and pre-existing — the framing predates PR #1025, which is what surfaced it. Graded non-blocking residue by that PR's round-1 review; the arms themselves were confirmed load-bearing under deletion in the same review.

Fix is to the prose, not the arms. Do not substitute a count for the count — name what the check refuses on and let the reader derive, per this repo's settled shape for these.

Re-derive before acting: do not trust the arm names or the function name in this description without reading the current master.

title: modscope: justfile_test's provenance sentence credits a commit the comparison did not exist on
description:
`internal/tools/modscope/justfile_test.go:474-477` (as of 9b4062a0) says the differential comparison was "Measured on the commit before \`joinContinuedHeader\` existed, with a backslash-continued header written into this justfile in place of vuln's", and reports that "this comparison named vuln".

The comparison is introduced by commit `0246c4bb` ("modscope: compare this reader against just on the real justfile"), which lands AFTER the fix commit. So on the commit the sentence names, the instrument it credits was not in the tree — the measurement must have been taken by transplanting the comparison backwards onto that tree.

The RESULT is not in dispute: PR #1001's round-4 reviewer reproduced both runs on two trees independently. What is wrong is the provenance — the sentence describes an experiment as having been run on a tree that did not contain the apparatus.

Fix is to the sentence, not to the test. Say what was actually done (comparison transplanted onto the pre-fix tree) or drop the commit reference.

Found by the round-4 review of PR #1001; graded non-blocking residue there. Re-derive before acting: do not trust the line numbers or the SHA in this description without checking them against current master.

title: PR #1001's round-3 correction list omits a fifth round-2 correction, and 'derived with an instrument' overstates what the script checks
description:
Found by the adversarial review of PR #1001 round 3 (bead gqlc-6n9y), 2026-08-18.
Residue: nothing false is live in code, so it did not block the merge. Filed
because both halves live in the PR body, which is a durable carrier that outlives
the branch.

HALF 1 -- A MISSING ENTRY. PR #1001's body carries a list of what round 2
corrected. Commit 0b49b868 replaced this sentence, which stood at
4aad2777:internal/tools/modscope/justfile_test.go:495-498:

  "This is the only one of the three that fails open -- a caller lost this way
   is not reported and nothing else here notices"

with a correctly-scoped one. No entry in the list describes that correction. It
is a false NEGATIVE (a real correction gone unrecorded), not the false POSITIVE
that made round 3's B2 a blocker, which is why it is residue.

Worth noting what the omitted sentence WAS: an "only one of the three" plus a
"nothing else here notices". That is precisely the defect class round 3's own
headline blocker was about. The list of corrections omits the correction most
similar to the thing the list exists to demonstrate.

HALF 2 -- THE METHOD CLAIM. The body says the list was "re-derived in round 3
with an instrument". The script, /tmp/factory/r3-list-check.sh, verifies rows it
is HANDED; it does not enumerate the round's corrections and hand them to itself.
So it can confirm every row present is real and cannot report a row absent --
exactly the failure that produced half 1. "Re-derived with an instrument" claims
a completeness the instrument does not have.

HOW TO REPAIR. Do not add the missing entry and leave the method sentence
standing -- that repeats the error one entry later. Either describe what the
script actually checks, or build the enumerating instrument: walk the round's
commits, extract every prose hunk, and require each to appear in the list. The
second is the honest form and is reusable, since this PR is on its fourth round
of the same defect.

Related: gqlc-6n9y, and the reviewer-instrument family generally -- a check
scoped smaller than the claim it is cited for.

title: bd/GH #941 description undercounts the colon-defect carriers at three; the PR body's four is correct
description:
Found by the adversarial review of PR #1001 round 3 (bead gqlc-6n9y), 2026-08-18.
Residue, withheld from that PR's round-4 scope.

THE DISAGREEMENT. Two durable carriers give different numbers for how many sites
name the parameter-default colon defect by bead id.

  PR #1001 body      four: justfile:390, main.go:308,
                     justfile_test.go:33, justfile_test.go:399
  bd gqlc-6n9y and
  GitHub #941 body   three

The reviewer re-took it at repo scope on merge base 49213009 and the PR body is
the correct one. The bead's undercount is INHERITED, not introduced by that
branch: the fourth carrier is the doc paragraph on
TestParseJustfileReadsWhatJustReads, and the bead accounts only for the row.

THE TRAP, and the reason this is its own bead rather than a one-line edit.
bd-gh-sync runs with --prefer-github, which makes the GitHub issue body
authoritative. Editing the bd description alone is silently reverted on the next
pull. The GitHub issue body must be edited FIRST, then bd updated -- see
`bd memories` on the bd-gh-sync revert behaviour.

DO NOT REPAIR THIS BY SUBSTITUTING FOUR FOR THREE. The shape that survives review
in this repo states the negative and names what is pinned, with no bare count. A
sentence that names the carriers without totalling them cannot go stale when a
fifth appears, which is exactly how this one broke.

Related: gqlc-6n9y (the PR), gqlc-3205 (nothing re-checks that bd moves
updated_at on a description edit).

title: modscope: justfileDisagreements compares per name last-wins, so a shadowed duplicate recipe's body difference is never asked
description:
Found by the adversarial review of PR #1001 round 3 (bead gqlc-6n9y), 2026-08-18.
Filed as residue: it does not block that PR and was explicitly withheld from its
round-4 scope.

THE GAP. In internal/tools/modscope/justfile_test.go the two sides disagree about
what a duplicate recipe name means:

  justfileDisagreements  :856-859   builds its map per NAME, last write wins
  unsweptModscopeCallers :391-395   decides per ENTRY

So when a justfile declares the same recipe name twice, the body difference
between the shadowed declaration and the winning one changes the answer the
DECISION consults, and this differential test never asks about it. The one thing
that would surface it is the read-twice complaint, which this test does not
raise (:519-522).

WHY IT IS LOW PRIORITY BUT REAL. This repo's justfile does not currently contain
a duplicate recipe name, so nothing is mis-swept today. The defect is that the
gate's silence on the shape is not a decision anyone took -- it is a consequence
of one side keying by name. That is the same fail-silent-where-fail-closed-was-
claimed shape the whole modscope cluster keeps producing.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. A probe that puts a duplicate recipe name in a copy of the
real justfile, where the two declarations differ in whether the body names the
modscope package, and asks whether either test reports. Do it out of tree
(scratch probes never touch a real package directory). Note `just` itself may
reject or warn on a duplicate name -- establish what `just --dump` does with it
FIRST, because if just refuses the file the whole question is moot and that is
the answer.

DO NOT WRITE A COUNT OR A UNIVERSAL INTO THE FIX. State what was probed.

Related: gqlc-98ii (the `mod` blind spot, same test, same silence-by-agreement
shape), gqlc-k2jq, gqlc-2woz, gqlc-6n9y.

title: codegen corpus: two fixture tests are the sole user of an import, so their paired removal reds at require.NoError not the guard
notes:
A measurement worth not re-deriving, from the independent review of PR #1002
round 3 (bd gqlc-wla6). Classified residue there. Filing so the sweep is on the
record rather than in a /tmp log.

THE SWEEP. For each name in corpusTests, drop the name AND drop its func Test
block from the fixture, run, restore. Both packages, at 15e8f9d2, every row
screened with go test -c and restored to a pristine md5.

  neo4j  20 of 21 rc=0.  TestListyNarrowsEachElement is not.
  age    28 of 29 rc=0.  TestEmittedMethodBindsAnInstantAsMicroseconds is not.

Each is the only fixture test whose body uses a given import -- "time" on the
neo4j side, "context" on the age side. Removing it orphans the import, so the
child module fails to build and the run reds at require.NoError with
[build failed], NOT at require.NotEmpty and not at ElementsMatch.

Pruning the orphaned import in the SAME edit restores rc=0. So this is the Go
compiler refusing an intermediate state a real commit would not ship, not the
harness catching anything.

WHY THE SHIPPED PROSE SURVIVES IT. The code comment's clause is past-tense
existential -- "a run with one name and its test removed together came back
green" -- which 20 of 21 and 28 of 29 satisfy, and its unit is "one commit's
edit", which a three-line commit meets. Deleting the earlier "two-line change"
count is what inoculates it. Nothing to fix in the comment.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WORTH DOING, IF ANYTHING. This is a fake-RED shape: a row reds
for a reason unrelated to what the test asserts, and the message a reader sees
names require.NoError rather than the corpus. That is the class the repo already
screens mutations for. Anyone building a future mutation matrix over this corpus
must screen for [build failed] and must not score these two rows as kills.

RELATED. Bears on gqlc-lwtp (sweep the conformance AST-census tests for the same
aggregate-emptiness shape) and gqlc-8bl0, both of which will want to mutate this
corpus. Same family as the go-test-c-is-the-mutation-screen note.

title: modscope: justfile_test's 'the 24 pinned bodies' pins 25, and recipeBodies has no unit test
description:
Two residues from the PR #1001 (gqlc-6n9y) round-2 review. Neither reopened that
round; both land on master with it.

1. A FALSE COUNT, ALREADY "CORRECTED" ONCE IN THE WRONG DIRECTION.
   `internal/tools/modscope/justfile_test.go:877-878` (and PR #1001 body line
   203) say "the 24 pinned bodies". A `go/parser` walk gives:

       ROWS=24   justRecipe LITERALS=25   (24 with an explicit body key, 1 zero-value)

   24 is the ROW count; 25 bodies are asserted, because one row carries two
   literals — row "a header spelled inside a string assignment is read anyway"
   has two, one with no `body:` key, and the neighbouring row has `want: nil`.
   Commit `bb520835` deliberately changed 25 -> 24 with the reason "Scoped to the
   test actually named: 24 literals". There are 25 literals, so the correction
   moved it the wrong way.

   SINGLE-INSTRUMENT WARNING: the 25 comes from ONE `go/parser` walk by the
   reviewer. Re-derive it with your own instrument before editing, and read the
   per-row breakdown rather than trusting a total. If you disagree, say so with
   the command — the reviewer flagged this as its own weak spot.

   Both load-bearing sub-claims around it HOLD and must not be disturbed: the
   longest pinned body is exactly 3 lines, and every row survives a 10-line cap
   (only the live differential reddens under that cap).

   FIX SHAPE: do not swap 24 for 25. That is replacing one count with another,
   and this line has already been "fixed" that way once. Say what the block pins
   without a cardinality, or name the object precisely enough that the number is
   derivable rather than asserted.

2. `recipeBodies` HAS NO UNIT TEST.
   `priorDependencies` was extracted and given seven rows on the explicit
   argument that the live `just --dump` differential only reaches THIS repo's
   justfile shape. That argument applies verbatim to `recipeBodies`, which has no
   unit rows — and it is what mutation row N38 survives on. Extract and pin it
   the same way, or write down why the two are not alike.

Related: gqlc-6n9y, gqlc-98ii (the `mod` blind spot found in the same review).
notes:
CORROBORATED 2026-08-18 by the PR #1001 round-3 adversarial review, with two
instruments beyond the original go/parser walk:

  AST     rows=24, justRecipe literals=25, literals with an explicit body key=24,
          zero-value literals=1
  BEHAVIOUR  the cap-at-ten mutation ("Row B") reddens the zero-value row

Diagnosis sharpened: 24 is the ROW count mislabelled as a BODY count. That is
why both load-bearing sub-claims still hold (longest pinned body is 3 lines;
every row survives a 10-line cap) while the sentence is false. So the repair is
to the noun, not to the digit -- and the shape that survives review here would
drop the total altogether rather than change 24 to 25.

Note commit bb520835 deliberately changed 25 -> 24 citing "24 literals". There
are 25 literals. Whoever fixes this should read that commit first so the same
correction is not made in the same wrong direction a second time.

title: modscope: goDirs' doc names two inputs where the code uses three
description:
Inherited prose defect, live on master, verified byte-identical between merge
base 49213009 and origin/master. Surfaced by the PR #1001 round-2 review, which
found the PR BODY claiming this had been fixed when the branch contains no
goDirs change at all. The claim was removed from that body; the underlying
defect is real and is this bead.

`internal/tools/modscope/main.go`: the sentence describing what `goDirs` decides
from names two inputs. The answer is decided by three:

  - moduleRoot
  - the `nested` prune set
  - **skipName** (main.go:157 — excludes `.`/`_`-prefixed entries, `testdata`,
    and `vendor`), applied in the walk at main.go:178 and again at :328

So an entry can be excluded from goDirs' answer by a rule the doc does not
mention. Verify the exact sentence and the exact input list yourself before
editing — do not take "two" or "three" from this bead. The repo's signature
defect is a count in prose that the artifact falsifies, and a bead is not
exempt from that.

FIX SHAPE: prefer stating the property over listing inputs. A list of N inputs
rots the moment someone adds an N+1th filter, which is exactly how this sentence
became wrong. If a list is genuinely the clearest form, derive it from the code
at the moment of writing and say what it is a list OF.

title: codegen: the corpus ElementsMatch failure message can be read positionally, and age's silent spellings were not re-measured after the guard landed
description:
Two weak residue items from the gqlc-wla6 / PR #1002 review. Both were rated
weak deliberately; neither reopened that PR. Recorded so they are not lost, not
because either is urgent.

1. THE FAILURE MESSAGE CAN BE READ POSITIONALLY.
   The corpus census compares with `ElementsMatch`, whose message says the
   comparison is "entry for entry and counting repeats". `ElementsMatch` IGNORES
   ORDER — it is a multiset comparison — but "entry for entry" is a phrase a
   reader can take positionally, i.e. as index-by-index. A CI reader sees only
   the message.
   The adjacent code comment does carry the correction ("comparison is by
   multiset"), so the information exists in the tree; it just is not in the
   carrier the failing reader gets.
   Note what is NOT wrong here: the message correctly states a RELATION and
   enumerates nothing. That was the round-1 defect (an enumeration of two causes
   that a duplicated entry fell outside of) and it is genuinely closed. Do not
   "fix" this by adding an enumeration back.

2. AGE'S SILENT SPELLINGS WERE NOT RE-MEASURED AFTER THE FIX.
   The three silent spellings and the duplicate-entry row were measured in the
   AGE package before the non-empty guard landed, and nobody re-took them after.
   No movement is EXPECTED — the name sets are identical between the packages
   and the guard was an additive edit — but expected is not witnessed. If anyone
   is in that file for another reason, re-take the four rows.

SCREENS, if either item is picked up (these cost real rounds on #1002):
  - `go test -c` is NOT the screen for these — the fixture compiles one module
    down (gqlc-hreu). Run the outer harness and read the CHILD log.
  - `\[(build|setup) failed\]` — assert BOTH spellings absent. A fixture parse
    error prints `[setup failed]`.
  - Anchor sibling PASS on `^[[:space:]]*--- PASS`; the space-only class misses
    testify's TAB indentation.

Related: gqlc-wla6, gqlc-mlf4, gqlc-lwtp, gqlc-hreu.

title: codegen/neo4j: the G4/G5 record.Get gates are pinned only by wording the emitter itself chooses
description:
Residue of PR #990 (bd gqlc-1uic, GH #975), named in both review rounds.

The corpus's record.Get arms (matrix rows G4 and G5) ARE killed when their gate is dropped -- round 2 spot-checked G4 first-party and confirmed it (emitter md5 14aafff2, RED = TestAnythingColumnsCarryTheirNull, 20 sibling PASS, build failed 0). So this is not an unpinned gate.

The weakness is WHAT kills them. Those arms word their own refusals, and the corpus asserts those words. So the assertion is held against a string the EMITTER chooses -- change the emitter's wording and the corpus row goes RED for a reason that is a rename, not a regression; keep the wording and a behavioural change underneath it can pass. The gate and its test agree because they are the same author, not because they are independent.

Contrast with what PR #990 did for the entity and list arms: those propagate the DRIVER's error (GetRecordValue's own wording, copied verbatim into testdata/driverstub_neo4j.go.txt from the real driver), so the assertion pins that the emission propagated something it did not author.

NOTE THE STANDING LIMIT either way: the corpus runs against the stub, so even the propagating arms pin "the emission propagated whatever GetRecordValue said", NOT the real driver's wording. Do not let a fix here overclaim in the other direction.

Low priority: this is a robustness-of-pin issue, not a hole. Worth doing when the record.Get arms are next touched.

title: codegen.ResolvedTypeName: a String() returning empty yields a refusal that names nothing
description:
Inherited hole, NOT created by PR #991 (GH #961) -- measured identical at cbb11a7e and at PR #991's head, by Linus round 1 on that PR.

codegen.ResolvedTypeName guards against a FAULT (panic while asking for the name), not against EMPTINESS. A type such as `struct{ resolver.ResolvedNode }` that declares `String() string { return "" }` does not panic, so the guard passes it through, and the refusal renders as:

    column "n" projects
    parameter $p is

-- a refusal that names nothing useful. This does not violate PR #991's rule ("a refusal that names an unmatched type must not fault while asking for the name"), which is why it was not a blocker there.

WHERE TO FIX: in codegen.ResolvedTypeName itself, not at either call site. That is precisely what #991's export ruling bought -- one implementation, so both internal/codegen and internal/codegen/age move together. Do not fix it in age.unservedColumn/unservedParam.

Related thin spot, same file family: fallThroughComment's assertion in internal/codegen/age is a substring match, which is weaker than the surrounding AST guards in sealedsum_test.go. Pre-existing and untouched by #991.

title: convention: a comment citing a test by name rots on rename and nothing checks it
description:
internal/query/cypher/typing.go carries a comment citing a test BY NAME. Nothing compiles, links or checks that citation, so it rots silently the moment the test is renamed or moved. Pre-existing convention across the repo, not introduced by any one branch; surfaced as residue F4 of the PR #965 round 4 Linus PASS.

The question to rule on is what the convention should be, not just this one site:

  (a) leave by-name citations and accept the rot;
  (b) drop the name and describe the property the test pins, so the sentence
      survives a rename;
  (c) gate it — a check that every quoted Test<Name> in a comment resolves to a
      declared test function.

(c) is cheap for Go (an AST walk over comments plus the test declarations in the module) and would convert a whole class of rotting prose into a CI failure. It also has a false-positive shape worth measuring first: a comment naming a test that lives in another module or was deliberately deleted.

Relates to gqlc-6xln (keep growing-range counts and universals out of durable carriers) — same family, different carrier: that one is about numbers going stale, this one about names going dangling.

Survey the repo for how many sites this affects before choosing; a convention ruling on one site is not a convention.

title: query: TestScalarAndEntityTypeString's table completeness is gated by nothing
description:
internal/query: TestScalarAndEntityTypeString drives a table of scalar and entity types through String(). Nothing checks the table is COMPLETE — a new scalar or entity variant added to the sealed sum can be omitted from the table and every test still passes.

This is the same class the merged PR #965 closed for TypeList's field declaration: a claim about a sealed sum that no artifact gates. #965's author disclosed this gap in its own weak-spot bullet and asked for a bead; the round-4 Linus PASS named it as residue F3.

The likely instrument is the one #965 already uses: an AST walk over the sealed sum's variants compared against the table's membership. A count is not enough — a count pins guard size, not membership.

Filed as residue F3 of the PR #965 round 4 Linus PASS.

title: convention: a published mutation must be reproducible as a diff, and a growing-range universal must not enter a durable doc
description:
Two conventions the PR #963 round-3 reviewer derived from measurements it made first-hand. Both are about how a measurement is WRITTEN so a later reader can re-run it, not about any one PR.

1. A PUBLISHED MUTATION MUST BE DESCRIBED AS A DIFF, NOT AS PROSE.

Every mutation row in this repository publishes an "md5 after" column. That column is author-self-certified by construction: a later reader can only reproduce it by guessing the exact bytes the author wrote.

MEASURED, not argued. The reviewer re-ran two inherited rows. MR-2 (delete an early-out) reproduced to the exact digit, b97b97d7, because deleting a named block is unambiguous. MR-2ctl (replace the same site with a panic) produced the SAME behavioural result to the digit — 268 panics, 275 FAIL — but a DIFFERENT hash, 027faa18 vs 276fafeb, purely because the two authors wrote different panic text.

So the column value is its MOVEMENT (changed=YES vs NO-OP), which is what it is actually for, and NOT its digits. Publishing digits invites a later reader to read a mismatch as a contradiction when it is only a difference in wording. Either publish the mutation as a literal diff, or say explicitly that the hash pins movement rather than identity.

2. A GROWING-RANGE UNIVERSAL MUST NOT BE COPIED INTO A LONGER-LIVED CARRIER.

A claim of the form "every commit since SHA is comment-only" is true when written and self-rots on the next code commit in that range, without anyone touching the sentence. It was acceptable in the #963 PR body, where the reviewer graded it correctly left alone: dating it would defeat its purpose and the PR was at merge, so the range closed at merge.

It is NOT acceptable in a spec, an ADR, a code comment or a bead — carriers that outlive the range. In those, either date the endpoint or state the claim over a closed range.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A BEAD: this repository has a signature defect — a prose claim the branch own artifacts falsify — that has cost five PRs a round each this wave. Both conventions above are that defect caught at the point of writing rather than at review.

ACCEPTANCE: written into the contributor-facing conventions the review briefs already draw on, so it is guidance rather than tribal knowledge. No CI gate is proposed; this is a writing convention and a gate for it would grade prose.

title: .gitignore lacks __pycache__ and *.pyc, and the hook suite writes both
description:
py_compile screening of .githooks/claude-pre-bash writes __pycache__ next to the extensionless hook — verified by the PR #946 round-7 reviewer. .gitignore covers neither __pycache__/ nor *.pyc, so anyone who screens the hook locally gets untracked noise in .githooks/ and risks staging it.

The PR #946 author agreed and deliberately kept the change out of that diff to avoid widening scope. One line each.

title: .githooks: claude-pre-bash's _EMITTED once-only guard is unpinned because main() exposes no seam
description:
Mutation M26 in PR #946's battery — replacing the `if not _EMITTED:` once-only guard with `if True:` — SURVIVES: no row in .githooks/tests/claude-pre-bash-test.sh detects it. The author agreed and named it rather than papering over it, and the round-7 reviewer confirmed the body states the gap without claiming it harmless.

Cause: main() offers no seam to invoke the emit path twice within one process, so a suite that shells out per row cannot observe once-only behaviour at all. Pinning it needs either a seam (a callable entry point the suite can invoke twice) or an in-process Python test rather than a bash-driven one.

Low priority: the failure mode is a duplicated warning line, not a missed refusal.

title: codegen/neo4j: four prose defects left in the C5 spec and the corpus fixture
description:
All four verified by the PR #966 round-3 reviewer, all pre-existing, none in scope for that PR:

1. docs/specs/codegen-stage-c5.md:237-239 says 'five column arms' in a sentence that then names SEVEN and says C5 adds 'an eighth'. Self-contradicting within one clause.
2. The same sentence cites generate.go:99-128. No generate.go in the tree is that long — the neo4j one is 44 lines. A stale line-number pointer, the rot class that cost #946/#951/#963 a round each.
3. internal/codegen/neo4j/testdata/corpus_test.go.txt:689-695 carries a 'could not have been written to carry' universal. The reviewer ruled it imprecise rather than false — on the reading that it is about what the FIXTURE could carry it holds — and upheld the author's decision to disclose and leave it. Still worth tightening.
4. Same file :520: 'a column is decoded through neo4j.GetRecordValue' is loose. An ANY VALUE column and an edge-union column both read record.Get. Contextually true where it sits, but it is the same claim PR #966 corrected in three other carriers.

Cite constructs, not line numbers, when fixing.

title: codegen: ADR 0025's map-member runtime types are unmeasured for temporal, spatial, byte-array and v6-only kinds
description:
ADR 0025 (merged in PR #968, master c4081ee4) records measured marker->Go-type mappings for map[string]any members across apache-age-pgx-v5, neo4j-go-v5 and neo4j-go-v6. The measurement covered integer, float, string, nil, bool, array and nested-map members, executed against real packstream hydrators in both driver majors plus the emitted AGE agtypeMap.

Not measured, and therefore not claimed by the ADR: temporal kinds (Date, LocalTime, LocalDateTime, Time, Duration, DateTime), spatial kinds (Point2D, Point3D), byte arrays, and v6-only kinds (the Vector[...] family and PackedUUID).

The ADR is honest about this -- it quantifies only over what was run -- so this is a coverage gap, not a false claim. Closing it means extending the same probe shape to those kinds and recording whether the three backends still agree.

Prior art to reuse rather than rebuild: PR #968's probe built copied driver modules under /tmp and packed a stream the way the server would (neo4j/internal/db hydrator_test.go's `build func()` pattern), then read members back through neo4j.Record (which is a true type alias for db.Record in both majors, so a caller reads the same bytes). The AGE half compiled schema_any_property's emitted models.go into a throwaway module and called agtypeMap directly. Both halves carried positive controls -- pack an int as float, and rename a key -- so a no-op cannot read as PASS.

Note the structural bound already established for integers: packstream has no integer marker wider than 8 bytes (packstream/unpacker.go:202,226-229,248; Int() errors 'Illegal int length' otherwise), so a neo4j map member structurally cannot carry a value outside int64 range. Ask whether an equivalent structural bound exists for each new kind before asserting agreement from a sample.

title: check-pr-closes suite: the <!-- c --><pre> opt-out carrier is a confirmed fail-open with no row of its own
description:
Found by the independent review of PR #901 round 8 (/tmp/factory/verdict-901-r8.md section 15). PRE-EXISTING and NOT introduced by #901 -- e04e507d honours the same shape identically. THE FAIL-OPEN, probed first-party rather than reasoned about. A Refs: opt-out marker placed between an inline `
` and its closing `
`: - POST /markdown returns `
Refs: gqlc-mirrored #617`,
    so GitHub HIDES the marker from a human reading the rendered body.
  - The gate HONOURS it (rc=0, warning annotation).

So an author can carry an opt-out that the gate accepts and a reviewer reading the
rendered PR body cannot see. Same class as the `x 
` shape, which has been
disclosed since round 5.

WHAT IS ALREADY THERE. The class is disclosed in the suite source at
.githooks/tests/check-pr-closes-test.sh:1002-1012 -- 'an inline 
 part-way
along a paragraph line opens the element in the output all the same, and the
marker below it lands inside ... this honours it' -- carrying the row 'a marker
below a 
 opened part-way along a line is honoured'. That class-level row's
comment does cover both exemplars.

THE GAP. PR #901's body writes 'everything on the far side of that split
(x 
, 
) is disclosed and rowed'. Both are disclosed; only
`x 
` has its OWN row. The reviewer graded this imprecision rather than
falsehood, because the class-level row's comment covers both -- but the second
exemplar is a first-party-confirmed fail-open carrying no row.

ACCEPTANCE. One `expect_green_saying` row in
.githooks/tests/check-pr-closes-test.sh for the `
` / marker /
`
` carriage, pinning that the gate honours it. The row must FAIL (not merely
run) when the behaviour it pins is changed -- give it a positive control.

CARE. This is a row that pins CURRENT behaviour, not a request to change it. If
the decision is instead to stop honouring markers inside a hidden 
, that is a
different and larger change and wants its own bead: the same strip governs the
`x 
` shape that has been deliberately disclosed since round 5.

title: codegen: the §3 shadow doc describes one gate; the parameter side has two
notes:
Residue R-B from the Linus review of PR #937 (merged as 3d0bcdc9, GH #741).

docs/specs/codegen-sentinel-taxonomy.md's §3 row at :222 justifies why the
tagged //gqlc:unreachable sites stay unreached with "the shadow rests on the two
arm lists being equal". That is an accurate description of the COLUMN side.

For the PARAMETER side it is incomplete. The reviewer's MU-L17 deleted Phase A's
parameter gate `if !ok { return }` (leaving the assertion as `prop, _ := ...`)
and measured: the mutation was KILLED by the conformance suite, but
TestSentinelTaxonomy/TestUnreachedBranchesAreUnreached PASSED. prepare.go:821
stayed unreached because the width check `tm.Property(prop.Type)` is a SECOND
shadow that catches the zero-value `prop` first. Only when MU-L18 bypassed BOTH
parameter gates did the fence go RED naming `param-type-invariant`.

So: the parameter shadow is two gates deep (type assertion + width check), and
the doc names one. Nothing in the doc is FALSE — the reviewer graded it "a doc
nuance, not a false claim", which is why it was residue and not a blocker.

Scope: amend the §3 justification so the parameter row states both gates, or
scope :222's sentence to the column side. Prefer wording that quantifies
nothing if a count would rot.

Do not re-derive from this note alone — verify at the then-current head that
both gates still exist and that MU-L17 still reproduces (single-gate deletion
must leave TestUnreachedBranchesAreUnreached green). If a later change collapsed
the two gates into one, the doc became correct and this bead closes as obsolete.

title: docs/adr/0025: the account of what the two Scalar pins redden under-counts, and one pin is unobservable in a whole-package run
description:
Non-blocking residue from PR #956 (bead gqlc-0otp), found by the round-1 Linus review. All four items are the same class: the merged text's account of its own pins is imprecise. None is a false universal; each under-claims rather than over-claims, which is the safe direction, so this was correctly graded non-blocking.

1. 'reddens both, at the subtest for the text that lost it' under-counts. Deleting the 'any' arm reddens Property/any, Property/[]any AND Scalar/any — three subtests, not one. The same under-report appears in the PR body's table.

2. Under the delete-'map[string]any' mutation, a whole-package run never reaches the closure pin at all: decodeFunc panics and the test binary dies. 'Reddens both' is only observable when the two are run separately. Worth stating, because a future reader reproducing the claim the obvious way will not see what the sentence promises.

3. 'only mention of agtypeMap outside its own declaration' — each golden also carries its doc comment.

4. The PR body says agtypeString 'is reached only through carrier == "string"'. True of decodeFunc's routing, which is the scope the sentence is about, but emitted helper bodies call agtypeString directly at render_models.go:519, :547 and :621. The PR page is a durable carrier, so the imprecision persists; not worth a CI-cancelling body edit on a merged PR, but worth recording here.

Also noted and NOT filed as a defect: types.go:204 still carries the unqualified 'unservedColumn refuses... so no emitted code reaches them'. Pre-existing and not false — the reviewer verified tm.Scalar has exactly two non-test callers (prepare.go:811, :1100), every route to them is refused by a named arm of unservedColumn, and the ScalarNull list path returns 'any' without calling tm.Scalar at all.

Acceptance: correct items 1-3 in the tree. Item 4 can only be fixed on the PR page or left recorded here.

title: query: the *ast.FuncType skip guard in sealedsum_test.go is not load-bearing
description:
Residue from PR #940 (bead gqlc-1vkb), filed by the round-3 Linus review.

internal/query/sealedsum_test.go's AST walk carries a skip arm for *ast.FuncType. Deleting that arm leaves the whole suite green: no fixture in internal/query declares a func-typed field or a func literal whose parameter list would reach the arm, so the guard classifies nothing on this corpus.

Two readings, both worth resolving:
 (a) the arm is dead and should go, or
 (b) it guards a shape that WILL appear and needs a fixture that fails without it.

Decide which, and if (b), add the fixture so the arm is measured. Note the measurement trap recorded on gqlc-1vkb: parseQueryPackage does os.ReadDir(".") + parser.ParseFile on real disk paths, so 'go test -overlay' does NOT reach it and a mutation row against this file reads as a vacuous PASS. Mutate on disk in a throwaway worktree with a positive control.
close_reason: Duplicate of gqlc-5ckc, which is the same finding filed 4 minutes earlier (22:28:32Z vs 22:32:24Z) from PR #940's round-3 residue. I created this one after searching the corpus with 'bd list --json', which silently caps at 50 rows while 55 beads exist — the original was outside the window and read as absent. gqlc-5ckc now carries this bead's full description (the two readings, and the parseQueryPackage/-overlay measurement trap). Work the finding on gqlc-5ckc.

title: query: the *ast.FuncType skip guard in sealedsum_test.go is not load-bearing
description:
Residue from PR #940 (bead gqlc-1vkb), filed by the round-3 Linus review.

internal/query/sealedsum_test.go's AST walk carries a skip arm for *ast.FuncType. Deleting that arm leaves the whole suite green: no fixture in internal/query declares a func-typed field or a func literal whose parameter list would reach the arm, so the guard classifies nothing on this corpus.

Two readings, both worth resolving:
 (a) the arm is dead and should go, or
 (b) it guards a shape that WILL appear and needs a fixture that fails without it.

Decide which, and if (b), add the fixture so the arm is measured. Note the measurement trap recorded on gqlc-1vkb: parseQueryPackage does os.ReadDir(".") + parser.ParseFile on real disk paths, so 'go test -overlay' does NOT reach it and a mutation row against this file reads as a vacuous PASS.
