   postcondition (the result is a set) is unaffected — the enumeration dedupes
   on the whole EdgeKey, not on the self-loop condition — but the stated
   rationale is not exhaustive, so a reader checking the code against the
   reason would conclude the dedupe is dead on the plural path. See gqlc-kph4,
   which is the coverage side of the same observation.

2. internal/resolver/resolve_test.go, TestEdgeUnionKeysAreASet. Its comment
   justifies the assertion by what codegen does with a duplicate (emits the
   switch case twice, package fails to compile). AGENTS.md discourages
   cross-layer appeals: the resolver's own reason to return a set is R3 §4.6
   dispatching on the candidate count, which is true whether or not codegen
   exists. Restate it from the resolver's contract and let the codegen
   consequence be at most a closing aside.

3. internal/codegen/prepare.go, admitEdgeUnionCandidates. The first gate (fewer
   than two candidates) cites "R3 spec §4.4" for the invariant it is asserting.
   The third gate — two candidates sharing an edge label — likewise depends on
   the resolver having returned a set rather than a bag, since a bag would
   reach it as a false duplicate-label refusal. It carries no citation. Give it
   the same one.
notes:
MANAGER SEQUENCING NOTE (2026-08-01). Deliberately NOT staffed in parallel with
gqlc-kph4, which is in flight on feat/resolver-plural-undirected-coverage.

This bead's item 1 is the edgeProbes doc comment and R3 spec §4.4 — the exact
text kph4 will be rewriting, because kph4's whole subject is the plural-endpoint
path those two currently describe incompletely. Two agents editing the same
paragraphs concurrently produces a conflict whose resolution is a judgement
call neither of them is placed to make.

Items 2 and 3 (TestEdgeUnionKeysAreASet's cross-layer justification, and the
missing R3 §4.4 citation on admitEdgeUnionCandidates' third gate) are genuinely
independent of kph4 and could have gone now. Kept together with item 1 anyway:
splitting one small comment-accuracy bead into two branches and two PRs costs
more review attention than it saves wall-clock, and item 1 is the one with real
content.

Staff immediately once kph4 lands, and re-read item 1 first — kph4 may have
already made it true, in which case this bead shrinks to items 2 and 3.

title: docs: sentinel taxonomy tables in docs/specs drift from codegen.allSentinels, with no fence
description:
docs/specs/codegen-stage-c3.md, c4.md, c5.md and c6.md carry taxonomy tables mapping
constructs to error sentinels, plus a mirror of codegen.allSentinels annotated with the
stage that introduced each. Nothing checks those tables against the Go slice, so they
drift.

Known drift as of gqlc-35yu.9:
  - the LIST / ANY property refusal added for apache-age-pgx-v5 (round 2) routes
    through ErrUnrepresentableWidth and is not in the construct tables
  - ErrUnrepresentableEdgeUnion (round 3, shared Phase A gate) is in neither the
    construct tables nor the allSentinels mirror

Raised by Carmack during gqlc-35yu.9 and deliberately not fixed there: the branch's own
precedent left the tables alone, and a drive-by two-row edit on an AGE-owned branch is
the wrong unit of work for drift that is already several entries deep.

Do this as one sweep: reconcile every table against allSentinels, and decide whether
the stage specs are historical records of what stage Cn delivered (in which case a
sentinel added by a later epic does not belong in them, and the mirror needs a new home)
or a live index (in which case add a fence that fails when the two disagree, the way
TestSentinelReachability already forces fixture coverage).
notes:
Fence landed on chore/sentinel-taxonomy-fence. Forks resolved:

(1) Historical record vs live index — HISTORICAL, decided on evidence rather than

title: codegen: narrow-width property conversions wrap silently instead of erroring
description:
A property whose schema width is narrower than the carrier the driver hands back is
converted at the field with a plain Go conversion, so a value that does not fit wraps
silently rather than failing. Found by Linus during review of gqlc-35yu.9.

Pre-existing and cross-backend: AGE narrows agtype's int64/float64 carriers to the
declared INT32/UINT64/FLOAT32 width, and the neo4j targets do the same from their own
carriers. Neither reports the loss.

This is a correctness question, not a codegen-mechanics one: a store can hold a value
outside the declared width (nothing in AGE or neo4j enforces a GQL property type at
write time unless the writer went through gqlc), so the read path is where it surfaces.

Decide the posture before implementing. Options: range-check at the field and fail the
decode; range-check and saturate; document that the schema's declared width is trusted.
Whichever is chosen must be the same on every backend, since the emitted surface is
backend-invariant, and it needs corpus coverage at the boundary values.

title: codegen/age: a multi-label node or edge type refuses the whole schema
description:
age.rejectMultiLabelSchema fails generation when the schema declares a node or
edge type keyed on more than one label. Verified against apache/age 1.7.0:
`CREATE (x:A:B {n: 1})` is a syntax error — AGE stamps exactly one label on a
vertex or an edge and its parser has no syntax for a second — so a graph
matching such a type cannot be written through this backend and no value
matching it can arrive to be decoded.

The gate is on the schema's whole entity table rather than on the columns a
batch projects, because Phase Z names an entity for every type in the schema
and the emitted Go surface is backend-invariant: a struct no query could fill
is still a struct the package would have to declare, with a label check
nothing could satisfy.

The cost is the same shape as gqlc-35yu.13's: a schema carrying one multi-label
type refuses AGE generation for the whole batch, including queries that never
touch it. test/data/codegen/valid/entity_multi_label_named is the fixture; it
is enrolled for neo4j-go-v5 only.
acceptance_criteria:
Either:
- a per-entity admission lands in the shared prepare phase, so a backend can
  refuse one entity without refusing the schema, and the AGE gate narrows to
  the queries that actually project the refused type; or
- the bead closes recording that whole-schema refusal is the right posture,
  with the reason stated where an author hitting it will find it.
notes:
SEQUENCING (2026-08-03): held behind gqlc-35yu.13 rather than parallelised, on a genuine collision — not on conflict risk as a blanket excuse.

Two reasons, and the second is the load-bearing one.

Territory: .15's answer lands in internal/codegen/age/prepare.go's gate and, if the per-entity route is taken, in the shared internal/codegen/prepare.go admission phase. .13 is in flight in exactly that gate — it is the LIST/ANY-width arm of the same unservedColumn machinery. Two agents editing one gate is a merge conflict for no gain.

Design: .15's two acceptance branches are not independent of .13's outcome. Both beads describe the SAME cost shape verbatim — 'a schema carrying one refused type refuses AGE generation for the whole batch, including queries that never touch it'. If .13 builds a per-entity admission mechanism, .15 consumes it and becomes a one-line enrolment. If .13 keeps whole-schema refusal, then .15 is no longer a per-bead choice at all: it is the same posture decision for both, and deciding it twice in two branches is how the two arms end up disagreeing.

So .15 starts after .13 merges, and its first act is to read what .13 actually did rather than re-deriving the posture blind. If .13 lands per-entity admission, .15 should be small. If it does not, .15 owns the posture decision for both arms and should say so in its own acceptance.

OUTCOME (2026-08-03, branch feat/age-multi-label-posture): second branch taken — whole-schema refusal recorded as the posture, in docs/adr/0027-age-refuses-a-multi-label-schema-whole.md. Not on principle; both alternatives were built and measured.

Shape (a), omit the struct on AGE: enrolled valid/entity_multi_label_named in both targets, dropped the entity on AGE, regenerated goldens. TestBackendInvariantSurface RED — "entity_multi_label_named declares a different Go surface under neo4j-go-v5 than under apache-age-pgx-v5", the AGE surface holding 3 declarations to neo4j's 4.

Shape (b/c), emit the struct and narrow the refusal to projecting queries: TestBackendInvariantSurface stays GREEN, because the comparison is over declarations and decodePersonEmployee is an unexported receiver-less func it skips. It emits, at exit 0, a decoder reading `if label != "Employee&Person"` — gqlc's own LabelSetKey join spelling, which no AGE vertex carries and no AGE statement can stamp. That is the disposition ADR 0025 rejected for temporal kinds.

The ADR 0025 channel shape does not transfer: the temporal enum splits, so its answer has to vary per member. Label-set arity does not — one label or unrepresentable, permanently, because the constraint is in AGE's grammar. A refusal channel whose answer can never vary reads as a capability.

The diagnostic is rewritten to carry the reasoning: names each refused type and its labels, gives `CREATE (x:A:B)` as the witness that does not parse, counts the queries the schema refusal takes with it, names both exits.

NO invalid/ FIXTURE, and none is possible today: manifest sentinels resolve through sentinelByName's three lanes (codegen., queryfile., cypher.) and conformance imports no single backend, so age.ErrUnsupportedSchema is unnameable there. Filed as gqlc-rv0h. The corpus is instead pinned from the AGE side — TestRejectsMultiLabelSchema asserts both that the manifest omits apache-age-pgx-v5 and that this backend refuses the schema.

INCIDENTAL FINDING: the GQL grammar admits no `&` in an edge's key label set — `-[:WORKED_FOR&FOR]->` fails with "no viable alternative at input ':WORKED_FOR&FOR'". So the EntityEdge arm of the multi-label check is unreachable from real input. Kept, because codegen.Entity can carry one and a grammar change would reach it silently.

title: codegen/age: fence that every AGE target emits an identical SessionInit
description:
All 12 apache-age-pgx-v5 golden targets carry their own copy of SessionInit.
Nothing asserts directly that the copies agree.

Today they agree by construction -- SessionInit is emitted from one template
with no per-target variation -- and the codegen fence proves each golden
matches what the emitter produces. So the property holds transitively. What
is unpinned is the template gaining a per-target conditional: the fence would
stay green while the copies diverged.

This matters because live_age_session_test.go binds ONE package's SessionInit
to pools that hand out handles generated into others. That binding is only
sound while the copies issue the same statements. The live arm checks the two
packages it mixes (rightly -- that is its own precondition), but the general
claim is a pure-text property of the emitted tree and does not belong behind a
testcontainer.

Assert it offline: read SessionInit's body out of every
test/data/codegen/valid/*/golden/apache-age-pgx-v5/graph.go and require all 12
byte-identical. No container, runs in the default build, fails the moment the
template grows a per-target branch.

Found by Linus as NB2 on gqlc-35yu.8, where the finding was ruled a naming
defect in that bead's own test and the exhaustive claim was split out to here.

Both backends emit a query's text as a Go RAW string literal:

    internal/codegen/age/render_queries.go:89
    internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go:179
    fmt.Fprintf(&b, "const %sQueryText = `%s`\n\n", p.Bare, p.SourceText)

Those two lines are byte-identical, so this is epic-wide, not an AGE gap.

## The invariant that breaks

Go discards carriage returns inside raw string literals -- it is in the spec,
not an implementation detail. So the VALUE of the emitted constant is
p.SourceText with every \r removed, while everything computed at generate time
was computed on p.SourceText WITH them. I checked internal/queryfile for
normalisation and found none, so a CRLF-authored .cypher file carries \r into
SourceText and the two byte strings genuinely differ.

For neo4j the consequence is cosmetic: \r\n and \n are the same query to the
server.

For AGE it is not, because dollarTag (age/render_queries.go:52) chooses the
dollar-quote delimiter by scanning the text, and gqlc-35yu.7 established that
the delimiter must be chosen against exactly the bytes the parser will scan --
that was B1, where a tag occurrence straddling the text/tag boundary produced
generated code that could not run. This is the same invariant failing for a
different reason: dollarTag scans the pre-emission bytes, and the parser sees
the post-emission ones. Removing \r can create a $gqlc-shaped occurrence that
dollarTag never saw.

## Reachability is narrow -- confirm before investing

Ordinary CRLF puts \r at line ends, which cannot forge $gqlc$: a trailing
`$gqlc\r\n` still has \n after the token, not $. Breaking it needs a bare \r
INSIDE the token, e.g. `$gql\rc` at the very end of the text, which no normal
authoring produces. That is why the .7 reviewer filed it non-blocking and why I
did not hold the merge for it.

Do NOT start by writing the fix. Start by deciding whether the reachable set is
empty. If it is, the right change may just be to normalise line endings at
queryfile read time so generate-time and emission-time bytes are the same by
construction, which kills the class rather than the instance -- and which is
probably worth doing anyway for golden stability across checkouts with
different autocrlf settings.

## Whichever way it goes, leave a fence

.7's TestDollarTagClosesOnlyAtTheEnds (age/render_queries_test.go) covers the
predicate but feeds it strings directly, so it cannot see this: the gap is
between what dollarTag is HANDED and what is EMITTED. A fence has to compare
the emitted constant's value against the bytes the tag was chosen on.

title: codegen tests: sweep the type-map tables against their domain, not a hand-counted length
description:
internal/codegen/age/types_test.go and internal/codegen/neo4j/types_test.go (:45, :60, :96, :118, :155) drive their type-map assertions from hand-written literal tables. Both carried require.Len(table, <literal count>) assertions, which assert that a literal sitting directly above has the length someone counted by hand: they fire only if an editor changes the table and forgets the number, and when they fire they name nothing about what was lost. The AGE ones were removed in gqlc-35yu.6; the neo4j ones remain.

Removing them leaves a real gap: deleting a row from a table now fails nothing, so a type silently stops being tested.

Fix: assert domain COVERAGE, not length — the union of the representable and unrepresentable tables must ElementsMatch the full domain, the way TestRunDriverAxis sweeps config.DriverValues(). That bites on both growth and shrink and is not tautological, because the expected side is derived rather than counted.

Blocker: the enumerators do not exist. There is no graph.PropertyTypeValues(), no resolver.TemporalValues(), no resolver.ScalarValues() — config.DriverValues() exists only because the YAML loader needed one. This bead adds them to internal/graph and internal/resolver and then sweeps both backends. Note graph.PropertyType is an OPEN string type, so its enumerator is a maintained list rather than a closed set, and the enumerator itself needs a fence.

Do both backends in one change: fixing one leaves the same hole plus an inconsistency.

Out of scope: typeMap.Temporal returning "any" for every kind with no rejection channel is gqlc-9n6t. Temporal has no switch at all, so it has neither growth nor shrink coverage today — but that fence and 9n6t's rejection channel are the same edit, so 9n6t owns it.

title: spec: the :many empty-result contract (empty slice, not nil) is emitted but unspecified
description:
Generated `:many` methods emit `out := make([]RowT, 0, len(records))`, so an empty result set returns a non-nil zero-length slice rather than nil. That is a deliberate emitter choice, but `docs/specs/codegen-stage-c1.md` never states it — the only nearby line is §'Columns is a non-empty slice', which is about something else.

gqlc-35yu.4 strengthened the live battery from `require.Empty` (which accepts nil) to `require.NotNil`, so the behaviour is now pinned by a test while remaining absent from the spec. Test and spec disagree about what is normative.

Worth settling before gqlc-35yu.8 brings the AGE arm into the same battery: if AGE's emitter reaches for `var out []RowT` the arm fails, and whether that failure is a bug in AGE or an over-tight test is currently unanswerable from the documents. The uniform-generated-interface promise argues for making it normative rather than relaxing the test.
acceptance_criteria: codegen-stage-c1.md states the :many empty-result contract explicitly and distinguishes it from :one's ErrNoRows; the live battery's assertion cites it.

title: codegen tests: narrow-width list-element fixture (int32/float32 in a list) — golden-uncovered conversion branch
description:
Found by adversarial review of gqlc-35yu.1 (2026-07-31), deliberately deferred out of that bead.

No fixture exercises a NARROW-WIDTH LIST ELEMENT (int32 or float32 inside a list), so the driver-carrier conversion branch at internal/codegen/neo4j/render_queries.go:654 is not covered by any golden.

title: TCK conformance ledger: execute the openCypher TCK against neo4j + AGE and track per-backend coverage
description:
Owner idea, 2026-07-31. Not yet scoped — this bead exists to hold the idea and the design tension, not to authorise a harness.

Proposal: run the whole vendored openCypher TCK generically against BOTH backends (neo4j and Apache AGE), analyse coverage, and incrementally drive it up.

CURRENT STATE
- The TCK is vendored at test/data/query/cypher/tck (tag 2024.3, via `just fetch-tck`).
- It is consumed PARSE-ONLY, by internal/query/cypher/acceptance_test.go, over a SUBSET of feature dirs (match, return, match-where, return-skip-limit, union, with, with-where, return-orderby, with-orderBy, with-skip-limit). Nothing executes TCK scenarios against a live backend.
- gqlc-35yu.4/.8 build a shared live scenario battery with per-backend adapters against live containers. That harness is the natural substrate for this work, which is why this bead depends on the epic.

THE DESIGN TENSION — RESOLVE BEFORE BUILDING
gqlc is a code generator, not a query engine. The TCK tests ENGINE semantics. So "TCK coverage" is ambiguous across three quite different levels, with very different cost and value:
  L1 PARSE      — does gqlc parse the scenario's query? (partially covered today)
  L2 GENERATE   — can gqlc emit code for it? Most TCK scenarios carry no schema and no typed params, so this needs a synthesised schema per scenario.
  L3 EXECUTE    — does the GENERATED code, run against backend X, produce the TCK's expected result table? This is the real prize and by far the most expensive: each scenario ships its own graph fixture as Cypher plus an expected-results table, so the harness must set up, generate, compile, run, and compare.

"100% coverage" is probably the WRONG TARGET. A large fraction of the TCK is out of scope for gqlc BY DESIGN — dynamic queries, and everything gqlc deliberately rejects (C6 scope limits, alias-required expressions, and similar). Chasing 100% would mean either weakening those rejections or permanently carrying a pile of unexplained failures.

The more valuable and actually achievable goal: a CLASSIFIED COVERAGE LEDGER in which every TCK scenario is either passing on a given backend or carries a recorded, reviewed reason for not being — out-of-scope-by-design, backend dialect gap, or genuine gqlc gap. Then the number to drive to zero is "genuine gqlc gaps", not "non-passing scenarios", and the ledger doubles as a per-backend dialect-gap map (which is adjacent to gqlc-35yu.12).

OPEN QUESTIONS
- Which level (L1/L2/L3) is the target? L3 per-backend is what "validate against both implementations" implies, but it is a large harness.
- Is the ledger a committed artefact (reviewable diff when coverage shifts) or a generated report?
- Where does it run? L3 against two live containers is nightly-job shaped, not PR-CI shaped.
acceptance_criteria: Framing agreed with the owner (which of the three coverage levels this targets, and how deliberately-out-of-scope scenarios are classified) before any harness work starts.
notes:
=== FRAMING RESOLVED 2026-08-01 — acceptance criterion met, harness work authorised ===
Decided under standing delegated authority (owner directive 2026-08-01: decide, record,
report). Reversible: nothing is built yet.

1. LEVEL — staged L1 -> L2 -> L3, one ledger spanning all three.
   The three levels are not alternatives; they are columns. A scenario that does not
   parse cannot generate, and one that does not generate cannot execute, so the ledger
   carries a per-level status and the levels gate each other naturally.
   L1 (parse) is backend-INDEPENDENT — it tests gqlc's Cypher front end, not a backend.
   It needs no container and no part of the 35yu epic, so it is separable and starts
   first. Split out as its own bead (see below); gqlc-modl retains L2/L3.
   L3 is the real prize and stays gated on 35yu.4/.8's live harness.

2. "100% COVERAGE" IS THE WRONG TARGET — this reverses the shape of the owner's original
   ask deliberately. A large fraction of the TCK exercises dynamic queries and constructs
   gqlc rejects BY DESIGN (C6 scope limits, alias-required expressions). Driving
   non-passing to zero would mean weakening those rejections. The number driven to zero
   is GENUINE GQLC GAPS.

3. CLASSIFICATION IS A CLOSED ENUM, and unclassified is a hard failure:
     pass | out-of-scope-by-design (must cite the ADR or spec clause) |
     dialect-gap (backend cannot; gqlc could) | gqlc-gap (genuine)
   A scenario present in the vendored TCK with no ledger row, or a row with no reason on
   a non-pass, fails the build. Per AGENTS.md "make illegal states unrepresentable": an
   unexplained failure must not be representable, because that is precisely how a ledger
   decays into a pile of ignored red.

4. THE LEDGER IS A COMMITTED ARTEFACT, not a generated report.
   Why: the value is the reviewable DIFF when coverage shifts. A generated report shows
   state; a committed ledger makes a silent regression — a scenario that stops parsing —
   a red line in a PR diff a human must approve. Direct precedent in this repo: the godog
   skiplist and the mustReject pins are committed for exactly this reason, and AGENTS.md
   already requires skiplist updates to travel in the same branch as the behaviour change
   that causes them. The ledger inherits that rule.

5. WHERE IT RUNS — L1 and L2 in PR CI (pure parse/generate, no containers, no meaningful
   wall-time). L3 in the nightly codegen_live job alongside 35yu.8. PR CI wall-time stays
   untouched, consistent with the epic's locked constraint.

6. SEQUENCING — L1 does not depend on the 35yu epic and may start whenever; L2/L3 stay
   blocked on 35yu.4/.8. gqlc-modl is NOT to be started while the 35yu epic is in flight.

=== CORRECTION 2026-08-01 — the CURRENT STATE above is STALE, and L1 IS ALREADY DONE ===
Read the code before acting on this bead; the description was written from a stale
snapshot. Measured on master at 536931a:

  - internal/query/cypher/acceptance_test.go enrols ALL 37 TCK feature leaf dirs, not the
    10-dir subset the description claims. 220 .feature files, 1615 scenarios.
  - The skiplist carries 140 entries, every one classified into one of EIGHT declared
    skipCategory constants (catRuntimeError, catResultAssertionOnly, catValueBelowBoundary,
    catGroupingKeySemantic, catBindingKindConflict, catWriteShapeConstraint,
    catClauseComposition, catSignatureArgCheck).
  - TestSkiplistCategoryPolicy already enforces both halves of the invariant I specified
    in the framing note: an entry with no valid category fails, AND a declared category
    with zero entries fails as a dead policy slot.
  - The corpus is never edited; skipped scenarios are reported and counted, never deleted.

CONSEQUENCE 1 — do NOT file or build an "L1 ledger" bead. L1 coverage is complete and the
classified-ledger mechanism already exists, in production, with its own policy test. My
framing note above independently specified this design; the repo got there first. That is
a strong signal the pattern is right.

CONSEQUENCE 2 — this bead's job is narrower and cheaper than the description implies:
EXTEND the existing skiplist/skipCategory mechanism to L2 (generate) and L3 (execute per
backend), rather than designing a new ledger format. Same committed-artefact rule, same
"uncategorised is a build failure" rule, same "never delete from the corpus" rule. Reuse
skipCategory's shape; the L3 taxonomy needs at least one new family the L1 set lacks —
backend dialect gap — which is where this bead meets gqlc-35yu.12.

CONSEQUENCE 3 — the honest headline number today is L1 = 1615 scenarios enrolled, 140
deliberately accepted with a recorded policy reason, 0 unexplained. That is the format the
L2/L3 columns should report in.

title: codegen/age: dialect-gap posture for neo4j-only Cypher in user query text
description: User query text executes verbatim (ADR 0005), so a query calling neo4j-only functions (datetime(), duration(), point(), etc.) or unsupported openCypher constructs generates fine for the AGE target and fails at RUNTIME with an AGE error. Evidence from the live battery and early AGE usage should inform which gaps are actually hit before building detection machinery. Post-epic backlog: intentionally unblocked, not on the epic critical path.
